definition_en: the details of where someone lives or where a place is, a formal speech, or the act of dealing with a problem or speaking to someone
core_image: 信封上写准门牌，让信息径直抵达目的地
scene: 社区礼堂里坐满了人，讲台前的麦克风已经调好。The mayor will address the crowd outside the town hall this evening.

senses.title: The details of where someone lives
senses.definition: the details of a place, such as a street and number, where a person lives or an organization can be found
senses.definitionCN: 一个人居住或一个机构所在的详细位置信息，如街道与门牌号
senses.example: Please write your address clearly at the top of the form.
senses.exampleCN: 请把你的地址清楚地写在表格顶端。
senses.why: Latin directus means set straight, and an address is the string of details that points other people straight to a place.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 directus 意为「使变直」，地址就是把人径直指向某个地点的那串信息，所以「指直」这个动作落成了地图上的坐标。

senses.title: A formal speech
senses.definition: a formal speech made to an audience on an important or official occasion
senses.definitionCN: 在重要或正式场合作的对听众的正式讲话
senses.example: The headmaster gave a short address to the graduating class.
senses.exampleCN: 校长向毕业班作了一段简短的致辞。
senses.why: Here the word names a whole piece of speech aimed at a hall, not a passing remark, so the directed words become a public event.
senses.whyCN: 这里的词指一整篇对准整个大厅的讲话，而不是随口一句话；被「指向」的话因此成了一场公开的活动。

senses.title: To name someone in speech
senses.definition: to speak to someone, or refer to someone, using a particular name, title or form of words
senses.definitionCN: 用特定的名字、头衔或说法来称呼某人或提及某人
senses.example: In that school, students address every teacher as sir or madam.
senses.exampleCN: 在那所学校，学生称呼每位老师为先生或女士。
senses.why: A title aimed straight at one person is how you address them; the target of the aiming is a human being, not a place.
senses.whyCN: 把一个头衔径直对准某个人，就是称呼他；这一次「对准」的目标是人，而不是地点。

senses.title: To deal with a problem
senses.definition: to give attention to a problem, need or issue and try to deal with it
senses.definitionCN: 关注某个问题、需求或议题并设法加以解决
senses.example: The report addresses the shortage of affordable housing in the city.
senses.exampleCN: 这份报告探讨了该市经济适用住房短缺的问题。
senses.why: Turn the same aiming gesture from a person to a difficulty: attention pointed straight at a problem is what dealing with it means.
senses.whyCN: 把同一个「对准」的动作从人转向难题：注意力径直对准问题，就是「处理」它的意思。

senses.title: To speak to a group
senses.definition: to speak directly to a person or group, especially in a formal situation
senses.definitionCN: 直接对某个人或一群人讲话，尤指在正式场合
senses.example: The mayor will address the crowd outside the town hall this evening.
senses.exampleCN: 市长今晚将在市政厅外向人群讲话。
senses.why: The prefix ad- means towards, so the oldest verb sense is simply sending words towards people who are present.
senses.whyCN: 前缀 ad- 表示「朝向」，所以动词最古老的用法就是把话朝着在场的人送过去。

senses.title: To write delivery details on mail
senses.definition: to write on a letter or parcel the details needed for it to be delivered
senses.definitionCN: 在信件或包裹上写明投递所需的信息
senses.example: She addressed the envelope and dropped it in the mailbox.
senses.exampleCN: 她在信封上写好地址，然后投进了邮筒。
senses.why: Writing the details on the surface of the mail is the core gesture made physical: the postman is pointed straight to the door.
senses.whyCN: 把投递信息写在邮件表面，是核心动作最具体的落点：邮差被径直指向那扇门。

intro.en: Address goes back to Latin ad- 'to' and directus 'set straight', and it reached English through Old French.
intro.cn: address 可追溯到拉丁语 ad-「朝向」与 directus「使变直」，并经古法语进入英语。

items.en: Dirigere meant 'to set straight, guide', and its past participle directus gave the idea of something made straight.
items.cn: dirigere 意为「使变直、引导」，其过去分词 directus 给出「被弄直的东西」这一概念。

items.en: Ad- 'to, towards' plus directus 'straight, set straight' produced the sense 'to direct towards', the base of the later French verb.
items.cn: ad-「朝向」加 directus「直的、被弄直的」，产生「把……指向」的意思，这是后来法语动词的基础。

items.en: Old French adresser meant 'to make straight, prepare, equip' and also 'to direct oneself or one's words to someone'.
items.cn: 古法语 adresser 意为「弄直、准备、装备」，也表示「使自己或自己的话朝向某人」。

items.en: Middle English adressen first meant 'to straighten, prepare, direct'; the noun sense 'a formal speech' is recorded later, and exact first dates are uncertain.
items.cn: 中古英语 adressen 最初意为「弄直、准备、指引」；名词「正式讲话」的义项出现较晚，确切首见年代不确定。

items.en: The word then split along two lines: the place a letter goes to, and the words directed at a person or an audience.
items.cn: 此后这个词沿两条线分开：一是信件所寄的地点，二是朝着某个人或听众说的话。

note.en: The look-alike group holds words built on the same straight-line root; the near-meaning group holds words for speeches, problems and homes with a different reach.
note.cn: 形近组收同一「指直」词根构成的词；近义组收表示演说、处理与住所的词，彼此适用范围不同。

entries.definition: The person to whom a letter or message is sent.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「收件人、收信人」，由本词加后缀 -ee 构成，指接收邮件的一方。

entries.definition: The person who writes or sends a message, or who speaks to someone.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「发件人、说话者」，由本词加后缀 -er 构成。

entries.definition: Able to be reached, located, or handled by a system.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「可寻址的、可处理的」，由本词加后缀 -able 构成。

entries.definition: Going straight to a point without turning aside; from the same Latin participle as address.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词或动词，义为「直接的、指引」，与 address 同出拉丁语 directus，共享「使变直」的词根。

entries.definition: A talk given to an audience; broader than address and needs no official occasion.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「演讲、讲话」，比 address 更宽，不要求正式场合。

entries.definition: A formal talk given to teach or inform, usually at a school or college.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「讲座、授课」，多在学校里以讲授知识为目的。

entries.definition: To make a determined effort to deal with a difficult problem.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「着手处理、应对」，强调下决心去解决难题，语气比 address 更主动。

entries.definition: The fact of living in a place, or the house where someone lives.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「居住、住所」，指住处本身，而 address 指写下来的位置信息。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the real Latin root directus and the phrases the word actually appears in.
normalIntro.cn: 下面的记忆钩子使用真实的拉丁词根 directus，以及这个词实际出现的搭配。

normal.en: Ad- means 'to' and directus means 'straight': an address sends you straight to a place.
normal.cn: ad- 是「朝向」，directus 是「直」：地址把你径直引到一个地方。

normal.en: The same Latin root gives direct, direction and director, all about pointing straight.
normal.cn: 同一拉丁词根还给出 direct、direction、director，都与「指向正前方」有关。

normal.en: To address a problem is to turn your words and attention straight at it.
normal.cn: address a problem 就是把话和注意力直接对准问题。

normal.en: An email address is the exact string that sends a message straight to one mailbox.
normal.cn: email address 就是那条把邮件径直送进某个邮箱的字符串。

normal.en: You address a person as a title: the name is aimed straight at them.
normal.cn: address someone as 就是用一个称呼直接对准某人。

abstract.en: Picture an envelope with a house number written so plainly that the postman needs no map.
abstract.cn: 想象一只信封，门牌写得清清楚楚，邮差不用看地图。

abstract.en: The same arrow that points to a house can point at a problem or at a person: it always means aiming straight at something.
abstract.cn: 指向房子的那支箭，也可以指向一个难题或一个人：它始终表示「径直对准」。

abstract.en: A speech is words aimed at a whole hall at once, which is why the noun and the verb share one shape.
abstract.cn: 演说是一次性对准整个大厅的话，所以名词和动词共用一个词形。

examples.cn: 请把你的地址清楚地写在表格顶端。

examples.cn: 这份报告探讨了该市经济适用住房短缺的问题。

root: 拉丁语 ad-「朝向」+ directus「使变直、被弄直的」，源自 dirigere「使变直、引导」；经古法语 adresser「弄直、指引」进入英语，核心动作是「把……径直指向」。

sensesIntro.en: Every sense of address comes from one gesture: aiming something straight at a target, whether a place on a map, a listener, a name, or a problem.
sensesIntro.cn: address 的每个义项都出自同一个动作：把某样东西径直对准目标——地图上的地点、听者、一个称呼，或一个难题。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: an envelope with a house number on it, and an arrow running straight from the envelope to the door.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只写着门牌的信封，一支箭从信封笔直射向那扇门。

branches.en: PLACE: the straight line ends at a door, whether the details are written on a letter or stored in a record.
branches.cn: 地点线：那条直线落在某扇门上，不论信息写在信上还是存进记录里。

branches.en: SPEECH: words aimed at a whole hall turn into a formal address.
branches.cn: 讲话线：对准整个大厅的话，成为一篇正式演说。

branches.en: NAME: a title aimed at one person is the way you address them.
branches.cn: 称呼线：对准某个人的头衔，就是称呼他的方式。

branches.en: PROBLEM: attention aimed at an issue is the modern sense of dealing with it.
branches.cn: 问题线：把注意力对准某个议题，就是现代用法的「处理」。

branches.en: AUDIENCE: the oldest verb sense, speaking straight to people who are present.
branches.cn: 听众线：最古老的动词义，直接对在场的人讲话。

intro.en: Address is a Latin prefix plus a participle, filtered through Old French; English then added ordinary endings.
intro.cn: address 由拉丁语前缀加一个分词构成，经古法语过滤后进入英语，英语再添上普通词尾。

latinIntro.en: Dirigere, directus and the prefix ad- are all recorded in Latin; only some intermediate Romance forms are reconstructed.
latinIntro.cn: dirigere、directus 与前缀 ad- 在拉丁语中均有记录，只有部分罗曼语中间形式属于重构。

definition_en: enough in amount for a purpose, good enough in quality or ability, or only just at the level required
core_image: 水正好倒到刻度线，不高也不低

senses.title: Enough in amount
senses.definition: existing in a quantity large enough for a particular need or purpose
senses.definitionCN: 数量大到足以满足某种需要或目的
senses.example: The shelter provides adequate food and clean water for every family.
senses.exampleCN: 收容所为每个家庭提供足够的食物和干净的水。
senses.why: Latin adaequatus means made equal: the amount is brought up to the level that the need sets, so it is enough but says nothing more.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 adaequatus 意为「被弄得相等」：数量被提到需求所划出的那条线上，不多不少，所以是「足够」，并不涉及好坏。

senses.title: Good enough in quality
senses.definition: of a standard that is good enough for a purpose, though not excellent
senses.definitionCN: 达到足以满足某一目的的标准，但算不上出色
senses.example: The room was small but adequate for two guests.
senses.exampleCN: 房间不大，但接待两位客人足够了。
senses.why: Equal to a line can be said of quality as well as quantity: if the standard is met, the thing is adequate, no matter how plain it is.
senses.whyCN: 「与一条线齐平」既可以衡量数量，也可以衡量质量：只要达到标准就算 adequate，东西再普通也没关系。

senses.title: Competent for a role
senses.definition: of a person, having the ability or training needed for a task or position
senses.definitionCN: 指人具备完成某项任务或担任某个职位所需的能力或训练
senses.example: After a month of training, she was adequate to the job.
senses.exampleCN: 经过一个月培训，她已能胜任这份工作。
senses.why: Put the same equality on a person: ability and the demands of the post meet at the line, and that meeting is what competence means here.
senses.whyCN: 把「相等」用到人身上，就是能力与岗位要求在那条线上相交；两者齐平，就是这里说的「胜任」。

senses.title: Barely sufficient
senses.definition: only just at the level required, with no margin of comfort or excellence
senses.definitionCN: 刚好达到要求，没有余量，也谈不上好
senses.example: His performance was adequate, but nobody praised it.
senses.exampleCN: 他的表现尚可，却没人称赞。
senses.why: This sense keeps the tightest edge of 'equal': the thing only touches the line and goes not one step beyond, which gives the word its faintly cool tone.
senses.whyCN: 这个义项保留了「相等」最紧的一面：只碰到那条线，一步也不多，因此这个词常带一点冷淡的「勉强及格」语气。

intro.en: Adequate is a Latin participle built on aequus 'level, equal'; its history is the idea of bringing something up to a line.
intro.cn: adequate 是建立在 aequus「平的、相等的」之上的拉丁语分词，它的历史就是「把某物提到某条线上」这一想法。

items.en: Aequus meant 'level, even, equal', and it also lies behind equal, equity and equator.
items.cn: aequus 意为「平的、均匀的、相等的」，equal、equity 与 equator 也出自它。

items.en: Aequare 'to make level or equal' is the verb formed from aequus.
items.cn: aequare 意为「使平整、使相等」，是由 aequus 构成的动词。

items.en: Ad- 'to' plus aequare formed adaequare, 'to make equal to, bring up to a level'.
items.cn: ad-「朝向」加 aequare 构成 adaequare，意为「使与……相等、提到同一水平」。

items.en: The past participle adaequatus meant 'made equal, equal to', and English took the adjective from it.
items.cn: 过去分词 adaequatus 意为「被弄得相等的、与……相等的」，英语由此借入形容词。

items.en: The word appears in English in the sixteenth century, first in the sense of equal to a requirement; the exact first date is uncertain.
items.cn: 这个词在十六世纪进入英语，最早表示「与要求相等」，确切的开始年份不确定。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers forms of the word and one Latin cousin; the near-meaning group gathers words for enough, for acceptable, and for ability.
note.cn: 形近组收本词的各个形式与一个拉丁同族词；近义组收表示「足够」「合格」与「有能力」的词。

entries.definition: The state of being enough or good enough for a purpose.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「足够、适当、胜任」，由本词加后缀 -acy 构成。

entries.definition: Not enough, or not good enough for what is needed.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「不足的、不适当的」，由否定前缀 in- 加本词构成。

entries.definition: A lack of something needed, or a failure to be good enough.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「不足、欠缺」，由 inadequate 加后缀 -acy 构成。

entries.definition: To treat two things as equal; built on the same Latin root aequus.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「把……等同看待」，与本词同出拉丁语 aequus「相等的」，是同根词而非派生词。

entries.definition: Enough for a stated purpose, in a more formal and precise tone than adequate.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「足够的」，语气比 adequate 更正式，也更强调正好满足某个目的。

entries.definition: The everyday word for the needed amount; it carries no judgement of quality.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词或副词，义为「足够的」，是最日常的说法，完全不涉及质量好坏。

entries.definition: Good enough to be accepted, with the emphasis on meeting someone's approval.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「令人满意的、合格的」，重点在于达到他人的认可。

entries.definition: Having enough skill for a task; used of people rather than of amounts.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「有能力的、称职的」，只用于人或其表现，不用于数量。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the real Latin root aequus 'level, equal' and the two fixed patterns adequate for and adequate to.
normalIntro.cn: 下面的记忆钩子使用真实的拉丁词根 aequus「平的、相等的」，以及 adequate for 与 adequate to 两个固定结构。

normal.en: Adequate is ad- 'to' plus aequus 'equal': something is adequate when it is brought up to the level needed.
normal.cn: adequate 是 ad-「朝向」加 aequus「相等」：把某物提到所需的高度，它就是 adequate。

normal.en: Aequus also gives equal and equity; all of them keep the image of a level line.
normal.cn: aequus 还给出 equal 与 equity，它们都保留了「同一条水平线」的画面。

normal.en: Adequate says nothing about excellence: it only says that the line has been reached.
normal.cn: adequate 完全不谈出色，它只说明那条线已经够到了。

normal.en: Adequate for a purpose and adequate to a task are the two patterns worth memorising.
normal.cn: adequate for 接目的，adequate to 接任务，这两个结构最值得记。

normal.en: The opposite is inadequate, made with the negative prefix in-.
normal.cn: 反义词是 inadequate，由否定前缀 in- 加本词构成。

abstract.en: Picture a glass of water filled exactly to a pencilled line, no drop above it.
abstract.cn: 想象一杯水正好倒到铅笔画的那条线上，一滴也不多。

abstract.en: Imagine three marks on a wall: below the line is inadequate, on the line is adequate, far above it is excellent.
abstract.cn: 想象墙上有三道刻度：线以下是不足，压线是够用，远远高出才是出色。

abstract.en: The same line measures rice, a room and a person's skill, which is why one adjective covers all three.
abstract.cn: 同一条线既量米、量房间，也量一个人的本事，所以一个形容词能同时管这三件事。

examples.en: The shelter provides adequate food and clean water for every family.
examples.cn: 收容所为每个家庭提供足够的食物和干净的水。

examples.en: The room was small but adequate for two guests.
examples.cn: 房间不大，但接待两位客人足够了。

examples.en: After a month of training, she was adequate to the job.
examples.cn: 经过一个月培训，她已能胜任这份工作。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「阿德夸特」——阿德把水倒到刻度线就停手：够用就好，不多不少。

root: 拉丁语 adaequatus「被弄得相等的」，源自 adaequare「使与……相等」，由 ad-「朝向」+ aequare「使平整、使相等」构成；aequus「平的、相等的」是它的词根。

sensesIntro.en: The four senses of adequate all measure something against a line: an amount, a standard of quality, a person's ability, or the bare minimum.
sensesIntro.cn: adequate 的四个义项都在拿某物去比对一条线：数量、质量标准、人的能力，或最低限度的及格线。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: water poured up to a marked line, no higher and no lower.
core.cn: 核心意象：水正好倒到刻度线，不高也不低。

branches.en: AMOUNT: the line marks how much is needed, and the supply reaches it exactly.
branches.cn: 数量线：刻度标出需要多少，供给正好到达那里。

branches.en: QUALITY: the same line applied to a standard means acceptable, not excellent.
branches.cn: 质量线：同一条线用来衡量标准，就是合格而不出色。

branches.en: PERSON: ability and the demands of a post meet at the line, and the person is competent.
branches.cn: 人线：能力与岗位要求在那条线上相交，人就能胜任。

branches.en: MINIMUM: the thing only touches the line, and that tightness gives the word its cool tone.
branches.cn: 最低线：只碰到那条线，这种紧贴感让这个词带上冷淡的语气。

branches.en: SHARED IMAGE: whether the object is rice or a room, the judgement is the same act of levelling.
branches.cn: 共同画面：不管对象是一袋米还是一间房，判断都是同一个「找齐」的动作。

intro.en: Adequate is a Latin participle; English builds its noun, adverb and negative with ordinary endings.
intro.cn: adequate 是一个拉丁语分词，英语用普通词尾构成它的名词、副词与否定形式。

latinIntro.en: Aequus, aequare and adaequatus are all recorded in Latin; only the deeper Indo-European root of aequus is reconstructed.
latinIntro.cn: aequus、aequare 与 adaequatus 在拉丁语中均有记录，只有 aequus 更早的印欧词根属于重构。

definition_zh: 调整；调节；适应；校准；整理；校正
definition_en: to change something slightly so that it fits better, to get used to a new situation, or to set a device to a standard
core_image: 把歪掉的画框扶正，让它与墙面刚好平行
scene: 新装的门关上时总蹭到地板，木匠蹲下来查看合页。He turned the screw to adjust the hinge.
sceneCN: 这里 adjust 是「校准、调校」（第 3 个义项：把部件或仪器调到正确位置）；句意为他转动螺丝来调节合页。

pos.zh: 及物动词：调整、调节；校准；整理（衣饰）；校正
不及物动词：适应（新环境）

derivatives.zh: 由本词加名词后缀 -ment 构成，义为「调整；调节；适应」
由本词加形容词后缀 -able 构成，义为「可调节的」
由本词加名词后缀 -er 构成，义为「调节器；理赔员」
由前缀 re- 加本词构成，义为「重新调整；再适应」

senses.title: To change something slightly
senses.definition: to change something a little, especially so that it works better or fits a situation
senses.definitionCN: 对某物作小幅改动，尤指使其运转更好或更适应情况
senses.example: You can adjust the height of the chair with this lever.
senses.exampleCN: 你可以用这个把手调整椅子的高度。
senses.why: Late Latin adiustare meant 'to bring to the right measure': the change is small because the thing is only slightly off and must be set right again.
senses.whyCN: 晚期拉丁语 adiustare 意为「使达到正确的尺度」：改动之所以小，是因为物件只偏了一点，把它拨回正确的位置即可。

senses.title: To get used to a new situation
senses.definition: to become familiar with a new place, condition or way of life and act comfortably in it
senses.definitionCN: 逐渐熟悉新的地点、状况或生活方式，并在其中自如行事
senses.example: It took her a month to adjust to the colder climate.
senses.exampleCN: 她花了一个月才适应更冷的气候。
senses.why: If the conditions have shifted, the person must be brought back into line with them; adjusting to something is the same straightening, applied to oneself.
senses.whyCN: 条件变了，人就得重新与它对齐；adjust to 说的是同一件「扶正」的事，只是对象换成了自己。

senses.title: To set an instrument to a standard
senses.definition: to set a device, instrument or machine so that it works correctly or shows a true value
senses.definitionCN: 把装置、仪器或机器调到正确运转或显示真实值的位置
senses.example: The technician adjusted the telescope before the observation began.
senses.exampleCN: 观测开始前，技师校准了望远镜。
senses.why: A device is right only when its reading matches the standard, so adjusting it is making it exactly right again, which is the original force of iustus 'correct'.
senses.whyCN: 仪器读数与标准吻合才算对，所以 adjust 就是让它重新精确地对上，这正是 iustus「正确」的本义。

senses.title: To tidy one's clothes or appearance
senses.definition: to move or arrange part of your clothing or appearance so that it sits neatly
senses.definitionCN: 把衣着或仪容的某部分弄整齐
senses.example: She adjusted her scarf before stepping into the interview room.
senses.exampleCN: 她进面试室前整了整围巾。
senses.why: A collar out of place is a small thing set right; the same verb covers straightening a tie and straightening a machine.
senses.whyCN: 领子歪了也是把一件小事扶正；同一个动词既管整理领带，也管调校机器。

senses.title: To correct a figure for a factor
senses.titleCN: 校正；扣除某因素的影响
senses.definition: to change a figure or result so that the effect of a particular factor is taken into account
senses.definitionCN: 改动数字或结果，以便把某一因素的影响计算在内
senses.example: The figures were adjusted for inflation before comparison.
senses.exampleCN: 这些数字在比较前已按通货膨胀作了校正。
senses.why: Here the correction happens on paper: the raw number is brought into line with a fair standard so that two sets of figures can be compared.
senses.whyCN: 这里的修正在纸面上完成：把原始数字拉到公平的标准线上，两组数字才能比较，所以也用同一个词。

intro.en: Adjust comes from Latin iustus 'right, just' through a verb meaning 'to bring to the right measure', and reached English from Old French.
intro.cn: adjust 出自拉丁语 iustus「正确的、公正的」，经由一个表示「使达到正确尺度」的动词，再从古法语进入英语。

items.en: Ius meant 'right, law', and the adjective iustus 'just, correct' grew from it.
items.cn: ius 意为「权利、法」，形容词 iustus「公正的、正确的」由它而来。

items.en: Iustus meant 'just, right, correct', and it still survives in the English words just and justice.
items.cn: iustus 意为「公正的、正确的」，英语的 just 与 justice 仍保留着它。

items.en: Ad- 'to' plus iustus formed adiustare, generally explained as 'to bring to the right measure, set right'.
items.cn: ad-「朝向」加 iustus 构成 adiustare，一般认为意为「使达到正确的尺度、把……弄正」。

items.en: Old French ajuster meant 'to arrange, fit, join', and it carried the verb into Middle English.
items.cn: 古法语 ajuster 意为「安排、使合适、接合」，它把这个动词带进中古英语。

items.en: The verb is recorded from the late fourteenth century, first for arranging and settling affairs and later for setting instruments; the exact first date is uncertain.
items.cn: 这个动词自十四世纪末有记录，先指安排与了结事务，后来才用于调校仪器；确切首见年代不确定。

note.en: The look-alike group holds the word's own family; the near-meaning group holds words for adapting, changing and setting instruments, which differ in scope.
note.cn: 形近组收本词自己的词族；近义组收表示适应、改动与调校的词，彼此范围不同。

entries.definition: A small change made so that something works or fits better.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「调整、调节」，由本词加后缀 -ment 构成。

entries.definition: Built so that its position or setting can be changed.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「可调节的」，由本词加后缀 -able 构成。

entries.definition: A person or device that adjusts, especially one who settles insurance claims.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「调节器、理赔员」，由本词加后缀 -er 构成。

entries.definition: To adjust again after a first change or a period of use.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「重新调整、再适应」，由前缀 re- 加本词构成。

entries.definition: To change something, or oneself, so as to suit new conditions; often a deeper change than adjust.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「使适应、改编」，改动往往比 adjust 更深，常指为适合新条件而改造。

entries.definition: To change something in form or detail, without the idea of fitting a standard.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「修改、改动」，只强调改变形式或细节，不含「对准标准」的意思。

entries.definition: To mark or correct an instrument against a known standard; narrower and more technical than adjust.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「校准、标定」，专指按已知标准对仪器进行标定，比 adjust 更专门。

entries.definition: To set a musical instrument or an engine to the right pitch or setting.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「调音、调校」，多用于乐器或发动机，调的是音高或运转状态。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the real Latin root iustus 'right' and the fixed patterns adjust to and adjust for.
normalIntro.cn: 下面的记忆钩子使用真实的拉丁词根 iustus「正确的」，以及 adjust to 与 adjust for 两个固定结构。

normal.en: Iustus is 'right': to adjust is to put something back to right.
normal.cn: iustus 是「正确的」：adjust 就是把某物重新弄正。

normal.en: The same root survives in just and justice, both about what is right.
normal.cn: 同一词根还留在 just 与 justice 里，两者讲的都是「正当」。

normal.en: Adjust to is for people and new conditions; adjust for is for figures and hidden factors.
normal.cn: adjust to 接人和新环境，adjust for 接数字和隐藏因素。

normal.en: Adjustable means the thing is built to be set right again and again.
normal.cn: adjustable 说明这件东西本来就被设计成可以反复调正的。

normal.en: An adjuster is the person who settles an insurance claim, literally setting the figure right.
normal.cn: adjuster 是处理保险理赔的人，字面上就是把那个数目「弄正」的人。

abstract.en: Picture a crooked frame pushed straight with one thumb until its edges run level with the wall.
abstract.cn: 想象用一根拇指把歪掉的画框推正，直到边缘与墙面平行。

abstract.en: The push is always small: adjust never means rebuild, only set right what has slipped.
abstract.cn: 那一下推动总是很轻：adjust 从不表示重造，只表示把滑开的部分拨回去。

abstract.en: A person can be the crooked frame: when the world shifts, the same small straightening happens inside.
abstract.cn: 人也可以是那只歪画框：世界一变，同样一次小幅的扶正就发生在自己身上。

examples.cn: 你可以用这个把手调整椅子的高度。

examples.en: It took her a month to adjust to the colder climate.
examples.cn: 她花了一个月才适应更冷的气候。

examples.en: The figures were adjusted for inflation before comparison.
examples.cn: 这些数字在比较前已按通货膨胀作了校正。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「阿贾斯特」——阿贾把歪画框一推，正好齐边：调整、校准。

root: 拉丁语 adiustare「使达到正确尺度」，由 ad-「朝向」+ iustus「正确的、公正的」构成，后者出自 ius「权利、法」；经古法语 ajuster 进入英语。

sensesIntro.en: The five senses of adjust all describe a small correction: an object, a person, an instrument, a piece of clothing, or a set of figures is brought back into line.
sensesIntro.cn: adjust 的五个义项都描述一次小幅校正：物件、人、仪器、衣饰或一组数字被重新拉回到该在的位置。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a crooked picture frame pushed straight until its edges line up with the wall.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只歪掉的画框被推正，边缘与墙面齐平。

branches.en: OBJECT: the chair or the frame is only a little off, so a small turn sets it right.
branches.cn: 物件线：椅子或画框只偏了一点，稍微一转就正了。

branches.en: PERSON: a newcomer is brought back into line with an unfamiliar place.
branches.cn: 人线：新来的人被重新调整到与陌生环境一致的线上。

branches.en: INSTRUMENT: a device is adjusted until its reading matches the standard.
branches.cn: 仪器线：装置被调到读数与标准吻合。

branches.en: APPEARANCE: a scarf or a tie is set neatly, the smallest version of the same act.
branches.cn: 仪容线：围巾或领带被弄整齐，是同一动作最小的版本。

branches.en: FIGURE: a number is corrected on paper so that a comparison becomes fair.
branches.cn: 数字线：数字在纸面上被校正，比较才变得公平。

definition_zh: 管理；行政；政府；给药；施行
definition_en: the work of managing an organization or public affairs, the government of a country, or the act of giving a drug or putting a law into effect
core_image: 桌子后面的人把任务、文件和物资一一分派到各个岗位
scene: 夜班病房里，护士推着小车按医嘱逐床分发药片。The nurse recorded the administration of the drug in the ward log.
sceneCN: 这里 administration 是「给药、用药」（第 4 个义项：把药物给予病人）；句意为护士把给药情况记进了病房记录。

pos.zh: 名词：管理、经营；行政；政府；给药；施行

derivatives.zh: 由本词去掉名词词尾而来，义为「管理；施行；给药」
由本词加形容词词尾 -ive 构成，义为「行政的；管理的」
由本词加表示人的后缀 -or 构成，义为「管理者；行政人员」
由本词加动词词尾 -ate 构成，义为「管理；经营」

senses.title: The work of managing an organization
senses.definition: the activity of organizing and running an institution, company or project
senses.definitionCN: 组织和运营机构、公司或项目的活动
senses.example: She studied business administration at a college in the north.
senses.exampleCN: 她在北方一所学院学习工商管理。
senses.why: Latin administrare meant 'to serve, carry out', and running an institution is service done on its behalf rather than for oneself.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 administrare 意为「服务、执行」：经营一个机构，就是替它做事、替它把事务办成，而不是替自己办事。

senses.title: Public administration; the work of government
senses.definition: the activity of managing public affairs and putting government policy into practice
senses.definitionCN: 管理公共事务、把政府政策付诸实施的活动
senses.example: Better public administration would shorten the queues at the office.
senses.exampleCN: 更好的公共行政能缩短办事窗口前的排队。
senses.why: Serving the state is the same service, only the master is now the public; administrare applied to the commonwealth becomes 'administration'.
senses.whyCN: 为国家做事还是同一件「服务」，只是主人换成了公众；administrare 一旦用到公共事务上，就成了「行政」。

senses.title: A government in office
senses.definition: the group of people who run a country at a particular time, especially in the United States
senses.definitionCN: 某一时期执掌国家的一批人，尤用于美国的说法
senses.example: The new administration promised to reform the tax system.
senses.exampleCN: 新一届政府承诺改革税制。
senses.why: The people who carry out the state's business are named after the activity itself, so the whole government takes the word for its work.
senses.whyCN: 负责替国家办事的那批人，直接用这项活动的名字来称呼；于是整个政府就用「工作」之名来指代。

senses.title: The giving of a drug
senses.definition: the act of giving a medicine or treatment to a patient, especially in a controlled way
senses.definitionCN: 把药物或治疗给予病人，尤指按规范进行
senses.example: The nurse recorded the administration of the drug in the ward log.
senses.exampleCN: 护士把给药情况记进了病房记录。
senses.why: To administer once meant 'to hand out, dispense'; giving a dose is that old sense of handing something over, surviving in medical usage.
senses.whyCN: administer 原本有「分发、施予」的意思；把一剂药发到病人手上，正是这个旧义在医学语境里的延续。

senses.title: The carrying out of a law, oath or rite
senses.titleCN: 施行；执行（法律、誓言、仪式）
senses.definition: the act of formally putting into effect something such as justice, an oath or a ceremony
senses.definitionCN: 正式使司法、誓言或仪式等生效的行为
senses.example: The administration of justice requires courts that are free from pressure.
senses.exampleCN: 司法要求法院不受压力干扰。
senses.why: Service hardens into execution: the official is the one who carries a rule or a rite all the way through to its end.
senses.whyCN: 「服务」进一步硬化成「执行」：官员的职责就是把一条规则或一项仪式从头办到底。

intro.en: Administration is Latin ad- plus ministrare 'to serve', and the whole family keeps the image of service carried out for someone else.
intro.cn: administration 是拉丁语 ad- 加 ministrare「服务」构成的，整个词族都保留着「替别人把事办成」的画面。

items.en: Minister meant 'servant, attendant', and it is generally connected with minus 'less'.
items.cn: minister 意为「仆人、随从」，一般认为与 minus「较少」有关。

items.en: Ministrare meant 'to serve, attend to, manage', and was formed from minister.
items.cn: ministrare 意为「服务、照料、料理」，由 minister 构成。

items.en: Ad- 'to' plus ministrare formed administrare, 'to serve, manage, carry out'.
items.cn: ad-「朝向」加 ministrare 构成 administrare，意为「服务、管理、执行」。

items.en: The noun administratio meant 'management, service, execution', and English took it through Old French.
items.cn: 名词 administratio 意为「管理、服务、执行」，英语经古法语把它借入。

items.en: Recorded in English in the fourteenth century for the managing of affairs; the medical and governmental senses developed later, and the exact dates are uncertain.
items.cn: 英语在十四世纪用它表示事务管理；医学义与政府义后来才发展出来，确切年代不确定。

note.en: The look-alike group is the word family built on the same serving root; the near-meaning group holds words for running affairs, for government, and for a measured amount of medicine.
note.cn: 形近组是建立在同一「服务」词根上的词族；近义组收表示管理事务、治理国家与药物用量的词。

entries.definition: To manage affairs, to put a law into effect, or to give a drug.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「管理、施行、给药」，与本词同出拉丁语 administrare。

entries.definition: Relating to the managing of an organization or to routine office work.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「行政的、事务性的」，由本词加形容词词尾构成。

entries.definition: A person who manages the day-to-day running of an institution.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「管理者、行政人员」，由本词加表示人的后缀构成。

entries.definition: A senior government official or a clergy member; literally a servant.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「部长、牧师」，字面意思是「仆人」，与本词共享同一个词根。

entries.definition: The process of running a business or team; closer to the everyday work than to public affairs.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「管理、经营」，偏指企业与团队的日常运作，不含政府义。

entries.definition: The group of people who govern a country, or the system by which it is governed.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「政府、政体」，是比 administration 更中性的通用说法。

entries.definition: The way in which an organization or country is controlled and directed.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「治理、治理方式」，强调运作机制本身，而不是执行事务的机构。

entries.definition: A measured quantity of a medicine taken at one time; the amount, not the act of giving it.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「一剂、剂量」，指一次服用的药量，而 administration 指给药这个动作。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the real Latin root minister 'servant' and the phrases the word actually appears in.
normalIntro.cn: 下面的记忆钩子使用真实的拉丁词根 minister「仆人」，以及这个词实际出现的搭配。

normal.en: Minister is a servant: administration is service carried out on behalf of an institution.
normal.cn: minister 是「仆人」：administration 就是替一个机构办事的服务。

normal.en: The same root gives minister, ministry, administer and administrator.
normal.cn: 同一词根给出 minister、ministry、administer 与 administrator。

normal.en: Public administration is service to the public, not private business.
normal.cn: public administration 是对公众的服务，而不是私人生意。

normal.en: In medicine, administration names the giving of the dose, not the dose itself.
normal.cn: 在医学里，administration 指把药给出去这个动作，而不是那一剂药本身。

normal.en: The administration of justice means carrying the law through, not writing it.
normal.cn: the administration of justice 指把法律执行到底，而不是制定法律。

abstract.en: Picture a servant walking a tray of papers down a corridor, handing each sheet to the right desk.
abstract.cn: 想象一个仆人端着一盘文件走过走廊，把每张纸递到该去的桌子。

abstract.en: The tray can hold tasks, money, laws or medicine: the word stays the same because the gesture is the same.
abstract.cn: 那只托盘里可以装任务、钱、法律或药：动作没变，词也就不变。

abstract.en: From behind the desk, the servant slowly becomes the one who decides, which is how the word also comes to mean a government.
abstract.cn: 从桌子后面开始，仆人慢慢变成拍板的人，这个词因此也能指一届政府。

examples.en: She studied business administration at a college in the north.
examples.cn: 她在北方一所学院学习工商管理。

examples.en: The new administration promised to reform the tax system.
examples.cn: 新一届政府承诺改革税制。

examples.en: The nurse recorded the administration of the drug in the ward log.
examples.cn: 护士把给药情况记进了病房记录。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「阿德米尼」——阿德把米一份份分给众人：管理、行政，也指给药。

root: 拉丁语 administratio，由 ad-「朝向」+ ministrare「服务」构成，ministrare 又出自 minister「仆人、随从」；核心意思是替他人把事务办成。

sensesIntro.en: All five senses of administration come from serving: serving an institution, serving the public, the people who serve as a government, and the handing over of a drug or a legal act.
sensesIntro.cn: administration 的五个义项都从「服务」长出来：替机构办事、替公众办事、替公众办事的那批人，以及把药物或法律行为交出去。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a person behind a table handing out tasks, papers and supplies to each post.
core.cn: 核心意象：桌子后面的人把任务、文件和物资一一分派到各个岗位。

branches.en: INSTITUTION: serving an organization gradually turns into running it.
branches.cn: 机构线：替一个机构办事，渐渐就变成经营它。

branches.en: PUBLIC AFFAIRS: the same service aimed at the state becomes administration.
branches.cn: 公共线：同样的服务对准国家，就成了行政。

branches.en: GOVERNMENT: the people who carry out public business are named after the work itself.
branches.cn: 政府线：替公众办事的那批人，直接用这件工作的名字来称呼。

branches.en: MEDICINE: handing out a dose is the oldest dispensing strand of the word.
branches.cn: 医学线：把一剂药发出去，是这个词最古老的「分发」支脉。

branches.en: LAW AND RITE: carrying a rule or a ceremony through to the end.
branches.cn: 法律与仪式线：把一条规则或一项仪式从头办到底。

intro.en: Administration is a Latin verb plus a noun ending, carried into English through Old French; its parts still build the rest of the family.
intro.cn: administration 是拉丁语动词加名词词尾，经古法语进入英语；这些组成部分至今仍在构成同族的其他词。

latinIntro.en: Minister, ministrare, administrare and administratio are all recorded in Latin, so only the still older Indo-European layer would be reconstructed.
latinIntro.cn: minister、ministrare、administrare 与 administratio 在拉丁语中均有记录，只有更早的印欧层才属于重构。

items.exampleCN: 它把「服务」变成「朝着某人去服务」。

items.example: It supplies the action behind the noun.

items.example: It adds the prefix to the verb of serving.
items.exampleCN: 它把前缀加到表示「服务」的动词上。

items.example: English took this noun through Old French.
items.exampleCN: 英语经古法语借入了这个名词。

items.example: It makes a noun of the act of managing.
items.exampleCN: 它把「管理」这一动作变成名词。

derivatives.zh: 由本词的拉丁动词形式而来，义为「管理；施行；给药」
由本词加后缀 -or 构成，义为「管理者；行政人员」

definition_zh: 行政的；管理的；后勤的
definition_en: relating to the management of an organization or government, or to the routine paperwork and support work of an office
core_image: 一叠表格与一串签字，把一项申请沿着流程往前推
scene: 新老师报到那天，领钥匙、办门禁、填工资单，跑了整整一层楼。Most of her first morning was spent on administrative tasks.
sceneCN: 这里 administrative 指日常事务性的行政工作（第 2 个义项：办公室里的文书与后勤事务）；句意为她第一个上午大部分时间都在处理行政事务。

pos.zh: 形容词：行政的；管理的；后勤的；由行政当局作出的

derivatives.zh: 由本词去掉形容词词尾而来，义为「管理；行政；政府」
由本词的词干加表示人的后缀 -or 构成，义为「管理者；行政人员」
由本词加副词后缀 -ly 构成，义为「在行政上」
由同一拉丁词根构成，义为「管理；施行；给药」

senses.title: Relating to managing an organization
senses.definition: connected with the work of managing an institution, company or government
senses.definitionCN: 与机构、公司或政府的管理工作有关的
senses.example: The reform was mainly administrative and changed no policy.
senses.exampleCN: 这次改革主要是行政层面的，并未改变政策。
senses.why: The adjective adds -ive 'tending to, relating to' to the stem of administratio, so it names whatever belongs to the carrying out of management.
senses.whyCN: 这个形容词在 administratio 的词干后加上 -ive「与……有关的」，因此凡是属于「执行管理」这件事的，都用它来指称。

senses.title: Routine office and support work
senses.definition: of the everyday paperwork, scheduling and support work that keeps an office running
senses.definitionCN: 指维持办公室运转的日常文书、排程与支持性工作
senses.example: Most of her first morning was spent on administrative tasks.
senses.exampleCN: 她第一个上午大部分时间都在处理行政事务。
senses.why: In an ordinary office the grand idea of carrying out policy shrinks to forms and schedules, so the word comes to mean back-office support.
senses.whyCN: 在日常办公室里，「执行政策」这件大事缩小成表格与日程，于是这个词就专指后台性的支持工作。

senses.title: Executive rather than judicial
senses.definition: of a decision, court or procedure, belonging to the executive branch rather than to the courts or the legislature
senses.definitionCN: 指决定、法庭或程序属于行政部门，而不是法院或立法机关
senses.example: The dispute went to an administrative tribunal instead of a criminal court.
senses.exampleCN: 这场纠纷交由行政裁判所处理，而不是刑事法院。
senses.why: Because administration also names the executive branch, the adjective marks whatever that branch does on its own authority.
senses.whyCN: administration 也指行政部门，所以这个形容词专门标记由行政部门依自身权限作出的事。

senses.title: Imposed by officials
senses.definition: of a penalty or measure, ordered by an administrative authority without a court trial
senses.definitionCN: 指处罚或措施由行政机关下令实施，不经过法院审理
senses.example: The company faced an administrative fine for late filing.
senses.exampleCN: 这家公司因逾期申报面临一笔行政罚款。
senses.why: If the executive can act on its own, its orders need no court, and the adjective flags exactly that kind of measure.
senses.whyCN: 行政部门若能自行行动，它的命令就无须法院；这个形容词标记的正是这类不经审理的措施。

intro.en: Administrative is the adjective of administration: Latin administrare 'to serve, carry out' plus the ending -ivus.
intro.cn: administrative 是 administration 的形容词形式：拉丁语 administrare「服务、执行」加上词尾 -ivus。

items.en: Minister 'servant' is the starting point of the family, and it is generally connected with minus 'less'.
items.cn: minister「仆人」是这个词族的起点，一般认为与 minus「较少」有关。

items.en: Ad- 'to' plus ministrare 'to serve' formed administrare, 'to serve, manage, carry out'.
items.cn: ad-「朝向」加 ministrare「服务」构成 administrare，意为「服务、管理、执行」。

items.en: Late Latin administrativus meant 'relating to management or service' and was built with the adjective ending -ivus.
items.cn: 晚期拉丁语 administrativus 意为「与管理或服务有关的」，由形容词词尾 -ivus 构成。

items.en: French administratif carried the adjective towards English, where it is recorded from the eighteenth century.
items.cn: 法语 administratif 把这个形容词带向英语，英语自十八世纪起有记录。

items.en: Its uses spread from state affairs to everyday office work, and then to measures taken by officials without a court.
items.cn: 它的用法从国家事务扩展到日常办公，再扩展到官员不经法院所作的措施。

note.en: The look-alike group is the word family built on administrare; the near-meaning group holds adjectives for management, for executive power, for bureaucracy and for office clerks.
note.cn: 形近组是建立在 administrare 之上的词族；近义组收表示管理、行政权、官僚作风与文书工作的形容词。

entries.definition: The noun for the work of managing, the government, or the giving of a drug.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「管理、行政、政府、给药」，是这个词的母词，同出拉丁语 administrare。

entries.definition: A person who manages the running of an institution or a computer system.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「管理者、行政人员」，由同一词干加后缀 -or 构成。

entries.definition: The verb meaning to manage affairs, carry out a law, or give a drug.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「管理、施行、给药」，与本词共享同一个拉丁词源。

entries.definition: In a way that relates to management or to official procedure.
entries.definitionCN: 副词，义为「在行政上」，由本词加后缀 -ly 构成。

entries.definition: Relating to the work of managing people or a business, rather than to paperwork.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「管理上的」，偏指管人与经营，而不是文书流程。

entries.definition: Relating to the part of government or a company that puts decisions into effect.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「行政的、执行的」，强调把决策付诸实施的那一部分权力。

entries.definition: Relating to rule-bound officials and slow procedures, usually with disapproval.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「官僚的、繁文缛节的」，通常带贬义，指受规则束缚的办事作风。

entries.definition: Relating to office clerks and their routine writing and filing work.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「文书的、职员的」，专指办事员写写记记的日常事务。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the real Latin verb administrare and the phrases the adjective actually appears in.
normalIntro.cn: 下面的记忆钩子使用真实的拉丁动词 administrare，以及这个形容词实际出现的搭配。

normal.en: The ending -ive marks an adjective, so administrative describes anything that belongs to administration.
normal.cn: 词尾 -ive 标明形容词，所以 administrative 描述一切属于 administration 的东西。

normal.en: The family runs minister, ministry, administer, administration and administrator.
normal.cn: 这一族依次有 minister、ministry、administer、administration 与 administrator。

normal.en: Administrative staff keep the forms moving; they do not set the policy.
normal.cn: 行政人员负责让表格流转起来，并不制定政策。

normal.en: Administrative law is the law about what officials may do.
normal.cn: 行政法是规定官员可以做什么的法律。

normal.en: An administrative fine is ordered by an office, not by a judge.
normal.cn: 行政罚款是由行政机关下令的，不是法官判的。

abstract.en: Picture a stack of forms clipped together, moving from desk to desk until every box is signed.
abstract.cn: 想象一叠夹在一起的表格，从一张桌子传到另一张桌子，直到每个格子都签了字。

abstract.en: The stack never decides anything itself; it only makes a decision travel, which is the essence of the office sense.
abstract.cn: 这叠表格本身从不作决定，它只是让一个决定走完流程，这正是「办公室义」的本质。

abstract.en: When the same stamp is pressed by an official instead of a judge, the word turns into its legal sense.
abstract.cn: 当同一枚印章由官员而不是法官盖下，这个词就转向了法律义。

examples.en: The reform was mainly administrative and changed no policy.
examples.cn: 这次改革主要是行政层面的，并未改变政策。

examples.en: Most of her first morning was spent on administrative tasks.
examples.cn: 她第一个上午大部分时间都在处理行政事务。

examples.en: The company faced an administrative fine for late filing.
examples.cn: 这家公司因逾期申报面临一笔行政罚款。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「阿德米尼斯」——阿德把一叠表格按顺序排好再传下去：行政的、事务性的。

root: 拉丁语 administrativus「与管理有关的」，由 administrare「服务、执行」加形容词词尾 -ivus 构成；administrare 出自 ad-「朝向」+ ministrare「服务」，再上溯到 minister「仆人」。

sensesIntro.en: The four senses of administrative all describe work done behind the scenes so that an organization, a government or its orders can function.
sensesIntro.cn: administrative 的四个义项都在描述幕后把事办好的工作，好让机构、政府或它的命令得以运转。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a stack of forms and a row of signatures that move a request along its route.
core.cn: 核心意象：一叠表格与一串签字，把一项申请沿着流程往前推。

branches.en: MANAGEMENT: whatever belongs to the running of an institution is administrative.
branches.cn: 管理线：凡属于机构运转的事务，都是 administrative。

branches.en: ROUTINE: in an office the same idea narrows to forms, files and schedules.
branches.cn: 日常线：在办公室里，同一概念收窄为表格、档案与日程。

branches.en: EXECUTIVE: the branch that carries out policy has its own tribunals and procedures.
branches.cn: 行政权线：负责执行政策的那一支，有自己的裁判所与程序。

branches.en: ORDER: an official can impose a measure without a judge.
branches.cn: 命令线：官员可以不经法官直接施加某项措施。

branches.en: SUPPORT: both office senses share the image of work done behind the scenes so that others can act.
branches.cn: 支持线：两个办公义项共享同一画面——在幕后把事办好，让别人得以行动。

intro.en: Administrative is the Latin stem administrat- plus -ive; the same parts also build the noun and the person who does the job.
intro.cn: administrative 是拉丁词干 administrat- 加 -ive 构成；同一批组成部分也用来构成名词与做事的人。

latinIntro.en: Minister, ministrare, administrare and administrativus are recorded in Latin; the deeper Indo-European root of minister is reconstructed.
latinIntro.cn: minister、ministrare、administrare 与 administrativus 在拉丁语中均有记录，minister 更早的印欧词根属于重构。

definition_zh: 钦佩；敬慕；欣赏；观赏；赞赏；惊叹
definition_en: to regard someone with respect and approval, or to look at something with pleasure and wonder
core_image: 站在画前退开半步，仰起头，眼睛睁大
scene: 美术馆里，一位老人退后几步，久久看着墙上的油画。He stepped back to admire the brushwork from a distance.
sceneCN: 这里 admire 是用欣赏的眼光细看画作（第 2 个义项：带着愉悦与专注观看）；句意为老人退后几步，从远处欣赏这幅画的笔触。

pos.zh: 动词：钦佩；敬慕；欣赏；观赏；赞赏

derivatives.zh: 由本词加表示「人」的后缀 -er 构成，义为「仰慕者；崇拜者」
由拉丁语 admirabilis 而来，义为「值得钦佩的；令人赞叹的」
由本词加名词后缀 -ation 构成，义为「钦佩；赞叹」
由现在分词 admiring 加 -ly 构成，义为「钦佩地；赞赏地」

senses.title: To respect someone deeply
senses.definition: to have a very high opinion of someone because of their qualities, achievements, or character
senses.definitionCN: 因某人的品质、成就或品格而对其怀有很高的评价
senses.example: I admire her patience with the youngest students.
senses.exampleCN: 我钦佩她对最小那几个学生的耐心。
senses.why: Admirari began as 'to wonder at', and wonder aimed at a person settles into respect: what makes you marvel is also what you rank above yourself.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 admirari 原本是「对……感到惊奇」；当这种惊奇对准一个人并稳定下来，就变成敬意——让你惊叹的东西，也正是你放到自己之上的东西。

senses.title: To look at something with pleasure
senses.definition: to look at something beautiful or impressive with enjoyment and close attention
senses.definitionCN: 带着愉悦与专注观看美好或令人赞叹的事物
senses.example: We stopped on the bridge to admire the sunset over the river.
senses.exampleCN: 我们在桥上停下来，欣赏河面上的落日。
senses.why: The ad- of admirari means 'towards', so the gaze stays directed outward; the verb that wonders at a person can rest just as well on a view or a painting.
senses.whyCN: admirari 里的 ad- 是「朝向」，目光始终朝外；同一个表示惊叹的动词，自然也能落在风景或油画上，变成纯粹的观赏。

senses.title: To praise someone openly
senses.definition: to say that you approve of someone or something, especially in front of others
senses.definitionCN: 公开表示赞许某人或某事物
senses.example: The coach admired the young player's decision to pass the ball.
senses.exampleCN: 教练称赞了这名年轻球员选择传球的决定。
senses.why: Esteem kept inside stays silent; spoken to others it becomes praise. English uses admire for the spoken form without dropping the idea of high regard.
senses.whyCN: 敬意留在心里是沉默的，一旦说给别人听就成了称赞；英语用 admire 表达说出口的敬意，而「评价很高」这层意思并没有丢。

senses.title: To marvel at something strange
senses.definition: to regard something with surprise and wonder, a literary use close to the oldest meaning of the word
senses.definitionCN: 带着惊讶与好奇看待某事物，属偏文学的用法，接近这个词最古老的意义
senses.example: The villagers admired the strange lights that moved above the marsh.
senses.exampleCN: 村民们惊叹于沼泽上方移动的奇怪光点。
senses.why: This sense leaves the Latin core untouched: mirari is simply 'to wonder', with no judgement of value added, so strange or even alarming things can be admired.
senses.whyCN: 这个义项保留了最原始的拉丁核心：mirari 只是「感到惊奇」，不附加价值判断，所以奇怪甚至让人不安的东西也可以被 admire。

senses.title: To be pleased with one's own appearance
senses.titleCN: 自我欣赏；对着镜子打量自己
senses.definition: to look at yourself or your own appearance with satisfaction, especially in a mirror or a reflective surface
senses.definitionCN: 满意地打量自己或自己的外貌，尤指对着镜子或反光的表面
senses.example: She admired herself in the shop window before going in.
senses.exampleCN: 进店之前，她对着橱窗打量了一下自己。
senses.why: The outward gaze can be folded back on the self; the object shifts from a view to your own reflection, while the pleasure of looking stays exactly the same.
senses.whyCN: 朝外的目光可以折回自身：对象从风景换成自己的倒影，而「看着愉快」这一点完全没有变。

intro.en: Admire comes from Latin admirari, built on mirari 'to wonder', and reached English through Old French.
intro.cn: admire 来自拉丁语 admirari，建立在 mirari「惊奇」之上，经由古法语进入英语。

items.en: Mirari meant 'to wonder at, marvel at'. It comes from mirus 'wonderful, strange', the same source as mirabilis 'marvellous'.
items.cn: mirari 意为「对……感到惊奇、惊叹」，来自 mirus「奇妙的、奇怪的」，也是 mirabilis「奇妙的」的来源。

items.en: Ad- 'to, towards' plus mirari produced admirari, 'to wonder at, look at with wonder'. The prefix gives the wonder a definite object.
items.cn: ad-「朝向」加 mirari 构成 admirari，意为「对……感到惊奇、以惊奇的目光看」；前缀让惊奇有了明确的对象。

items.en: The action noun admiratio meant 'wonder, admiration', and the adjective admirabilis meant 'worthy of wonder'; both are recorded in classical Latin.
items.cn: 动作名词 admiratio 意为「惊奇、赞叹」，形容词 admirabilis 意为「值得惊叹的」，二者在古典拉丁语中都有记录。

items.en: Old French admirer kept the sense 'to wonder at, regard with wonder', and this is the form English borrowed.
items.cn: 古法语 admirer 保留了「对……感到惊奇、以惊奇的目光看待」的意思，英语借入的正是这个形式。

items.en: English records the verb in the sixteenth century, first for wondering at something and soon for holding someone in high regard. The everyday sense of looking at something with pleasure is later, and its exact first date is uncertain.
items.cn: 英语在十六世纪记录了这个动词，先表示「对某物感到惊奇」，很快又表示「敬重某人」；日常用来表示「欣赏地看」的义项出现更晚，确切年代不确定。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the word's own family and one distant relative from the same Latin verb; the near-meaning group gathers attitudes of high regard that differ in warmth and formality.
note.cn: 形近组收这个词自己的词族，以及一个同出拉丁动词的远亲；近义组收各种表示高度评价的态度，温度与正式程度各不相同。

entries.definition: A person who admires someone or something, formed from the verb with the suffix -er.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「仰慕者、崇拜者」，由动词加后缀 -er 构成。

entries.definition: Worthy of admiration, going back to Latin admirabilis 'worthy of wonder'.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「值得钦佩的、令人赞叹的」，来自拉丁语 admirabilis「值得惊叹的」。

entries.definition: The feeling of admiring someone or something, from Latin admiratio.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「钦佩、赞叹」，来自拉丁语 admiratio。

entries.definition: A reflective surface; it goes back through Old French mirer 'to look at' to the same Latin mirari, though its meaning has travelled far.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「镜子」；经由古法语 mirer「观看」上溯到同一个拉丁语 mirari，与 admire 同源，但词义已经走得很远。

entries.definition: To hold someone in esteem, often because of their rights, role or qualities; it lacks the element of wonder that admire keeps.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「尊重、尊敬」，多因对方的权利、身份或品质而敬重，不含 admire 那种「惊奇」的意味。

entries.definition: To regard someone with high respect as a considered judgement; formal in tone.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「敬重、器重」，多指经过考量的评价，语气正式。

entries.definition: To respect someone deeply and with a trace of awe; stronger and more solemn than admire.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「崇敬」，敬意更深并带一点敬畏，比 admire 更庄重。

entries.definition: To recognise the value of something and enjoy it, common for art, music or help rather than for a person's character.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「欣赏、领会其价值」，多用于艺术、音乐或别人的帮助，而不是评价一个人的品格。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the real Latin verb mirari and the phrases this verb actually appears in.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些记忆钩子使用真实的拉丁动词 mirari，以及这个词实际出现的搭配。

normal.en: Mirari is 'to wonder', so admire started life as 'to wonder at'.
normal.cn: mirari 是「惊奇」，所以 admire 最初的意思就是「对……感到惊奇」。

normal.en: The same root gives mirror, since Old French mirer 'to look at' comes from this Latin verb.
normal.cn: 同一词根还给出 mirror：古法语 mirer「观看」正出自这个拉丁动词。

normal.en: Admiration is the feeling, an admirer is the person, and admirable is the quality worth the feeling.
normal.cn: admiration 是那份感受，admirer 是怀着感受的人，admirable 是值得这份感受的品质。

normal.en: Admire someone for their courage names the exact quality that made you wonder.
normal.cn: admire someone for their courage 把让你惊叹的那项品质直接点了出来。

normal.en: Widely admired means the wonder is shared by many people rather than felt by one.
normal.cn: widely admired 表示这份赞叹由许多人共享，而不是一个人独有。

abstract.en: Picture a visitor who steps back from a painting, tilts the head and stays there; the step back is the ad-, the look is the mirari.
abstract.cn: 想象一位参观者从画前退开半步、微微仰头停在那里：退开的动作是 ad-，那道目光是 mirari。

abstract.en: The same look can point at a person, a landscape, a strange light or a mirror; only the object changes.
abstract.cn: 同一道目光可以指向一个人、一片风景、一团奇异的光或一面镜子，变的只是对象。

abstract.en: Wonder comes first and respect second: the word still carries the widened eyes of that first onlooker.
abstract.cn: 先有惊奇，后有敬意：这个词至今仍带着最初那位观看者睁大的眼睛。

examples.en: I admire the way she keeps her calm during emergencies.
examples.cn: 我钦佩她在紧急情况下保持镇定的方式。

examples.en: Tourists gather on the hill every evening to admire the harbour lights.
examples.cn: 游客每天傍晚聚在山上，欣赏港口的灯火。

examples.en: The judge admired the young man for telling the truth.
examples.cn: 法官因这个年轻人说出真相而称赞他。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「阿德迈尔」——阿德退后两步，仰头看迈尔画在墙上的壁画，越看越服气：钦佩、欣赏。

root: 拉丁语 admirari「对……感到惊奇」由 ad-「朝向」+ mirari「惊奇」构成，mirari 又出自 mirus「奇妙的、奇怪的」。同族还有 admiratio「赞叹」与 admirabilis「值得惊叹的」。

sensesIntro.en: All five senses keep one Latin gesture, looking towards something with wonder: at a person's character, at a beautiful scene, at a good deed said aloud, at something strange, or at one's own reflection.
sensesIntro.cn: 五个义项都保留同一个拉丁动作，就是带着惊奇朝某物看去：看向一个人的品格、一片美景、一件被说出口的好事、某种奇异之物，或自己的倒影。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a visitor steps back from a painting and looks up with widened eyes.
core.cn: 核心意象：参观者从画前退开半步，仰起头，睁大眼睛。

branches.en: ESTEEM: wonder at a person settles into respect for their qualities.
branches.cn: 敬意线：对一个人的惊奇沉淀为对其品质的敬重。

branches.en: THE EYE: the same look rests on a scene, a painting or a building and becomes enjoyment.
branches.cn: 目光线：同一道目光落在风景、油画或建筑上，就成了观赏的愉悦。

branches.en: THE VOICE: esteem spoken aloud turns into praise.
branches.cn: 说出口线：心里的敬意说给别人听，就成了称赞。

branches.en: THE OLD CORE: wonder without any judgement of value survives in literary use.
branches.cn: 古老核心线：不带价值评价的惊奇在文学用法中留存下来。

branches.en: THE MIRROR: the gaze turns back and the object becomes oneself.
branches.cn: 镜面线：目光折回，对象变成了自己。

intro.en: Admire is a Latin verb borrowed through French, and English builds the rest of the family with ordinary suffixes.
intro.cn: admire 是经法语借入的拉丁动词，英语再用普通后缀搭出这一词族的其余成员。

latinIntro.en: Latin mirari, mirus, admirari and admiratio are all recorded; no reconstructed form is needed for this family.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 mirari、mirus、admirari 与 admiratio 都有文献记录，这个词族不需要借助重构形式。

items.example: It points the wonder at a particular object.
items.exampleCN: 它把惊奇指向某个具体对象。

items.example: This verb is the heart of the whole family.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词是整族词的核心。

items.example: It describes whatever causes the wonder.
items.exampleCN: 它描述引起惊奇的那个东西。

items.example: The prefix and the verb joined into one word.
items.exampleCN: 前缀与动词合成了一体。

items.example: It is the action noun of admirari.
items.exampleCN: 它是 admirari 的动作名词。

items.example: It forms admiration.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 admiration。

items.example: It forms admirable.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 admirable。

items.example: It forms admirer.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 admirer。

items.example: It forms admiringly.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 admiringly。

latinEntries.structure: Latin verb from ad- and mirari
latinEntries.meaning: to wonder at, look at with wonder
latinEntries.meaningCN: 对……感到惊奇；以惊奇的目光看

definition_zh: 承认；入场费；进入许可；录取；入院；供认
definition_en: the act of accepting that something is true, or the right, permission or money needed to enter a place or an institution
core_image: 门口的一道闸：一边放人进来，一边把不愿说的事放进来
scene: 剧院门口排起长队，售票窗上贴着手写的价目。Admission is twenty dollars for adults and half price for children.
sceneCN: 这里 admission 指进场要付的钱（第 2 个义项：入场费）；句意为成人入场二十美元，儿童半价。

pos.zh: 名词：承认；入场费；进入许可；录取；入院

derivatives.zh: 同一词族的动词，义为「承认；准许进入」，admission 正由它的拉丁名词形式而来
由动词加名词后缀 -ance 构成，义为「进入权；进入」，多用于正式告示
由本词加形容词后缀 -ible 构成，义为「可采纳的；可接受的」
由否定前缀 in- 加 admissible 构成，义为「不可采纳的；不予接受的」

senses.title: The act of accepting that something is true
senses.definition: the act of agreeing that something is true, especially something you would rather not accept
senses.definitionCN: 同意某事为真，尤指自己本不愿接受的事
senses.example: His admission that he had copied the essay shocked the class.
senses.exampleCN: 他承认那篇文章是抄来的，这让全班都吃了一惊。
senses.why: Admission is the noun of admittere, 'to let in': a fact you had been keeping outside the door is finally allowed through, and the word names that letting-in.
senses.whyCN: admission 是 admittere「放进来」的名词形式：一个被你挡在门外很久的事实终于被放进来，这个词命名的正是这次「放行」。

senses.title: The money paid to enter a place
senses.definition: the amount of money that you must pay to enter a museum, theatre, sports ground or similar place
senses.definitionCN: 进入博物馆、剧院、体育场等场所必须支付的费用
senses.example: Admission to the exhibition costs ten pounds.
senses.exampleCN: 这个展览的入场费是十英镑。
senses.why: Once the letting-in becomes a service, it acquires a price: the door that could open for nothing can also sell the right of passage, and the price takes the name of the act itself.
senses.whyCN: 当「放人进来」变成一项服务，它就有了价钱：这扇门本来可以无偿打开，也可以把通行权卖出去，而这个价钱直接沿用了「放行」这个动作的名字。

senses.title: Permission or the right to enter
senses.definition: permission or the right to enter a place, join a group, or be present at an event
senses.definitionCN: 进入某场所、加入某团体或出席某活动的许可与权利
senses.example: No admission without a ticket.
senses.exampleCN: 没有票不得入场。
senses.why: This is the literal core of the Latin word: ad- means to and mittere means send, so admission is the state of being sent in through a doorway.
senses.whyCN: 这是拉丁词的字面核心：ad- 表示「向」，mittere 表示「送」，admission 就是「被送进门内」的那种状态。

senses.title: Acceptance into a school or college
senses.definition: the act of accepting someone as a student or member of an institution, or the process of doing so
senses.definitionCN: 接纳某人为学生或机构成员的行为，或这项工作本身的流程
senses.example: The college changed its admission rules for overseas applicants.
senses.exampleCN: 学院修改了海外申请者的录取规则。
senses.why: A school is a door too: the noun for entering a building came to describe passing the academic gate, and in the plural it names the office that decides who gets through.
senses.whyCN: 学校也是一扇门：原本描述「进楼」的名词被用来描述通过学业这道门，而复数形式还指决定放谁进来的那个招生部门。

senses.title: Being taken into hospital
senses.definition: the act of taking a patient into hospital so that they can be cared for
senses.definitionCN: 把病人收进医院接受照护的行为
senses.example: Her admission to hospital followed a week of chest pain.
senses.exampleCN: 胸口疼了一个星期之后，她住进了医院。
senses.why: Medical language fixes the same image to one building: the hospital is the door, and the patient sent through it becomes an admission on the ward list.
senses.whyCN: 医学语境把同一个意象固定到一座建筑上：医院就是那扇门，被送进去的病人就成了病房名单上的一条「入院」记录。

senses.title: A statement used as evidence in court
senses.definition: a formal statement in which someone accepts that they did something wrong, which may be used as evidence against them
senses.definitionCN: 正式承认自己做过错事的陈述，可能被用作对自己不利的证据
senses.example: The detective read the suspect's admission aloud to the jury.
senses.exampleCN: 警探把嫌疑人的供认当庭念给了陪审团听。
senses.why: In court the thing let in is a statement: once the record opens to it, the admission belongs to the case, so the legal use leans on the same doorway image.
senses.whyCN: 在法庭上被放行的是陈述本身：记录一旦对它敞开，这份承认就成了案件的一部分，法律用法仍靠那扇门的意象支撑。

intro.en: Admission is the Latin noun of admittere, 'to send in', and it entered English through French with the doorway image intact.
intro.cn: admission 是 admittere「送进去」的拉丁名词，经法语进入英语时，「门」的意象依然完整。

items.en: Mittere meant 'to send, let go', and it is also the source of mission, permit and transmit.
items.cn: mittere 意为「送出、放开」，也是 mission、permit 与 transmit 的来源。

items.en: Ad- 'to' plus mittere formed admittere, 'to send to, let in, allow to enter'.
items.cn: ad-「向」加 mittere 构成 admittere，意为「送到、放进来、准许进入」。

items.en: The noun admissio is recorded for 'a letting in, an approach'. The sense of acknowledging a fact is not classical Latin but developed later in French and English.
items.cn: 名词 admissio 有「放行、进入」的记录；而「承认某事实」的义项并非古典拉丁语所有，是后来在法语和英语中发展出来的。

items.en: Old French admission carried the word into English with the sense of a letting in and of acceptance.
items.cn: 古法语 admission 把这个词带进英语，义为「放行」与「接纳」。

items.en: The noun is recorded in English from the fifteenth century, the acknowledgement sense appears in the sixteenth, and the fee sense is generally dated to the nineteenth. Exact dates are uncertain.
items.cn: 这个名词自十五世纪起见于英语，承认义在十六世纪出现，入场费义一般认为定于十九世纪；确切年代不确定。

note.en: The look-alike group is built on the Latin verb mittere 'to send'; the near-meaning group gathers other words for entering and for confessing, which split the two halves of admission between them.
note.cn: 形近组都建立在拉丁动词 mittere「送」之上；近义组收其他表示「进入」与「认罪」的词，它们分别承担了 admission 的两半意思。

entries.definition: The verb behind the noun, meaning to let in or to accept that something is true.
entries.definitionCN: 名词背后的动词，义为「准许进入」或「承认某事为真」。

entries.definition: The right to enter a place, formed with the suffix -ance and common on official notices.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「进入权、进入」，由后缀 -ance 构成，常见于正式告示。

entries.definition: Allowed to be used as evidence or accepted as valid, formed with -ible.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「可采纳的、可接受的」，由后缀 -ible 构成。

entries.definition: An official order to do something, or a payment for a sale; it shares mittere with admission but has a different prefix and a different sense.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「委托、佣金」；与 admission 同出 mittere，但前缀不同、意义也已分开。

entries.definition: The act of entering or the door through which you enter; physical and concrete, unlike the abstract permission in admission.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「进入、入口」，指具体动作或具体的门，不像 admission 那样偏重抽象的许可。

entries.definition: The act of going in, or an item entered in a list or competition; broader and less institutional.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「进入、条目、参赛作品」，范围更宽，机构色彩更淡。

entries.definition: A statement admitting guilt, especially in religion or law; heavier and more moral than admission.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「供认、忏悔」，多用于宗教或法律，语气比 admission 更重，道德意味更强。

entries.definition: The act of registering as a student or member; it names the sign-up rather than the decision to accept.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「注册、入学人数」，指完成注册这一动作，而不是学校决定录取。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the real Latin verb mittere and the phrases admission actually appears in.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些记忆钩子使用真实的拉丁动词 mittere，以及 admission 实际出现的搭配。

normal.en: Mittere is 'to send', so admission is being sent in through a door.
normal.cn: mittere 是「送」，所以 admission 就是被送进门里去。

normal.en: Mission, permit, transmit and admit all carry the same mittere.
normal.cn: mission、permit、transmit 与 admit 都带着同一个 mittere。

normal.en: An admission fee is the price of the door, not the price of what is inside.
normal.cn: admission fee 是那道门的价钱，不是门里那些东西的价钱。

normal.en: Hospital staff speak of an admission when a patient is taken in and written on the ward list.
normal.cn: 病人被收进医院、名字写进病房名单时，医护人员说的就是一次 admission。

normal.en: An admission that something is true is a fact finally allowed past the guard.
normal.cn: admission that something is true 就是一个终于被放过大门的真相。

abstract.en: Picture one gate doing two jobs: it lets people into a building and it lets an unwelcome fact into a conversation.
abstract.cn: 想象同一道门兼做两件事：既放人进楼，也把一个不受欢迎的事实放进谈话里。

abstract.en: The noun always looks at the moment of passing through, never at what happens afterwards.
abstract.cn: 这个名词看的始终是「穿过门」的那一刻，而不是之后发生了什么。

abstract.en: A fee, a letter of acceptance and a confession are all tickets through the same opening.
abstract.cn: 一笔费用、一封录取通知和一次供认，都是穿过同一个出口的票。

examples.en: The museum charges no admission on public holidays.
examples.cn: 这家博物馆在公共假日不收门票。

examples.en: His admission of guilt ended the two-year dispute.
examples.cn: 他承认了自己的过错，这场持续两年的争执就此结束。

examples.en: Letters of admission will be mailed in March.
examples.cn: 录取通知书将在三月寄出。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「额的米神」——门口收银员说：想进去，先交我的米（钱）才神气：入场费、准入。

sensesIntro.en: Every sense of admission is a single doorway seen from a different side: a fact let in, a price for passage, a right to enter, an academic gate, a hospital bed, or a statement admitted into the record.
sensesIntro.cn: admission 的每个义项都是同一道门的不同侧面：放一个事实进来、为通行定价、拥有进入的权利、跨过学业之门、被收进病床，或一份被记录接纳的陈述。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a gate that opens for people and for facts at the same time.
core.cn: 核心意象：一道同时为人与事实打开的门。

branches.en: THE RECORD: a fact or a confession is let in past the guard of silence.
branches.cn: 记录线：一个事实或一份供认被放过了沉默这道岗。

branches.en: THE PRICE: the same passage is sold at the ticket window.
branches.cn: 价钱线：同一次通行在售票窗口被标上了价。

branches.en: THE RIGHT: the door grants or withholds the mere permission to pass.
branches.cn: 权利线：这道门只决定给不给通过的许可。

branches.en: THE SCHOOL: the academic gate, and the office that decides who passes it.
branches.cn: 学校线：学业之门，以及决定谁可以通过的那个部门。

branches.en: THE WARD: one building takes the image over, and the patient becomes a line on a list.
branches.cn: 病房线：某座建筑接过了这个意象，病人成了名单上的一行。

intro.en: Admission is a Latin action noun; its endings and the verb behind it still build admittance, admissible and inadmissible.
intro.cn: admission 是拉丁语动作名词；它的词尾以及背后的动词，至今仍在构成 admittance、admissible 与 inadmissible。

latinIntro.en: Latin mittere, admittere and admissio are all recorded, and admissus is the recorded past participle.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 mittere、admittere 与 admissio 均有文献记录，admissus 是记录在案的过去分词。

被放进来的；获准进入的

definition_zh: 承认；认错；准许进入；接纳；容纳；容许；采纳
definition_en: to agree that something is true, or to allow a person or thing to enter
core_image: 守门人侧身让路，把门外的人与门外的事实一并放进来
scene: 病房外的长椅上，家属等着护士叫名字。She was admitted to hospital late that night with a high fever.
sceneCN: 这里 admitted 是被医院收下住院（第 4 个义项：被机构接纳，如入院、入学）；句意为她那天深夜因高烧住进了医院。

pos.zh: 动词：承认；准许进入；接纳；容纳
动词：承认（admit to）；容许（admit of）

derivatives.zh: 由拉丁名词 admissio 而来，义为「承认；进入许可；入场费」
由本词加名词后缀 -ance 构成，义为「进入权；进入」
由过去分词加 -ly 构成，义为「诚然；无可否认地」
由本词加形容词后缀 -ible 构成，义为「可采纳的；可接受的」

senses.title: To agree that something is true
senses.definition: to agree, often unwillingly, that something is true
senses.definitionCN: 往往不情愿地同意某事为真
senses.example: He finally admitted that the plan had failed.
senses.exampleCN: 他最终承认这个计划失败了。
senses.why: Admittere is 'to let in': a fact you have kept outside the door is allowed through, and the verb names that inward movement rather than the fact itself.
senses.whyCN: admittere 是「放进来」：一个被你挡在门外的事实获准通过，这个动词命名的是「往里放」的动作，而不是事实本身。

senses.title: To confess to a fault
senses.definition: to say that you have done something wrong or illegal
senses.definitionCN: 说出自己做过错事或违法的事
senses.example: She admitted taking the money from the drawer.
senses.exampleCN: 她承认拿了抽屉里的钱。
senses.why: The door is the same, but what passes through is your own fault: you stop guarding it and let it into the record, which is why admit to is the usual pattern.
senses.whyCN: 门还是那扇门，只是通过的是自己的过错：你不再把它守住，而是让它进入记录，所以这个义项常用 admit to 这个结构。

senses.title: To allow someone to enter a place
senses.definition: to allow a person or thing to enter a building, room or other place
senses.definitionCN: 允许人或物进入某座建筑、某个房间或其他场所
senses.example: The usher admitted us through a side door.
senses.exampleCN: 引座员让我们从侧门进去了。
senses.why: This is the plain physical sense of mittere with ad-: a person is sent in, and the verb records the doorkeeper's decision to let them pass.
senses.whyCN: 这是 mittere 加 ad- 最朴素的物理义：一个人被送进门内，动词记下的就是守门人放行的决定。

senses.title: To accept someone into an institution
senses.definition: to accept someone into a hospital, school, club or other institution, very often in the passive
senses.definitionCN: 接纳某人进入医院、学校、社团等机构，常用被动形式
senses.example: Only twelve students are admitted to the programme each year.
senses.exampleCN: 这个项目每年只录取十二名学生。
senses.why: An institution is a door with rules attached: to be admitted is to be let through those rules, whether the place waiting is a hospital bed or a seat in a class.
senses.whyCN: 机构是一扇挂着规矩的门：被接纳就是被放行通过这些规矩，门外等着的可能是一张病床，也可能是一个课桌位。

senses.title: To have room for a number of people
senses.definition: of a hall, room or vehicle, to have space for a certain number of people
senses.definitionCN: 指厅堂、房间或车辆能装下一定数量的人
senses.example: The hall admits up to five hundred people.
senses.exampleCN: 这个大厅最多可容纳五百人。
senses.why: The metaphor turns around here: the building becomes the doorkeeper, and the number it admits is simply the number its space can let through.
senses.whyCN: 比喻在这里转了个方向：建筑本身成了守门人，它能「放进来」的人数，就是它的空间能放过的人数。

senses.title: To allow something to be possible
senses.definition: to allow the possibility of something, used especially in the phrase admit of
senses.definitionCN: 容许某事存在可能性，尤用于 admit of 这一结构
senses.example: The evidence admits of only one explanation.
senses.exampleCN: 这些证据只容许一种解释。
senses.why: If a door can let something through, a situation can also let a reading through; the negative admits of no delay means the door is firmly shut.
senses.whyCN: 如果一扇门能放东西通过，一种情况也能放过某种解读；否定形式 admits of no delay 就是说这扇门关得死死的，一点余地都没有。

senses.title: To allow evidence in court
senses.definition: of a court or judge, to allow evidence or an argument to be considered officially
senses.definitionCN: 指法院或法官允许把某项证据、主张正式纳入审理
senses.example: The judge admitted the recording as evidence.
senses.exampleCN: 法官采纳了那段录音作为证据。
senses.why: Legal procedure borrows the doorway: evidence stands outside until the rules of admissibility let it in, and the ruling that opens the door is called an admission.
senses.whyCN: 法律程序借用了这道门：证据本来站在门外，直到可采性规则把它放进来，而那道开门的裁定就叫 admission。

intro.en: Admit comes from Latin admittere, 'to send in', the same verb that gives admission; English took it through Old French and later reshaped it after the Latin spelling.
intro.cn: admit 来自拉丁语 admittere「送进去」，与 admission 同出一个动词；英语经由古法语借入，后来又按拉丁拼写改写过。

items.en: Mittere meant 'to send, let go', and it also lies behind mission, permit and transmit.
items.cn: mittere 意为「送出、放开」，mission、permit 与 transmit 也都出自它。

items.en: Ad- 'to' plus mittere formed admittere, 'to send to, let in, allow to enter'.
items.cn: ad-「向」加 mittere 构成 admittere，意为「送到、放进来、准许进入」。

items.en: The past participle admissus meant 'let in, allowed', and it is the form from which the noun admissio was built.
items.cn: 过去分词 admissus 意为「被放进的、获准的」，名词 admissio 正是由这个形式构成。

items.en: Old French amettre meant 'to send, allow'; English borrowed it in the Middle English period and later respelled the word closer to Latin admittere.
items.cn: 古法语 amettre 意为「送出、允许」；英语在中古英语时期借入，后来又把拼写改得更接近拉丁语 admittere。

items.en: The verb is recorded in the fifteenth century for allowing entry; the sense of acknowledging a fact appears in the sixteenth century, and the pattern admit of is established by the seventeenth. Exact dates are approximate.
items.cn: 这个动词在十五世纪有「准许进入」的记录；承认事实的义项见于十六世纪，admit of 这一结构到十七世纪已经确立。确切年代只是近似。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers forms of the same Latin verb and one word with a different prefix; the near-meaning group gathers other ways of saying that something is true or that entry is allowed.
note.cn: 形近组收同一个拉丁动词的各路形式，以及一个前缀不同的同根词；近义组收其他表示「承认事实」与「允许进入」的说法。

entries.definition: The noun of the same verb, naming the act of letting in or of acknowledging something.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，与 admit 同出一源，表示「放行」或「承认」这一行为。

entries.definition: The right to enter, formed with -ance and often seen on official notices.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「进入权」，由 -ance 构成，常见于正式告示。

entries.definition: An adverb meaning 'it must be admitted that'; formed from the past participle plus -ly.
entries.definitionCN: 副词，义为「诚然、无可否认地」，由过去分词加 -ly 构成。

entries.definition: Allowed to be used as evidence or accepted as valid.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「可采纳的、可接受的」。

entries.definition: To carry out a crime or to promise yourself to something; it shares mittere but not the door of ad-.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「犯（罪）、承诺」；与 admit 同出 mittere，但没有 ad- 那扇门的意象。

entries.definition: To admit guilt or wrongdoing, especially in religion or law; heavier in tone than admit.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「供认、忏悔」，多用于宗教或法律，语气比 admit 更重。

entries.definition: To accept or recognise that something is true or that someone exists; more formal and often more neutral.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「承认、认可」，更正式，也常更中性，还可表示「确认收到」。

entries.definition: To admit that something is true only after resisting, usually in an argument or contest.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「让步承认」，往往是在争论或较量中先抵抗再承认。

entries.definition: To let something happen or let someone do something; it names permission, not the acknowledgement of a fact.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「允许」，说的是准许，而不是承认某个事实。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the real Latin verb mittere and the structures admit to and admit of.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些记忆钩子使用真实的拉丁动词 mittere，以及 admit to 与 admit of 这两个结构。

normal.en: Mittere is 'to send', so admit is to send someone in through the door.
normal.cn: mittere 是「送」，所以 admit 就是把某人送进门里。

normal.en: The same verb gives admission, admittance and admissible.
normal.cn: 同一个动词还给出 admission、admittance 与 admissible。

normal.en: Admit to marks the fault you let into the record.
normal.cn: admit to 标出的是你放进记录的那项过错。

normal.en: Be admitted to hospital is the passive of the same doorway.
normal.cn: be admitted to hospital 就是那扇门在被动语态里的样子。

normal.en: Admit of means the situation leaves room for a reading; in the negative it leaves none.
normal.cn: admit of 表示某种情况给某种解读留了余地；用在否定句里就是一点余地都没有。

abstract.en: Picture one doorkeeper doing two jobs at once: letting a visitor in and letting a secret out.
abstract.cn: 想象一个守门人同时做两件事：放一位访客进来，同时放一个秘密出去。

abstract.en: Everything admit does is about crossing a boundary, whether that boundary is a doorway, a rule or a silence.
abstract.cn: admit 做的一切都关乎跨过一道界线，不管这道界线是门框、规矩，还是沉默。

abstract.en: A hall that admits five hundred people and a court that admits a tape are both measuring how much can pass through.
abstract.cn: 能容纳五百人的大厅和采纳一盘录音的法庭，量的都是「允许多少东西通过」。

examples.en: She admitted that she had never read the report.
examples.cn: 她承认自己从未读过那份报告。

examples.en: The club admits new members only after a vote.
examples.cn: 这个俱乐部只有经过投票才会接纳新会员。

examples.en: The hall admits up to five hundred people.
examples.cn: 这个大厅最多可容纳五百人。

sensesIntro.en: Seven senses of admit all describe something crossing a boundary: a fact past your silence, a fault past your pride, a person past a door, a student past a rule, a crowd into a hall, a possibility into a reading, or a tape into a courtroom.
sensesIntro.cn: admit 的七个义项都在描述某物跨过一道界线：事实跨过你的沉默、过错跨过你的自尊、一个人跨过门、一名学生跨过规矩、一群人进到厅里、一种可能性进入某种解读，或一盘录音进入法庭。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a doorkeeper steps aside and lets someone, or some fact, through the gate.
core.cn: 核心意象：守门人侧身让开，放一个人或一个事实通过闸口。

branches.en: THE TRUTH: something kept outside the door of speech is finally let in.
branches.cn: 真相线：一直被挡在言语门外的东西终于被放了进来。

branches.en: THE INSTITUTION: a person is sent through a real doorway or through the rules of a school.
branches.cn: 机构线：一个人被送过真实的门，或被送过一所学校的规矩。

branches.en: THE SPACE: the building itself becomes the doorkeeper and counts how many it can let through.
branches.cn: 空间线：建筑自己成了守门人，数着自己能放多少人通过。

branches.en: THE POSSIBILITY: a situation lets a reading through, or refuses to.
branches.cn: 可能性线：一种情况放过某种解读，或者拒绝放过。

branches.en: THE COURT: evidence waits outside until the rules of admissibility open the door.
branches.cn: 法庭线：证据在门外等着，直到可采性规则把门打开。
