definition_zh: 收养；采纳；采用；正式通过；采取（态度）；选定（候选人）
definition_en: to take a child into your family as your own, or to accept and begin to use an idea, method or plan
core_image: 把别人的孩子或别人的主意，认下来变成自己的
scene: 社区活动室里，居民围坐讨论新的垃圾分类办法。The committee voted to adopt the new recycling plan.
sceneCN: 这里 adopt 指委员会投票正式通过一份方案（第 4 个义项：正式通过决议或计划）；句意为委员会投票通过了新的回收计划。

pos.zh: 动词：收养；采纳；采用；正式通过；选定

derivatives.zh: 由拉丁名词 adoptio 而来，义为「收养；采纳；采用」
由本词加形容词后缀 -ive 构成，义为「收养的；有收养关系的」
由本词加后缀 -able 构成，义为「可收养的；可采用的」
由本词加表示「人」的后缀 -er 构成，义为「收养人；采用者」

senses.title: To take a child into your family legally
senses.definition: to take another person's child into your family and become its legal parent
senses.definitionCN: 把别人的孩子接进自己的家庭，成为其法定父母
senses.example: The couple adopted a girl from the local orphanage.
senses.exampleCN: 这对夫妇从当地孤儿院收养了一个女孩。
senses.why: Optare means 'to choose', so adoption is a choosing into the family: the child is not born into it but picked out and made one's own, with ad- marking the direction towards oneself.
senses.whyCN: optare 意为「选择」，所以收养是一次「选进家门」：孩子不是生在这个家里，而是被挑中并认作自己的，ad- 标出的正是「朝向自己」的方向。

senses.title: To accept an idea or suggestion
senses.definition: to accept an idea, suggestion or proposal and treat it as your own
senses.definitionCN: 接受某个想法、建议或提议，并把它当作自己的
senses.example: The manager adopted my suggestion for the new schedule.
senses.exampleCN: 经理采纳了我关于新排班表的建议。
senses.why: An idea offered by someone else is chosen out of several and taken over, which is the same gesture as taking a child into the household: it stops being theirs and becomes yours.
senses.whyCN: 别人提出的主意，被从几个选项里挑出来接手过来，这和小孩子被接进家门是同一个动作：它不再属于对方，而成了你的。

senses.title: To start using a method or system
senses.definition: to begin to use a particular method, system, technology or way of working
senses.definitionCN: 开始使用某种方法、制度、技术或工作方式
senses.example: Many schools have adopted a shorter lunch break.
senses.exampleCN: 许多学校采用了更短的午休安排。
senses.why: Choosing a method is only the first step: once chosen it is made yours and repeated until it becomes routine, so the word covers both the decision and the daily practice that follows.
senses.whyCN: 选中一种方法只是第一步：一旦选定，它就被认作自己的并且反复执行，直到成为惯例，所以这个词同时覆盖决定与随后每天的实行。

senses.title: To approve a resolution formally
senses.titleCN: 正式通过（决议、法案、预算）
senses.definition: of a committee, board or assembly, to formally accept and approve a resolution, law or budget
senses.definitionCN: 指委员会、董事会或议会正式接受并通过决议、法律或预算
senses.example: The board adopted the budget after a long debate.
senses.exampleCN: 董事会经过长时间辩论后通过了预算。
senses.why: A vote is a public choosing: the text is selected from alternatives and from that moment belongs to the body that passed it, which is why the word suits resolutions and budgets.
senses.whyCN: 投票是一次公开的选择：文本从若干备选里被挑出，从那一刻起就属于通过它的那个机构，所以这个词特别适合决议与预算。

senses.title: To take up an attitude or position
senses.definition: to take up a particular attitude, position, tone or stance, often for a purpose
senses.definitionCN: 采取某种态度、立场、语气或姿态，往往带有目的
senses.example: He adopted a calm tone even though he was furious.
senses.exampleCN: 尽管非常恼火，他还是采取了平静的语气。
senses.why: An attitude can be put on like a coat chosen for the weather: the verb keeps the old 'take to oneself' gesture, and what is taken up may be a manner rather than an object.
senses.whyCN: 态度可以像按天气挑一件外套那样披上：这个动词保留了古老的「取为自己所有」的动作，被取用的可能是一种做派，而不是一件实物。

senses.title: To select a candidate for office
senses.definition: of a political party or group, to choose and officially accept someone as its candidate
senses.definitionCN: 指政党或团体挑选并正式认可某人为其候选人
senses.example: The party adopted her as its candidate for the city council.
senses.exampleCN: 该党选定她为市议会的候选人。
senses.why: A party picks one name out of the field and stands behind it; the choosing is made official, so the person is adopted in the old sense of being taken up as one's own.
senses.whyCN: 政党从一群人里挑出一个名字并站到它后面；这次选择被正式确认，于是这个人就在「被认作自己人」的古老意义上被 adopt 了。

intro.en: Adopt comes from Latin adoptare, built on optare 'to choose', and it reached English through Old French with the legal sense of taking a child first.
intro.cn: adopt 来自拉丁语 adoptare，建立在 optare「选择」之上，经古法语进入英语，最早带的正是「收养孩子」这一法律义。

items.en: Optare meant 'to choose, wish, desire', and it also gives English option and optional.
items.cn: optare 意为「选择、希望、想要」，英语的 option 与 optional 也出自它。

items.en: Ad- 'to' plus optare formed adoptare, 'to choose for oneself, take as one's own'. The oldest use is of taking a child into a family.
items.cn: ad-「朝向」加 optare 构成 adoptare，意为「选来作为自己的、认作己有」；最古老的用法就是收养孩子。

items.en: The noun adoptio named the legal act of adopting a child, and adoptatus was its past participle.
items.cn: 名词 adoptio 指收养孩子的法律行为，adoptatus 是它的过去分词。

items.en: Old French adopter kept the legal sense, and English borrowed the verb from it in the fifteenth century.
items.cn: 古法语 adopter 保留了法律义，英语在十五世纪从这个形式借入了动词。

items.en: The sense of taking a child comes first; taking up an idea, method or attitude develops later, and the parliamentary sense of adopting a resolution is later still. Exact dates are approximate.
items.cn: 收养孩子的义项出现最早；采纳想法、方法或态度的义项后来才发展出来，而议会「通过决议」的义项更晚。确切年代只是近似。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the word's own family and one relative from the same Latin verb of choosing; the near-meaning group gathers other verbs of taking something up or of approving it.
note.cn: 形近组收这个词自己的词族，以及一个同出拉丁「选择」动词的亲属；近义组收其他表示「接手采用」或「批准」的动词。

entries.definition: The noun for the act of adopting a child, an idea or a rule.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「收养、采纳、采用」，指收养孩子、采纳想法或采用规则的行为。

entries.definition: An adjective describing a parent or family related by adoption rather than by birth.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「收养的」，指通过收养而非血缘建立的父母或家庭关系。

entries.definition: Able to be adopted, said especially of children or animals waiting for a home.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「可收养的、可采用的」，尤指等待家庭的孩子或动物。

entries.definition: A person who adopts a child, an animal or a new practice.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「收养人、采用者」，指收养孩子、领养动物或采用新做法的人。

entries.definition: A choice or the right to choose; it shares optare with adopt but has no ad- and no idea of taking something over.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「选择、选项」；与 adopt 同出 optare，但没有 ad-，也不含「接手过来」的意思。

entries.definition: To accept an idea or change with enthusiasm; warmer and more emotional than adopt.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「欣然接受」，带有热情，比 adopt 更有情绪色彩。

entries.definition: To take on a role, duty or manner; it also means to suppose something is true.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「承担、采取（姿态）」，另有「假定」的意思。

entries.definition: To care for a child in your home for a period without becoming its legal parent.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「寄养、代为抚养」，只在一段时间内照顾孩子，并不成为其法定父母。

entries.definition: To officially agree to a plan or request; it names the consent, not the taking over.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「批准、同意」，说的是准许，而不是接手使用。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the real Latin verb optare and the objects that adopt most often takes.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些记忆钩子使用真实的拉丁动词 optare，以及 adopt 最常接的那些对象。

normal.en: Optare is 'to choose', so adopt is to choose something and make it your own.
normal.cn: optare 是「选择」，所以 adopt 就是把某样东西选中并变成自己的。

normal.en: Option and adopt share the same root: one offers a choice, the other takes it.
normal.cn: option 与 adopt 同根：一个提供选项，另一个把选项接过来。

normal.en: You adopt a child, a policy, an approach or a resolution, and in each case the object becomes yours.
normal.cn: 你可以收养孩子、采用政策、采用方法或通过决议，每一种情况下对象都变成了你的。

normal.en: Adopt a tone is the word at its most flexible: even a manner of speaking can be taken up.
normal.cn: adopt a tone 是这个词最灵活的用法：连说话的语气都可以被「取用」。

normal.en: A party adopts a candidate, turning a private choice into an official one.
normal.cn: 政党 adopt 一位候选人，就是把私下里的选择变成正式的决定。

abstract.en: Picture a signature at the bottom of a page: what was someone else's becomes yours the moment the pen lifts.
abstract.cn: 想象纸页下方的一笔签名：笔一抬起来，原本属于别人的东西就成了你的。

abstract.en: The word always moves in one direction, from outside the circle to inside it.
abstract.cn: 这个词的动作永远朝一个方向走：从圈子外面走到圈子里面。

abstract.en: A child, an idea and a budget all cross the same line, and the line is the decision to take them in.
abstract.cn: 一个孩子、一个主意和一份预算跨过的是同一条线，这条线就是「决定把它们收进来」。

examples.en: The couple decided to adopt a child from the local orphanage.
examples.cn: 这对夫妇决定从当地孤儿院收养一个孩子。

examples.en: Many schools have adopted a shorter lunch break.
examples.cn: 许多学校采用了更短的午休安排。

examples.en: The board adopted the budget after a long debate.
examples.cn: 董事会经过长时间辩论后通过了预算。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「阿多普特」——阿多一把抱起孤儿普特：收养；转头又把邻居的办法也抱过来用：采纳。

root: 拉丁语 adoptare「选来作为自己的」，由 ad-「朝向」+ optare「选择、愿望」构成；optare 同时是 option 与 optional 的词根，adoptare 最早专指收养孩子。

sensesIntro.en: All six senses of adopt are one act of choosing something outside the circle and taking it inside: a child, a suggestion, a method, a resolution, a manner, or a candidate.
sensesIntro.cn: adopt 的六个义项都是同一个动作：把圈子外面的东西选中并接进圈子里，可能是孩子、建议、方法、决议、做派或候选人。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a signature makes something that belonged to others belong to you.
core.cn: 核心意象：一笔签名，让原本属于别人的东西归了自己。

branches.en: THE FAMILY: the oldest sense, where a child is chosen into a household.
branches.cn: 家庭线：最古老的义项，孩子被选进一个家庭。

branches.en: THE IDEA: someone else's suggestion is picked up and spoken of as yours.
branches.cn: 想法线：别人提出的建议被接过来，从此算作你的。

branches.en: THE METHOD: the chosen way of working is repeated until it becomes habit.
branches.cn: 方法线：被选中的做法不断重复，直到成为惯例。

branches.en: THE ASSEMBLY: a vote turns a private choice into a binding decision.
branches.cn: 议事线：一次投票把私下的选择变成有约束力的决定。

branches.en: THE SURFACE: a manner put on like a coat, and a candidate taken up as the party's own.
branches.cn: 表层线：像披外套一样采取某种做派，以及把某位候选人认作本党的人。

intro.en: Adopt is a Latin verb of choosing; its stem and its Latin noun adoptio build the modern family.
intro.cn: adopt 是一个表示「选择」的拉丁动词；它的词干与拉丁名词 adoptio 撑起了现代这一词族。

latinIntro.en: Latin optare, adoptare, adoptio and adoptatus are all recorded, so nothing in this family has to be reconstructed.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 optare、adoptare、adoptio 与 adoptatus 都有文献记录，这一词族里没有需要重构的成分。

items.exampleCN: 它还给出 option 与 optional。

items.meaning: adoption, a taking as one's own

items.exampleCN: 它是英语名词的来源。

items.exampleCN: 这个词干把词义带进 adoption 与 adoptive。

definition_zh: 成年人；成体；成年的；仅限成年人的；成熟的
definition_en: a person or animal that is fully grown, or having reached the stage of full growth
core_image: 个头已经长足的人站在孩子身后，一伸手就够到了高处的箱子
scene: 候车室里，一个小女孩踮起脚去够行李架上的箱包。A tall adult lifted the suitcase down for her.
sceneCN: 这里 adult 指成年人（第 1 个义项：已经长大的人）；句意为一位高个子成年人帮她把箱子取了下来。

pos.zh: 名词：成年人；成体
形容词：成年的；仅限成年人的；成熟的

collocations.zh: 青壮年；刚成年的年轻人

derivatives.zh: 由本词加名词后缀 -hood 构成，义为「成年；成年期」
由本词加后缀 -like 构成，义为「像成年人一样的」

senses.title: A person who is fully grown
senses.definition: a person who has finished growing and has reached the age at which they are legally responsible
senses.definitionCN: 身体已经长成、并达到法定责任年龄的人
senses.example: Every adult in the room was asked to sign the form.
senses.exampleCN: 房间里的每位成年人都被要求在这张表上签字。
senses.why: Adultus is the past participle of adolescere, 'to grow up', so the noun literally names someone who has grown: the word describes a finished growth, not a birthday.
senses.whyCN: adultus 是 adolescere「长大」的过去分词，所以这个名词字面上指「已经长成的人」：这个词描述的是长成的状态，而不是某次生日。

senses.title: A fully grown animal or plant
senses.definition: an animal, plant or insect that has reached its final stage of growth
senses.definitionCN: 已经到达生长最后阶段的动物、植物或昆虫
senses.example: The adult of this moth lives for only a few days.
senses.exampleCN: 这种蛾的成体只能活几天。
senses.why: The same participle is applied to organisms that never sign a form: whatever has reached its final form counts as adult, so the word marks a stage of growth rather than a legal age.
senses.whyCN: 同一个分词也被用在从不签表格的生物身上：凡是长到最终形态的，都算作 adult，可见这个词标的是生长阶段，而不是法定年龄。

senses.title: Fully grown, as an adjective
senses.definition: of a person or animal, having reached full size or maturity
senses.definitionCN: 指人或动物已经长到完整尺寸或达到成熟
senses.example: An adult male can weigh over two hundred kilos.
senses.exampleCN: 一头成年雄性可以重达两百多公斤。
senses.why: The adjective keeps the participle's force, 'having grown up', and simply attaches that finished state to a body, without adding any legal or social claim.
senses.whyCN: 形容词保留了分词原有的「已经长成」这层力量，只把这种完成状态挂在一个身体上，并不附加法律或社会层面的判断。

senses.title: Intended only for adults
senses.definition: of films, books or websites, intended only for grown people, often because of sex or violence
senses.definitionCN: 指电影、书刊或网站只供成年人观看，常因涉及性内容或暴力
senses.example: The site asks for proof of age before showing adult content.
senses.exampleCN: 这个网站在展示成人内容前会要求验证年龄。
senses.why: Here the word stops describing a body and starts drawing a line: what lies behind the line may be seen only by those who have already grown, so adult becomes a label on the boundary itself.
senses.whyCN: 这里这个词不再描述身体，而是划出一条线：线后面的东西只有已经长大的人才可以看，于是 adult 成了贴在这道界线上的标签。

senses.title: Sensible and responsible
senses.definition: of behaviour or a manner, sensible, responsible and free of childishness
senses.definitionCN: 指行为或态度明理、负责、不带孩子气
senses.example: She gave a very adult answer to a rude question.
senses.exampleCN: 面对一个无礼的问题，她给出了十分成熟的回答。
senses.why: Maturity is read as conduct rather than age: because the word already means 'grown', it can be borrowed for behaviour, and a child can act adult while a grown person may not.
senses.whyCN: 成熟可以从行为而不是年龄上看出来：正因为这个词本义就是「长成」，它可以被借去形容举止，于是孩子也能表现得很 adult，而成年人未必做得到。

intro.en: Adult is the Latin past participle of 'to grow up', taken into English first as an adjective and only later as a noun.
intro.cn: adult 是拉丁语「长大」的过去分词，先作为形容词进入英语，后来才用作名词。

items.en: Alere meant 'to nourish, feed', and it also lies behind aliment and the growth word adolescere.
items.cn: alere 意为「养育、喂养」，aliment 以及表示生长的 adolescere 也都出自它。

items.en: Alescere was an inceptive verb meaning 'to begin to grow, be nourished', formed from alere.
items.cn: alescere 是由 alere 构成的起始动词，意为「开始生长、得到滋养」。

items.en: Ad- 'to' plus alescere formed adolescere, 'to grow up'; its present participle adolescens gives English adolescent.
items.cn: ad-「向」加 alescere 构成 adolescere，意为「长大」；它的现在分词 adolescens 给出英语的 adolescent。

items.en: The past participle adultus meant 'grown up, mature', and English took the adjective from this form.
items.cn: 过去分词 adultus 意为「已长成的、成熟的」，英语正是从这个形式借走了形容词。

items.en: The adjective is recorded in English in the fifteenth century, and the noun for a grown person becomes common from the seventeenth. The use of adult for content meant only for grown people is a twentieth-century development.
items.cn: 形容词在十五世纪见于英语，指「成年人」的名词用法从十七世纪起变得常见；而把 adult 用在「仅限成人观看的内容」上，是二十世纪才发展出的用法。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the word's own forms and the two Latin relatives from the same verb of growing; the near-meaning group sets grown-up and mature beside the legal opposites.
note.cn: 形近组收这个词自身的形式，以及同出拉丁「生长」动词的两个亲属；近义组把 grown-up、mature 与法律上的反义说法放在一起。

entries.definition: The period or state of being an adult, formed with the suffix -hood.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「成年、成年期」，由后缀 -hood 构成。

entries.definition: A young person who is growing up but has not yet finished; it comes from the same Latin verb as adult.
entries.definitionCN: 名词或形容词，义为「青少年、青春期的」；与 adult 同出拉丁语中表示「长大」的那个动词，指尚未长成的人。

entries.definition: The period between childhood and adulthood, from the same Latin growth verb.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「青春期」，同样来自那个表示生长的拉丁动词。

entries.definition: Resembling an adult in manner or appearance, formed with -like.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「像成年人一样的」，由后缀 -like 构成。

entries.definition: An adult, used especially by or to children; warmer and more conversational than adult.
entries.definitionCN: 名词或形容词，义为「大人、成年人的」，多为儿童使用或对儿童使用，比 adult 更口语、更亲切。

entries.definition: Fully developed in body or behaviour; it stresses development rather than the legal status of adult.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「成熟的」，强调发育或行为上的成熟，而不强调成年的法律身份。

entries.definition: A person below the legal age of adulthood; the legal opposite of an adult.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「未成年人」，是 adult 在法律意义上的反义说法。

entries.definition: Young and not yet adult, used especially in law and biology; formal in tone.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词或名词，义为「少年的、幼体」，多用于法律与生物学，语气正式，与成年相对。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the real Latin verb alere and the phrases adult actually appears in.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些记忆钩子使用真实的拉丁动词 alere，以及 adult 实际出现的搭配。

normal.en: Alere is 'to nourish': adult is the participle of a body that has been fed up to full size.
normal.cn: alere 是「养育」：adult 就是一个被养到足量的身体留下的分词。

normal.en: Adolescere means 'to grow up'; adolescent is still growing, adult has finished.
normal.cn: adolescere 意为「长大」：adolescent 还在长，adult 已经长完。

normal.en: Adulthood is the state, and adultlike describes anything that resembles it.
normal.cn: adulthood 是那种状态，adultlike 描述任何与之相似的东西。

normal.en: Adult education is schooling for grown people, not a lesson in how to be grown.
normal.cn: adult education 是给已经长大的人办的教育，不是教人怎样长大的课。

normal.en: An adult film is marked by an age line, not by the age of the actors.
normal.cn: adult film 的标记是一道年龄界线，而不是演员的年龄。

abstract.en: Picture a height mark on a door frame: the word points at the line a body has finally reached.
abstract.cn: 想象门框上的一道身高记号：这个词指的就是身体终于到达的那条线。

abstract.en: The same line can be drawn around a person, a moth, a plant or a film.
abstract.cn: 同一条线可以画在一个人身上，也可以画在一只蛾、一棵植物或一部电影上。

abstract.en: Because the word means 'finished growing', it can praise a child's behaviour as easily as it can label a whole industry.
abstract.cn: 正因为这个词的意思是「长完了」，它既能夸奖一个孩子的举止，也能给整个行业贴标签。

examples.en: Every adult in the room was asked to sign the form.
examples.cn: 房间里的每位成年人都被要求在这张表上签字。

examples.en: The adult of this moth lives for only a few days.
examples.cn: 这种蛾的成体只能活几天。

examples.en: The site asks for proof of age before showing adult content.
examples.cn: 这个网站在展示成人内容前会要求验证年龄。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「阿达特」——阿达个子终于长足，家里人才改口叫他大人：成年人、成年的。

root: 拉丁语 adultus「已长成的」，是 adolescere「长大」的过去分词；adolescere 由 ad-「向」+ alescere「生长」构成，alescere 又出自 alere「养育」。

sensesIntro.en: All five senses grow out of one participle meaning 'having grown': a person, a plant or insect, an adjective for full size, a line drawn around forbidden content, and behaviour that looks mature.
sensesIntro.cn: 五个义项都长自同一个意为「已经长成」的分词：一个人、一株植物或一只昆虫、形容尺寸长足的形容词、围住不宜内容的一道线，以及看起来成熟的举止。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a mark on a door frame showing the height a body has finally reached.
core.cn: 核心意象：门框上的一道记号，标出身体最终到达的高度。

branches.en: THE PERSON: the grown human being, the sense that carries the word today.
branches.cn: 人线：已经长成的人，是今天最常用的义项。

branches.en: THE ORGANISM: the same stage word applied to animals, plants and insects.
branches.cn: 生物线：同一个表示阶段的词，被用在动物、植物与昆虫身上。

branches.en: THE BODY: the adjective simply states that full size has been reached.
branches.cn: 身体线：形容词只是说明已经长到完整尺寸。

branches.en: THE LINE: the word turns into a boundary drawn around forbidden material.
branches.cn: 界线线：这个词变成围住不宜内容的一道边界。

branches.en: THE MANNER: maturity moves from the body to behaviour.

definition_zh: 前进；推进；进展；晋升；提出；预付；前进的步伐；上涨
definition_en: to move forward, to make progress, to raise to a higher rank, to put forward an idea, or to pay money before it is due
core_image: 一队人顶着风朝雾里迈步，最前面的那一排最先被雾吞掉
scene: 雨夜里，队伍沿山脊缓慢向前，探路的灯在雾里忽明忽暗。The column advanced along the ridge without a sound.
sceneCN: 这里 advance 指队伍在地面上向前移动（第 1 个义项：向前挺进）；句意为队伍沿着山脊悄无声息地前进。

pos.zh: 动词：前进；推进；进展；晋升；提出；预付
名词：前进；进展；预付款；上涨

derivatives.zh: 由本词加名词后缀 -ment 构成，义为「推进；进步；晋升」
由本词加 -ed 构成形容词，义为「高级的；先进的；晚期的」
由本词加 -ing 构成形容词，义为「前进的；发展中的」

senses.title: To move forward on the ground
senses.definition: to move forward, especially as a group or a body of troops moving towards a place
senses.definitionCN: 向前移动，尤指队伍或军队朝某地推进
senses.example: The troops advanced through the valley at dawn.
senses.exampleCN: 部队在黎明时穿过山谷推进。
senses.why: The Latin element ante means before or in front, so to advance is literally to put the body in front of the point it held.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语成分 ante 意为「在前面」，所以 advance 字面上就是把身体放到原先位置的前方。

senses.title: To make progress or develop
senses.definition: to develop, improve, or move to a higher stage, as knowledge, technology, or a plan does
senses.definitionCN: 指知识、技术或计划等发展、改善，进入更高阶段
senses.example: Research on batteries has advanced faster than expected.
senses.exampleCN: 电池研究的发展比预期更快。
senses.why: Progress is forward motion applied to something abstract; the same image of reaching the front is moved from feet to knowledge.
senses.whyCN: 进展是把「向前移动」用在抽象事物上；同一个「跑到最前面」的画面，从脚步移到了知识上。

senses.title: To rise to a higher rank
senses.definition: to raise someone to a higher position or rank, or to rise to one
senses.definitionCN: 把某人提到更高的职位或等级，或本人升到更高位置
senses.example: She was advanced to head of the department after two years.
senses.exampleCN: 两年后她被提升为部门主管。
senses.why: Standing at the front of a formation is both a place and a rank, so the spatial idea of moving forward became the social idea of promotion.
senses.whyCN: 站在队列前排既是位置，也是等级；于是「向前移动」这个空间概念就变成了「晋升」这个社会概念。

senses.title: To put forward an idea
senses.definition: to suggest or present an idea, plan, or theory for other people to consider
senses.definitionCN: 提出想法、计划或理论，供他人考虑
senses.example: The engineer advanced a simple fix for the leaking pipe.
senses.exampleCN: 工程师为漏水的管道提出了一个简单的修补办法。
senses.why: To set something in front of people is to lay it on the table for discussion, so being in front turns into being proposed.
senses.whyCN: 把东西摆到众人前面，就是把它放到桌面上供人讨论；「在前」于是转成了「提出」。

senses.title: To pay money before it is due
senses.definition: to pay or lend money before it is owed or before the usual time
senses.definitionCN: 在应付之前或通常时间之前付出或借出钱款
senses.example: The publisher advanced her a sum against future sales.
senses.exampleCN: 出版商预支给她一笔钱，以后从销售中扣除。
senses.why: Money that arrives before the goods is like a runner who reaches the front early; the forward image is simply transferred to payment.
senses.whyCN: 钱比货物先到，就像一个提前跑到前面的人；「向前」的画面就这样被搬到了付款上。

senses.title: Forward movement or a step of progress
senses.definition: noun: forward movement, or a step of progress or improvement
senses.definitionCN: 名词，指向前的移动，或进展、改进的一步
senses.example: Recent advances in printing have cut the cost of small runs.
senses.exampleCN: 印刷术近来的进步降低了小批量印刷的成本。
senses.why: The noun keeps the physical picture intact: an advance is one step taken to the front, whether with the feet or in a field of study.
senses.whyCN: 名词完整保留了那个身体画面：advance 就是朝前迈出的一步，不论用脚走还是在某个领域里走。

senses.title: Money paid ahead of time
senses.definition: noun: money paid before it is earned or before the agreed time, often as a loan or a first instalment
senses.definitionCN: 名词，指在挣得之前或约定时间之前付出的钱，常为借款或首期款
senses.example: He asked for a cash advance on his salary.
senses.exampleCN: 他申请预支一部分工资现金。
senses.why: The noun can also name the thing that arrives early: the money itself stands in front of the work it is meant to pay for.
senses.whyCN: 名词也可以指那件「早到」的东西：钱本身站到了它本该偿付的活儿前面。

senses.title: To rise in price or value
senses.definition: of prices, shares, or amounts, to rise to a higher level
senses.definitionCN: 指价格、股票或数额上升到更高水平
senses.example: Shares advanced three percent after the announcement.
senses.exampleCN: 公告发布后股价上涨了百分之三。
senses.why: On a price chart, going up is drawn as moving to the right, so a rising line is literally a line that advances.
senses.whyCN: 在价格图表上，「向上」被画成向右延伸，所以一条上涨的线字面上就是一条向前推进的线。

intro.en: Advance came into English from Old French, and the older source is generally traced to Latin abante, 'from in front'.
intro.cn: advance 从古法语进入英语，更早的来源一般认为可追溯到拉丁语 abante，意为「从前面」。

items.en: Ante meant 'before, in front of', and it supplies the forward direction of the whole family.
items.cn: ante 意为「在……之前、在前面」，为这一族词提供了「向前」的方向。

items.en: Ab 'from' plus ante formed abante, 'from before, in front'. The form is late, and how far it was used in everyday speech is source uncertain.
items.cn: ab「从」加 ante 构成 abante，意为「从前面」。这个形式出现较晚，它在日常口语中用得多广，来源不确定。

items.en: Old French avancer meant 'to move forward, to push forward, to promote'; the loss of the b and the new ending are French developments.
items.cn: 古法语 avancer 意为「向前移动、推进、提升」；b 的脱落与新的词尾都是法语自身的变化。

items.en: English borrowed the verb as avancen in the thirteenth century; the noun advance appears later, built on the same French stem.
items.cn: 英语在十三世纪借入动词形式 avancen；名词 advance 出现较晚，建立在同一个法语词干上。

items.en: Commercial and financial uses grew in the eighteenth and nineteenth centuries: to advance money, a cash advance, and prices advancing in the market.
items.cn: 商业与金融用法在十八、十九世纪发展起来：advance money、cash advance，以及市场上的价格上涨。

note.en: The look-alike group is built on the same French stem; the near-meaning group gathers words for moving ahead, improving, promoting and paying early.
note.cn: 形近组都由同一个法语词干构成；近义组收表示向前、进步、提升与提前付款的词。

entries.definition: The noun for progress, or for promotion to a higher rank.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「推进、进步、晋升」，由本词加 -ment 构成。

entries.definition: At a high level or stage; also the past form of the verb.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「高级的、先进的、晚期的」，同时是动词的过去式与过去分词。

entries.definition: Moving forward or developing; the present participle of the verb.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词或现在分词，义为「前进的、发展中的」。

entries.definition: A related noun from the same French element avant, but it branched off to mean a favourable position.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「优势」，与本词同出古法语 avant「在前」，但已分化为表示有利位置的另一支。

entries.definition: To go on or move forward, often after a stop; more formal and less military.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「继续进行、前往」，常指停顿之后继续，语体更正式，军事色彩更弱。

entries.definition: To move forward or improve over time, stressing steady development rather than one step.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「前进、进展」，强调持续的逐步发展，而非单次迈步。

entries.definition: To move someone to a higher rank or position; the usual word for a job.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「提升、晋升」，是谈职位升迁时最常用的词。

entries.definition: To help something develop or succeed; a formal verb close to the supporting sense of advance.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「促进、推动」，语气正式，接近 advance 表示支持某事的那层意思。

entries.definition: Money lent, often the everyday word for a sum advanced to someone.
entries.definitionCN: 名词或动词，义为「贷款、借出」，常是预支给某人一笔钱时的日常说法。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the real Latin element ante and the everyday phrases the word appears in.
normalIntro.cn: 下面的记忆钩子使用真实的拉丁语成分 ante，以及这个词日常出现的搭配。

normal.en: Ante is 'before, in front', so whatever advances goes to the front of where it was.
normal.cn: ante 是「在前面」，所以任何 advance 都是跑到原先位置的前方。

normal.en: Old French avancer already meant both to move forward and to promote, so the job sense is old, not modern.
normal.cn: 古法语 avancer 已经同时表示「向前」与「提升」，所以晋升义由来已久，并非现代才有。

normal.en: In advance means the ticket, the warning or the money arrives before the thing itself.
normal.cn: in advance 指票、警告或钱比事情本身先到。

normal.en: An advance on a salary is money that runs ahead of the work it pays for.
normal.cn: an advance on a salary 就是跑到活儿前面的钱。

normal.en: On a chart the line advances to the right, which is why shares can advance.
normal.cn: 图表上的线向右推进，所以股票也可以用 advance 表示上涨。

abstract.en: Picture a column of soldiers stepping into fog: the front of the line keeps vanishing, and the back keeps filling the gap.
abstract.cn: 想象一队士兵走进雾里：队伍最前面不断消失，后面的人不断补上。

abstract.en: Every advance is a small trade, leaving a known spot for one you cannot see yet.
abstract.cn: 每一次前进都是一次小交换：离开熟悉的位置，走向还看不见的地方。

abstract.en: The same step forward can be a march, a discovery, a promotion or a payment made early; only the direction stays the same.
abstract.cn: 同一个向前的动作可以是行军、发现、升职或提前付款，不变的只有方向。

examples.en: The troops advanced through the valley at dawn.
examples.cn: 部队在黎明时穿过山谷推进。

examples.en: Research on batteries has advanced faster than expected.
examples.cn: 电池研究的发展比预期更快。

examples.en: He asked for a cash advance on his salary.
examples.cn: 他申请预支一部分工资现金。

sensesIntro.en: The eight senses all come from one gesture, putting something in front: a body, a project, a rank, an idea, a sum of money, a price.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项都出自同一个动作——把东西放到前面：身体、工程、职位、想法、钱款、价格。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a line of people stepping forward into fog, the front edge always the first to enter.
core.cn: 核心意象：一队人朝雾里迈步，最前面的边缘总是最先进入。

branches.en: THE BODY: a group moves to the front of the ground it occupies.
branches.cn: 身体线：队伍朝所占地面之前移动。

branches.en: THE PROJECT: forward motion becomes progress, and the noun names that single step.
branches.cn: 工程线：向前的动作变成进展，名词就指那迈出的一步。

branches.en: THE LADDER: standing at the front of a formation turns into standing higher in rank.
branches.cn: 阶梯线：站到队列前排，转成职位上的升高。

branches.en: THE TABLE: an idea is set in front of others so that they can examine it.
branches.cn: 桌面线：把想法摆到别人面前供人审视。

branches.en: THE MONEY: cash, wages and prices can all arrive early or move higher than the usual point.
branches.cn: 钱款线：现金、工资和价格都可以比通常的时点更早到达或走高。

definition_zh: 优势；有利条件；好处；领先；占先；（正式）有利于
definition_en: a condition that puts someone in a better position, a benefit, a lead over a rival, or a favourable use of something
core_image: 站在坡上的人往下一看，别人的路线全在自己眼里
scene: 这座山城交通不便，可空气干净、房租便宜，很多人舍不得搬走。The town's clean air and low rents are its main advantages.

senses.title: A condition that puts you in a better position
senses.definition: a circumstance, quality, or position that makes someone or something more likely to succeed than others
senses.definitionCN: 使某人或某物比其他人或物更可能成功的处境、特点或地位
senses.example: Speaking three languages is a real advantage in this job.
senses.exampleCN: 会三种语言在这份工作里是真正的优势。
senses.why: Old French avant means in front, so an advantage is literally the position of being out in front of others.
senses.whyCN: 古法语 avant 意为「在前面」，所以 advantage 字面上就是站在别人前面的那个位置。

senses.title: A benefit or good feature
senses.definition: a useful or favourable feature of something, especially when it is weighed against its drawbacks
senses.definitionCN: 某事物有用或有利的特点，尤指在与缺点权衡时
senses.example: One advantage of the flat is that it faces south.
senses.exampleCN: 这套公寓的一个好处是朝南。
senses.why: From 'being in front' comes 'what counts in your favour': a feature that puts the thing ahead when pros and cons are compared.
senses.whyCN: 从「站在前面」引申出「于你有利之处」：在权衡利弊时，把事物推到前面的那个特点就是好处。

senses.title: A lead over a rival
senses.definition: the state of being ahead of a competitor, or the margin by which you are ahead
senses.definitionCN: 领先于竞争者的状态，或领先的差距
senses.example: The home team held a two-goal advantage at half time.
senses.exampleCN: 主队在半场时保持两球领先。
senses.why: The spatial front becomes measurable: in a race or a match, being in front can be counted in goals, points, or seconds.
senses.whyCN: 空间上的「在前」变成了可计量的东西：在比赛里，领先可以用球数、分差或秒数来数。

senses.title: To make good use of something
senses.definition: in the phrase take advantage of, to use an opportunity or a situation for your own benefit
senses.definitionCN: 用于短语 take advantage of，指利用机会或形势为己谋利
senses.example: Take advantage of the quiet mornings to finish your reading.
senses.exampleCN: 利用清早安静的时间把阅读做完。
senses.why: To use a favourable position is to convert someone else's offered opening into your own front place.
senses.whyCN: 利用有利位置，就是把别人给出的机会转化成自己的「前排」。

senses.title: To treat someone unfairly for gain
senses.definition: in the phrase take advantage of, to treat someone unfairly in order to get what you want
senses.definitionCN: 用于短语 take advantage of，指为得到自己想要的东西而不公平地对待他人
senses.example: He took advantage of her kindness and borrowed money he never returned.
senses.exampleCN: 他利用她的好说话借了钱，却一直没有还。
senses.why: The same 'front position' can be abused: whoever is ahead can press the advantage against someone weaker.
senses.whyCN: 同一个「占前」的位置也可能被滥用：占上风的人会借势欺压较弱的一方。

senses.title: The next point after deuce
senses.definition: in tennis, the point scored after deuce, which lets the scorer win the game with one more point
senses.definitionCN: 网球中在平分之后得到的一分，再得一分即可赢下这一局
senses.example: She won the game on her second advantage.
senses.exampleCN: 她在第二次占先时赢下了这一局。
senses.why: The scoring term keeps the old spatial meaning: the player with the advantage is one step in front of an otherwise level score.
senses.whyCN: 这个计分术语保留了古老的空间义：拿到 advantage 的球员，在原本平分的比分上领先一步。

senses.title: In a way that shows something well
senses.definition: in the phrase to advantage, in a way that makes someone or something look as good as it can
senses.definitionCN: 用于短语 to advantage，指让某人或某物显得尽可能好看
senses.example: The low light showed the old hall to advantage.
senses.exampleCN: 昏暗的灯光把这间旧厅衬托得格外好看。
senses.why: Here the front position is visual: light or arrangement puts the best face of a thing forward for the viewer.
senses.whyCN: 这里「在前」是视觉上的：光线或布置把事物最好的一面推到观者眼前。

intro.en: Advantage is a French noun built on avant 'before, in front', the same element that lies behind advance.
intro.cn: advantage 是建立在 avant「在前」之上的法语名词，而 avant 也是 advance 背后的同一个成分。

items.en: Ante meant 'before, in front of' and is the ultimate source of the French element avant.
items.cn: ante 意为「在……之前、在前面」，是法语成分 avant 的最终来源。

items.en: Avant kept the Latin sense of being in front, in space as well as in rank or time.
items.cn: avant 保留了拉丁语「在前」的意思，既指空间，也指位次或时间。

items.en: Avantage named the state of being ahead, and early on it also meant profit or a favourable opportunity.
items.cn: avantage 指「处于前面」的状态，早期还表示好处或有利的机会。

items.en: English borrowed the noun in the fourteenth century; the verb followed, first in the sense of giving someone an edge.
items.cn: 英语在十四世纪借入这个名词；动词随后出现，最初表示给某人占先的机会。

items.en: The phrases take advantage of and to advantage spread widely, and tennis gave the word a fixed scoring sense.
items.cn: take advantage of 与 to advantage 两个短语广泛流行，网球又赋予这个词固定的计分义。

note.en: The look-alike group is the word's own family of forms and negatives; the near-meaning group gathers words for a favourable position or a benefit.
note.cn: 形近组是这个词自己的词族形式与否定形式；近义组收表示有利位置或好处的词。

entries.definition: Adjective meaning favourable or likely to bring success.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「有利的、有益的」，由本词加 -ous 构成。

entries.definition: Adverb meaning in a way that brings benefit.
entries.definitionCN: 副词，义为「有利地、有益地」，由 advantageous 加 -ly 构成。

entries.definition: A condition that makes success harder; the negative of the target noun.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「不利条件、劣势」，由否定前缀 dis- 加本词构成。

entries.definition: Adjective describing people who lack the ordinary chances others have.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「处于不利地位的、贫困的」，由 disadvantage 加 -d 构成。

entries.definition: A good effect or a gain from something; purely about what is gained, with no image of position.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「益处、好处」，只谈所得，没有「处于前面」的位置意象。

entries.definition: A small but decisive quality that makes one side more likely to win.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「微弱但关键的优势」，强调胜负天平上的那一点差别。

entries.definition: A good quality that deserves praise, judged on its own rather than against a rival.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「优点、长处」，就事论事地判断，而不是与他人比较。

entries.definition: The positive side of a situation, especially one that also has drawbacks.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「好处、有利的一面」，多用于本身也有缺点的情形，语气较口语。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the real French element avant 'in front' and the phrases the word appears in.
normalIntro.cn: 下面的记忆钩子使用真实的法语成分 avant「在前」，以及这个词实际出现的短语。

normal.en: Avant is 'in front', so an advantage is the place in front of everyone else.
normal.cn: avant 是「在前面」，所以 advantage 就是站在所有人前面的那个位置。

normal.en: Advantage and advance share the same French stem, which is why both are about being ahead.
normal.cn: advantage 与 advance 共用同一个法语词干，所以两者都围绕「在前」。

normal.en: Take advantage of keeps the old spatial idea: step into the opening while it is still open.
normal.cn: take advantage of 保留了古老的空间意象：趁着口子还开着就迈进去。

normal.en: A two-goal advantage is simply a front position that can be counted.
normal.cn: 两球领先不过是一个可以用数字数出来的「前排位置」。

normal.en: To advantage means the light or the setting has put the best side of a thing forward.
normal.cn: to advantage 指光线或环境把事物最好的一面推到了前面。

abstract.en: Picture one walker on a slope looking down at the whole path while the others see only the next step.
abstract.cn: 想象一个走在坡上的人俯看整条路线，而其他人只看得见下一步。

abstract.en: An advantage is not a thing; it is a relation between your position and everyone else's.
abstract.cn: 优势不是一件东西，而是你的位置与其他人位置之间的一种关系。

abstract.en: The same word covers a head start, a good feature and a kindness being abused, because all three are forms of standing ahead.
abstract.cn: 同一个词既指先手、又指优点、还指被人利用的善意，因为三者都是「占前」的不同形态。

examples.en: Speaking three languages is a real advantage in this job.
examples.cn: 会三种语言在这份工作里是真正的优势。

examples.en: The town's clean air and low rents are its main advantages.
examples.cn: 干净的空气和低廉的房租是这座城的主要长处。

examples.en: He took advantage of her kindness and borrowed money he never returned.
examples.cn: 他利用她的好说话借了钱，却一直没有还。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「阿德万提吉」——阿德站上万能台阶往下一看，谁都比他矮一截：优势。

root: 古法语 avantage「在前的位置、好处」，源头是 avant「在前面」，最终可追到拉丁语 ante「在……之前」。

sensesIntro.en: All seven senses describe some form of standing ahead: in chances, in usefulness, in a score, in the use of an opening, or in how something is shown.
sensesIntro.cn: 七个义项都在描述某种「站在前面」：机会上的、用处上的、比分上的、抓住口子上的，或呈现效果上的。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one walker stands higher on the slope and sees the whole path the others must still climb.
core.cn: 核心意象：一个行者站得更高，看得见别人还要爬的整条路。

branches.en: THE POSITION: being ahead of others, whether as a general condition or as a countable lead.
branches.cn: 位置线：领先他人，可以是总体处境，也可以是可数出的领先幅度。

branches.en: THE FEATURE: when pros and cons are weighed, the good feature is the one that comes out in front.
branches.cn: 特点线：权衡利弊时，好特点就是被推到前面的那一个。

branches.en: THE OPENING: a favourable situation is an opening that can be stepped into.
branches.cn: 机会线：有利形势就是一个可以迈进去的口子。

branches.en: THE ABUSE: the same front position can be used to press down on someone weaker.
branches.cn: 滥用线：同一个「占前」的位置，也可以用来欺压较弱的一方。

branches.en: THE FIXED USES: a tennis score and a phrase about lighting both keep the old spatial sense.
branches.cn: 固定用法线：网球比分与谈论光线的短语，都保留着古老的空间义。

intro.en: Advantage is a French noun whose stem is avant 'in front'; English added ordinary endings to build the family.
intro.cn: advantage 是词干为 avant「在前」的法语名词；英语再加上普通词尾构成这一词族。

latinIntro.en: Latin ante and abante are recorded, as is the French noun avantage; only the deeper Indo-European root of ante is reconstructed.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 ante 与 abante 都有记录，法语名词 avantage 也有记录；只有 ante 更早的印欧语词根属于重构。

items.example: Ante is the oldest recorded element behind the word.
items.exampleCN: ante 是这个词背后有记录的最古老成分。

items.example: It combines with ante in abante.
items.exampleCN: 它与 ante 组合成 abante。

items.example: Abante is generally taken as the older source of avant.
items.exampleCN: abante 一般认为就是 avant 的更早来源。

items.example: Avant is the stem of the whole family.
items.exampleCN: avant 是整个词族的词干。

items.example: English borrowed this noun as advantage.
items.exampleCN: 英语把这个名词借来作 advantage。

items.example: It turns avant into a noun of state.
items.exampleCN: 它把 avant 变成表示状态的名词。

items.example: It forms advantageous.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 advantageous。

items.example: It forms advantageously.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 advantageously。

items.example: It forms disadvantage.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 disadvantage。

derivatives.zh: 由本词加形容词后缀 -ous 构成，义为「有利的；有益的」
由否定前缀 dis- 加本词构成，义为「不利条件；劣势」
由 disadvantage 加 -d 构成形容词，义为「处于不利地位的」

definition_zh: 广告（英式口语）；提及、谈到（advert to，正式）；使人注意
definition_en: a British informal word for an advertisement, or a formal verb meaning to refer to something or to draw attention to it
core_image: 一只手把路人的脸轻轻掰向亮着的橱窗
scene: 电影开场前那几分钟，屏幕上一连放了好几段推销短片。She skipped every advert before the film started.
sceneCN: 这里 advert 是英式口语里的「广告」（第 1 个义项：广告）；句意为电影开场前她把每一段广告都跳过了。

pos.zh: 名词（英式口语）：广告
动词（正式）：提及；使人注意

derivatives.zh: 与本词同族的名词，由 advertise 加 -ment 构成，义为「广告」；本词正是它的缩略形式
与本词同族的动词，义为「做广告；宣传；登广告招聘」
由 advert 与 editorial 缩合而成的混成词，义为「社论式广告」

senses.title: A British word for an advertisement
senses.definition: a notice, picture, or short film that promotes a product, service, or event, used chiefly in British informal speech
senses.definitionCN: 推广商品、服务或活动的告示、图片或短片，主要用于英式口语
senses.example: He put an advert in the local paper for a second-hand bike.
senses.exampleCN: 他在本地报纸上登了一则二手自行车的广告。
senses.why: British speakers cut the long word advertisement down to its first two syllables, and the clipped form became the everyday spoken word.
senses.whyCN: 英国人把长词 advertisement 砍到开头两个音节，这个截短的形式就成了日常口语里的说法。

senses.title: To refer to something formally
senses.definition: to refer to a fact, topic, or event briefly, especially in speech or writing; used with to and mostly formal
senses.definitionCN: 简短地提到某个事实、话题或事件，尤见于讲话或文章，常与 to 连用，语体正式
senses.example: He adverted briefly to the earlier report.
senses.exampleCN: 他简短地提到了先前那份报告。
senses.why: Latin advertere is 'to turn toward', so to advert to a subject is to turn one's words in that direction.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 advertere 是「使转向」，所以 advert to 某话题就是把话头转向那个方向。

senses.title: To draw attention to something
senses.definition: to call attention to something, often a risk or a detail that others have overlooked
senses.definitionCN: 使人注意到某事，常指别人忽略的风险或细节
senses.example: The report adverted to the danger of relying on one supplier.
senses.exampleCN: 报告提示了只依赖一家供应商的危险。
senses.why: Turning someone toward a thing is the physical act behind the word: first the head turns, then the attention follows.
senses.whyCN: 把某人转向某物，正是这个词背后的身体动作：头先转过去，注意力随后跟上。

intro.en: Advert has two histories in one spelling: a Latin verb about turning attention, and a nineteenth-century British clipping of advertisement.
intro.cn: advert 这同一个拼写里装着两段历史：一段是拉丁语中表示「转动注意力」的动词，一段是十九世纪英式英语对 advertisement 的截短。

items.en: Ad 'to, toward' plus vertere 'to turn' formed advertere, 'to turn toward'.
items.cn: ad「朝向」加 vertere「转」构成 advertere，意为「使转向」。

items.en: The same verb also came to mean 'to turn the mind to, notice, pay attention', and this is the sense English kept.
items.cn: 同一个动词后来也表示「把心思转向、注意到、留意」，英语保留的正是这一层意思。

items.en: French developed avertir from the Latin verb, with the sense of turning someone's attention, often as a warning. Whether English took the verb through French or straight from Latin is not fully settled.
items.cn: 法语从这一拉丁动词发展出 avertir，意思是把人的注意力转向某处，常带警告意味。英语是经法语还是直接借自拉丁语，尚无定论。

items.en: The verb advert is recorded in the fifteenth century with the senses 'to notice' and 'to mention', usually with to.
items.cn: 动词 advert 在十五世纪有记录，义为「注意到」与「提及」，通常与 to 连用。

items.en: The noun advert is a clipped form of advertisement and is now marked as British and informal; the verb survives mainly in formal writing.
items.cn: 名词 advert 是 advertisement 的截短形式，如今标为英式口语；动词则主要残存于正式书面语。

note.en: The look-alike group is the advertising family the clipped noun belongs to; the near-meaning group gathers other words for public notices and promotion.
note.cn: 形近组是这个词所属的广告词族；近义组收其他表示公开告示与推广的词。

entries.definition: The full noun for a public notice that promotes something; the word this clipping comes from.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「广告」，是推广某事物的公开告示，也是本词截短前的完整形式。

entries.definition: The verb meaning to make a product, service, or job known to the public.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「做广告；宣传；登广告招聘」，与名词同属一族。

entries.definition: The activity or industry of promoting goods and services.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「广告业、广告活动」，由 advertise 加 -ing 构成。

entries.definition: An advertisement written and laid out to look like an ordinary article.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「社论式广告」，由 advert 与 editorial 缩合而成。

entries.definition: A short film promoting a product, broadcast on television or radio; a noun in this use.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「电视或广播广告」，特指播出的一段推销短片。

entries.definition: A public statement giving information; it need not sell anything.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「公告、通知」，只提供信息，不一定要推销东西。

entries.definition: A sign or printed sheet giving information or a warning.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「告示、通知」，指提供信息或警告的牌子或印刷品。

entries.definition: Activity that publicizes a product, often with special offers.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「推广、促销」，指宣传商品的活动，常伴随优惠。

entries.definition: An informal word for a mention that publicizes something, as on a show.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「（节目里的）宣传、推销」，属口语说法。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the real Latin verb advertere 'to turn toward' and the clipped noun's British setting.
normalIntro.cn: 下面的记忆钩子使用真实的拉丁动词 advertere「使转向」，以及这个截短名词的英式语境。

normal.en: Advertere is 'to turn toward': an advert turns your eyes toward a product.
normal.cn: advertere 是「使转向」：一条 advert 就是把你的眼睛转向某个商品。

normal.en: The verb keeps the older sense, so to advert to something is to turn your words toward it.
normal.cn: 动词保留更早的意思：advert to 某事就是把话头转向它。

normal.en: British speech clips advertisement to advert, just as it shortens many long borrowed words.
normal.cn: 英式口语把 advertisement 截成 advert，就像它缩短许多借来的长词一样。

normal.en: An advert break is the slot in which the turning of attention is sold.
normal.cn: advert break 就是拿「让人转头」这件事去卖钱的时段。

normal.en: Advert and avert look close but pull opposite ways: one turns toward, the other turns away.
normal.cn: advert 与 avert 长得像，方向却相反：一个转向，一个转开。

abstract.en: Picture a hand gently turning a passer-by's face toward a lit window.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手轻轻把路人的脸转向亮着的橱窗。

abstract.en: That single turn of the head is the whole history of the word: toward a product, toward a fact, toward a risk.
abstract.cn: 这一个转头的动作就是这个词的全部历史：转向商品、转向事实、转向风险。

abstract.en: An advert asks for a second of attention; the verb advert spends that second on a subject.
abstract.cn: 一条广告只求一秒钟的注意力；动词 advert 则把那一秒花在某个话题上。

examples.en: He put an advert in the local paper for a second-hand bike.
examples.cn: 他在本地报纸上登了一则二手自行车的广告。

examples.en: She never watches the adverts between the programmes.
examples.cn: 节目之间的广告她从来不看。

examples.en: He adverted briefly to the earlier report.
examples.cn: 他简短地提到了先前那份报告。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「阿德沃特」——阿德把路人的头一掰，全都转向橱窗：广告。

root: 拉丁语 advertere「使转向」，由 ad-「朝向」+ vertere「转」构成；动词「提及、使人注意」由此而来，名词 advert 则是 advertisement 的截短，属英式口语。

sensesIntro.en: Only a few senses survive: the clipped British noun for an advertisement, and the formal verb for turning attention or words toward something.
sensesIntro.cn: 现代留下的义项不多：英式口语中作 advertisement 缩略的名词，以及正式语体中表示把注意力或话语转向某事的动词。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a hand turns a passer-by's face toward a lit shop window.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只手把路人的脸转向亮着的橱窗。

branches.en: THE NOUN: a long borrowed noun is clipped into one brisk spoken word.
branches.cn: 名词线：一个长长的借词被砍成一个干脆的口语词。

branches.en: THE PLACEMENT: printed pages and broadcast slots are where that clipped noun lives.
branches.cn: 投放线：报纸版面与播出时段就是这个截短名词的活动场所。

branches.en: THE MENTION: the formal verb turns the flow of speech toward a topic.
branches.cn: 提及线：正式的动词把话语的流向转向某个话题。

branches.en: THE WARNING: attention is drawn to a risk before it does damage.
branches.cn: 提醒线：在风险造成伤害之前，把注意力引到它身上。

branches.en: THE SHARED TURN: whether selling, mentioning or warning, something is being turned toward the listener.
branches.cn: 共同转向：无论是推销、提及还是提醒，都是把某物转向听者。

intro.en: Advert rests on the Latin prefix ad- and the verb vertere; English adds ordinary endings to build the advertising family.
intro.cn: advert 建立在拉丁语前缀 ad- 与动词 vertere 之上；英语再加上普通词尾构成广告词族。

latinIntro.en: Latin vertere and advertere are recorded; the noun advert is not a Latin form but a modern English clipping.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 vertere 与 advertere 都有记录；名词 advert 并非拉丁语形式，而是现代英语的截短。

items.example: It joins vertere to form advertere.
items.exampleCN: 它与 vertere 结合构成 advertere。

items.example: The turning root is shared with convert and reverse.
items.exampleCN: 这个表示「转」的词根与 convert、reverse 共用。

items.example: English took its formal verb from this form.
items.exampleCN: 英语的正式动词就来自这个形式。

items.example: It forms advertise.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 advertise。

items.example: It forms advertisement.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 advertisement。

items.meaning: an activity or an action in progress
items.meaningCN: 活动，或正在进行的动作
items.example: It forms advertising.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 advertising。

items.example: It forms adverted.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 adverted。

items.example: It forms adverts.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 adverts。

items.meaning: an advertisement written like an article
items.example: The magazine placed an advertorial beside the feature.
items.exampleCN: 杂志在专题报道旁放了一篇社论式广告。

derivatives.zh: 与本词同族的动词，义为「做广告；宣传；登广告招聘」
由 advertise 加名词后缀 -ment 构成，义为「广告」
由 advertise 加 -ing 构成，义为「广告业；广告活动」

definition_zh: 做广告；宣传；登广告招聘；登广告征求；公开宣扬；使引人注意
definition_en: to make a product, service, or job known to the public, to ask for something by placing a notice, or to make something conspicuous
core_image: 一块牌子被举到人群头顶上，四周的人都抬起了头
scene: 街角面包店的玻璃上贴出一张手写纸条，说是缺一个帮手。The bakery advertised for an assistant in its window.
sceneCN: 这里 advertise 指登广告招人（第 2 个义项：登广告招聘）；句意为面包店在橱窗里登广告招一名帮手。

pos.zh: 动词：做广告；宣传；登广告招聘；登广告征求；使引人注意

derivatives.zh: 由本词加名词后缀 -ment 构成，义为「广告」
由本词加表示施动者的后缀 -er 构成，义为「广告主；登广告的人」
由本词加 -ing 构成，义为「广告业；广告活动」

senses.title: To promote goods or services publicly
senses.definition: to tell the public about a product, service, or event, usually by paying for space or time in the media
senses.definitionCN: 向公众介绍商品、服务或活动，通常通过付费购买媒体版面或时段
senses.example: The company advertised its new phone on television.
senses.exampleCN: 公司在电视上为新手机会做广告。
senses.why: The Latin verb means to turn someone toward something, and a paid advertisement is an organised way of turning a whole audience toward a product.
senses.whyCN: 这个拉丁动词意为把某人转向某物，而付费广告就是有组织地把整群观众转向一件商品。

senses.title: To announce a job vacancy
senses.definition: to make a job known publicly so that people can apply for it
senses.definitionCN: 公开告知某个职位空缺，以便人们前来应聘
senses.example: The bakery advertised for an assistant in its window.
senses.exampleCN: 面包店在橱窗里登广告招一名帮手。
senses.why: A vacancy is made public in the same way as a product: a notice turns the attention of anyone who might want it.
senses.whyCN: 职位空缺和商品一样被推到公众面前：一张告示把可能想来应征的人的注意力转过来。

senses.title: To ask for something by notice
senses.definition: to place a notice asking for something you want, such as a flat, a worker, or a lost item
senses.definitionCN: 刊登告示，寻求自己想要的东西，如房子、人手或失物
senses.example: They advertised for a lodger in the free paper.
senses.exampleCN: 他们在免费报纸上登广告找房客。
senses.why: Here the sign is turned toward the public with a question rather than an offer, but the mechanism is the same raised notice.
senses.whyCN: 这里的牌子带的是问题而不是推销，但机制相同：把告示举到公众面前。

senses.title: To make your own affairs public
senses.definition: to make something about yourself widely known, often in a way that draws unwanted judgement
senses.definitionCN: 把自己某方面的事广泛告知他人，常带有招来非议的意味
senses.example: He advertised his ignorance by arguing with the referee.
senses.exampleCN: 他跟裁判争执，等于公开宣扬自己的无知。
senses.why: The word can expose as well as sell: whatever is turned toward the crowd becomes public, including a fault you meant to hide.
senses.whyCN: 这个词既能推销也能暴露：凡是被转向人群的东西都会变公开，包括你本想藏起来的缺点。

senses.title: To make something stand out
senses.definition: of a feature, colour, or mark, to make something easily noticed, especially in formal or literary use
senses.definitionCN: 指某个特征、颜色或标记使事物容易被注意到，多用于正式或文学语体
senses.example: A bright red door advertised the little shop from the end of the street.
senses.exampleCN: 一扇鲜红的门从街尾就让人注意到这家小店。
senses.why: Anything conspicuous is, in the old sense, advertising itself: it turns the eye without paying for the attention.
senses.whyCN: 任何显眼的东西都在「老意义」上自我宣传：它不花钱就把目光转了过来。

senses.title: To be presented as something
senses.definition: in the pattern be advertised as, to be described in a particular way in order to attract people
senses.definitionCN: 用于 be advertised as 结构，指为了吸引人而以某种方式描述某事
senses.example: The event was advertised as a family day.
senses.exampleCN: 这场活动被宣传为家庭日。
senses.why: A notice does not only say what a thing is; it chooses a frame for it, and that chosen frame is what the public is turned toward.
senses.whyCN: 告示不只是说明事物是什么，还为它挑好一个框；公众被转向的正是这个挑好的框。

intro.en: Advertise began as a Latin verb about turning attention; its modern commercial sense is a later English development.
intro.cn: advertise 最初是一个表示「转动注意力」的拉丁动词；现代的商业义是英语后来发展出来的。

items.en: Ad 'to, toward' plus vertere 'to turn' formed advertere, 'to turn toward'.
items.cn: ad「朝向」加 vertere「转」构成 advertere，意为「使转向」。

items.en: The verb also took the sense 'to turn the mind to, notice, pay attention', which passed into French and English.
items.cn: 这个动词还发展出「把心思转向、注意到、留意」的意思，并传入法语和英语。

items.en: English recorded advertise in the fifteenth century meaning 'to turn one's attention' and 'to inform, give notice'.
items.cn: 英语在十五世纪记录到 advertise，义为「把注意力转向」以及「告知、通知」。

items.en: The sense moved from informing one person to giving public notice of goods, and newspapers made this the dominant use.
items.cn: 词义从告知某个人，转为公开告知商品信息；报纸让这一用法成为主流。

items.en: The commercial sense is now the main one; advertisement was formed from the verb with -ment, and British speech clips it to advert.
items.cn: 商业义如今是主要义项；advertisement 由这个动词加 -ment 构成，英式口语又把它截短为 advert。

note.en: The look-alike group is the word's own family; the near-meaning group gathers verbs for promoting, publicizing and pushing a product.
note.cn: 形近组是这个词自己的词族；近义组收表示推广、宣传与推销的动词。

entries.definition: The noun for a public notice that promotes something; formed from the verb with -ment.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「广告」，指推广某事物的公开告示，由本词加 -ment 构成。

entries.definition: The person or company that pays for an advertisement.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「广告主、登广告者」，由本词加 -er 构成。

entries.definition: The business or activity of promoting goods and services.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「广告业、广告活动」，由本词加 -ing 构成。

entries.definition: A British informal clipping of advertisement, not of the verb.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「广告」，是 advertisement 的英式口语截短形式，并非直接由动词截成。

entries.definition: To help sell or make popular a product or event, often through campaigns.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「推广、促销」，常通过活动让商品或活动更好卖、更受欢迎。

entries.definition: To make something widely known, whether or not it is for sale.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「宣传、公布」，只强调让公众知道，不一定是卖东西。

entries.definition: To plan how a product is sold and presented, a broader business activity than placing ads.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「营销、推销」，比投放广告范围更广，包含销售与呈现的整体规划。

entries.definition: To mention a product or show in order to help it, as a guest might on air.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「（在节目里）顺带宣传」，如嘉宾在播出中提及自己的作品。

entries.definition: To try hard to sell or praise something, often in a way people distrust.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「兜售、吹捧」，常带有令人不信任的意味。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the real Latin verb advertere and the older sense of informing, which the modern selling sense grew out of.
normalIntro.cn: 下面的记忆钩子使用真实的拉丁动词 advertere，以及现代「推销」义所由来的「告知」旧义。

normal.en: Advertere is 'to turn toward', so advertising turns a crowd's eyes toward a product.
normal.cn: advertere 是「使转向」，所以 advertising 就是把一群人的眼睛转向商品。

normal.en: The earliest English sense was simply 'to inform', and advertising still starts with making something known.
normal.cn: 英语最早的义项只是「告知」，而广告至今仍从「让人知道」开始。

normal.en: Advertisement came later from advertise with -ment, so the verb is the older English word.
normal.cn: advertisement 是后来由 advertise 加 -ment 构成的，所以动词才是更早的英语词。

normal.en: To advertise for a waiter is to hold up a notice that asks, not one that praises.
normal.cn: advertise for a waiter 举起的是一张「求人」的告示，而不是夸赞的告示。

normal.en: A careless remark can advertise your mistake, because the word means making something public, not only selling.
normal.cn: 一句不慎的话就能 advertise 你的错误，因为这个词的意思是「使公开」，不只是「卖东西」。

abstract.en: Picture a plate lifted above a crowd and turned slowly so that everyone can read it.
abstract.cn: 想象一块牌子被举到人群头顶，慢慢转动，让每个人都能读到。

abstract.en: Advertising does not make a thing better; it only makes it seen.
abstract.cn: 广告不会让东西变好，它只是让东西被看见。

abstract.en: The same raised sign can sell soap, ask for a worker, or expose a fault; only the message changes.
abstract.cn: 同一块举起的牌子可以卖肥皂、招工人，也可以暴露缺点，变的只是牌子上写的内容。

examples.en: The company advertised its new phone on television.
examples.cn: 公司在电视上为新手机会做广告。

examples.en: The bakery advertised for an assistant in its window.
examples.cn: 面包店在橱窗里登广告招一名帮手。

examples.en: The event was advertised as a family day.
examples.cn: 这场活动被宣传为家庭日。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「阿德外台兹」——阿德把牌子举过头顶，一圈人都抬头看：做广告。

root: 拉丁语 advertere「使转向」，由 ad-「朝向」+ vertere「转」构成；英语先有动词 advertise「使人注意、告知」，商业上的「做广告」义是后来从「公开告知」发展出来的。

sensesIntro.en: All six senses turn something toward an audience: a product, a vacancy, a request, a private fault, a conspicuous feature, or a chosen label.
sensesIntro.cn: 六个义项都是把某样东西转向受众：商品、职位空缺、请求、私下的过失、显眼的特征，或一个挑好的名目。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a sign is lifted above a crowd and turned so that every face follows it.
core.cn: 核心意象：一块牌子被举到人群上方并转动，每张脸都跟着转过去。

branches.en: THE MARKET: paid space and time turn an audience toward goods.
branches.cn: 市场线：付费买下的版面与时段把观众转向商品。

branches.en: THE NOTICE BOARD: a job or a request is posted where the right people will see it.
branches.cn: 告示牌线：职位或请求被贴到合适的人能看见的地方。

branches.en: THE PUBLIC CONFESSION: whatever is shown to the crowd can also expose the one who showed it.
branches.cn: 公开线：凡是展示给人群的东西，也可能反过来暴露展示它的人。

branches.en: THE SPOTLIGHT: a bright colour or mark draws the eye without any notice being bought.
branches.cn: 聚光线：鲜艳的颜色或标记不用花钱登告示就能把目光拉过来。

branches.en: THE LABEL: to advertise as is to choose the words in which the public will first see a thing.
branches.cn: 标签线：be advertised as 就是替公众挑好第一眼看到它时用的说法。

intro.en: Advertise joins the Latin prefix ad- to the turning verb vertere; English endings then build the whole advertising family.
intro.cn: advertise 把拉丁语前缀 ad- 与表示「转」的动词 vertere 结合在一起；英语词尾随后构成整个广告词族。

latinIntro.en: Latin vertere and advertere are recorded; the modern commercial sense has no Latin equivalent.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 vertere 与 advertere 都有记录；现代的商业义在拉丁语里并没有对应义项。

items.example: It joins vertere to form advertere.
items.exampleCN: 它与 vertere 结合构成 advertere。

items.example: The same root appears in convert and reverse.
items.exampleCN: 同一词根还出现在 convert 与 reverse 里。

items.example: The English verb comes from this form.
items.exampleCN: 英语的动词来自这个形式。

items.example: It carries the Latin verb into English as advertise.
items.exampleCN: 它把拉丁动词带入英语，成为 advertise。

items.example: It forms advertisement.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 advertisement。

items.meaning: a person or thing that does
items.example: It forms advertiser.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 advertiser。

items.meaning: an activity or an action in progress
items.meaningCN: 活动，或正在进行的动作
items.example: It forms advertising.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 advertising。

items.example: It forms advertised.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 advertised。

items.example: It forms advertises.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 advertises。

core_image: 报纸整版里被买下的那一小块，只放一张图和一句话
scene: 临街的橱窗整个换上了新一季的海报，路人纷纷停下脚步拍照。The new advertisement filled the whole shop window.
sceneCN: 这里 advertisement 指橱窗里那张付费的商业广告（第 1 个义项：广告）；句意为这张新广告占满了整个橱窗。

pos.zh: 名词：广告；广告宣传；公告、启事；活招牌

derivatives.zh: 由 advertisement 去掉名词后缀 -ment 所得的动词形式，义为「做广告；宣传」
