senses.title: A paid notice promoting something
senses.definition: a notice, picture, film, or online item that is paid for and used to promote a product, service, or event
senses.definitionCN: 为推广商品、服务或活动而付费发布的告示、图片、影片或网络内容
senses.example: The new advertisement filled the whole shop window.
senses.exampleCN: 这张新广告占满了整个橱窗。
senses.why: The word is built on advertise, which means turning attention toward something; the notice is the paid means of making that turn happen.
senses.whyCN: 这个词建立在 advertise 之上，意思是把注意力转向某物；广告就是让这次「转过去」发生的付费手段。

senses.title: The act of advertising
senses.definition: the activity or business of making goods known to the public, used as an uncountable noun in formal writing
senses.definitionCN: 让公众知道商品的这一活动或行业，在正式书面语中作不可数名词
senses.example: The advertisement of tobacco is now tightly controlled.
senses.exampleCN: 如今烟草广告受到严格管控。
senses.why: The noun can name the whole activity, not just one item: the -ment ending also carries the sense of an action or its result.
senses.whyCN: 这个名词也能指整个活动，而不只是一则东西：-ment 词尾本来就同时表示动作与其结果。

senses.title: A public notice or announcement
senses.definition: a formal public notice giving information, such as a legal announcement or a notice in a newspaper
senses.definitionCN: 提供信息的正式公开告示，如法律公告或报纸上的启事
senses.example: The court placed an advertisement of the hearing in the local paper.
senses.exampleCN: 法院在本地报纸上刊登了开庭公告。
senses.why: Before the word meant selling, it meant making something publicly known, and that older sense survives in official notices.
senses.whyCN: 在表示「卖东西」之前，这个词表示「让公众知道」；这一旧义仍活在官方告示里。

senses.title: Something that openly shows a quality
senses.definition: in phrases such as be no advertisement for, a person or thing that publicly shows the good or bad qualities of something
senses.definitionCN: 用于 be no advertisement for 等短语，指公开显示某事物好坏品质的人或物
senses.example: That shabby waiting room is no advertisement for the clinic.
senses.exampleCN: 那间破旧的候诊室可给这家诊所做不了好招牌。
senses.why: Anything that puts a quality on public view is doing what an advertisement does, without being paid or printed.
senses.whyCN: 凡是把某种品质摆到公众眼前的东西，都在做广告所做的事，只是没有付费、也没有印出来。

intro.en: Advertisement is an English noun formed from the verb advertise plus -ment; the selling sense came later than the sense of public notice.
intro.cn: advertisement 是由动词 advertise 加 -ment 构成的英语名词；卖东西的义项晚于「公开告示」的义项。

items.en: Ad 'to, toward' plus vertere 'to turn' formed advertere, 'to turn toward'.
items.cn: ad「朝向」加 vertere「转」构成 advertere，意为「使转向」。

items.en: Later Latin also used the verb for turning the mind to something, that is, noticing or paying attention.
items.cn: 后期拉丁语也用这个动词表示把心思转向某事，即注意到、留意。

items.en: The verb advertise entered English meaning 'to inform' and 'to turn one's attention'; the noun was not yet established.
items.cn: 动词 advertise 进入英语时意为「告知」与「把注意力转向」；名词当时尚未确立。

items.en: Advertise plus the noun suffix -ment gave advertisement, first for the act of giving public notice and then for the notice itself.
items.cn: advertise 加名词后缀 -ment 构成 advertisement，先指发布公告这一行为，后指公告本身。

items.en: With the growth of newspapers and consumer goods, the commercial sense became dominant; British speech later clipped the word to advert.
items.cn: 随着报纸与消费品的发展，商业义成为主流；英式口语后来把这个词截短为 advert。

note.en: The look-alike group is the word's own family; the near-meaning group gathers other kinds of public notice and publicity.
note.cn: 形近组是这个词自己的词族；近义组收其他类型的公开告示与宣传用语。

entries.definition: The verb from which the noun is formed, meaning to make something known publicly.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「做广告；宣传」，本词正是在它后面加 -ment 构成的。

entries.definition: The person or company that pays for advertising.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「广告主、登广告者」，由 advertise 加 -er 构成。

entries.definition: The industry or activity that produces and places ads.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「广告业、广告活动」，由 advertise 加 -ing 构成。

entries.definition: A British informal clipping of this same noun, much shorter in speech.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「广告」，是本词的英式口语截短形式，口语中短得多。

entries.definition: The shortest everyday word for an advertisement, used in speech and headlines.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「广告」，是最短的日常说法，多用于口语与标题。

entries.definition: A broadcast advertisement, especially one shown on television or radio.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「电视或广播广告」，特指播出的一段推销短片。

entries.definition: A public statement of information, with no selling purpose.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「公告、通知」，只提供信息，没有推销目的。

entries.definition: A sign or sheet giving information or a warning.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「告示、通知」，指提供信息或警告的牌子或纸张。

entries.definition: Attention given to someone or something by the media, whether paid for or not.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「公众关注、宣传」，指媒体给予的关注，付费与否都算。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the real structure of advertise plus -ment and the word's older sense of public notice.
normalIntro.cn: 下面的记忆钩子使用 advertise 加 -ment 的真实结构，以及这个词更早的「公开告示」义。

normal.en: Advertere is 'to turn toward', so an advertisement turns a reader's eyes toward a seller.
normal.cn: advertere 是「使转向」，所以 advertisement 就是把读者的眼睛转向卖家。

normal.en: The -ment ending turns the act of advertising into a thing you can hold: a page, a poster, a clip.
normal.cn: -ment 词尾把「做广告」这个动作变成能拿在手里的东西：一页纸、一张海报、一段片子。

normal.en: The word first meant a public notice, not a sales pitch, and that older sense survives in official announcements.
normal.cn: 这个词最早指公开告示，而不是推销话术；这一旧义仍活在官方公告里。

normal.en: Be no advertisement for means the thing itself shows the bad side of what it belongs to.
normal.cn: be no advertisement for 指某物本身就暴露出它所属之物的坏的一面。

normal.en: British speech cuts the long noun to advert, which is why the two words differ so much in length.
normal.cn: 英式口语把这个长名词砍成 advert，所以这两个词的长度差得这么远。

abstract.en: Picture one square of a newspaper page that has been bought and filled with a single bright picture.
abstract.cn: 想象报纸一整版里被买下的那一小方块，里面只放一张鲜亮的图。

abstract.en: An advertisement is a paid turn of the head: someone bought the moment your eyes moved.
abstract.cn: 广告是一次付费的转头：有人买下了你目光移动的那一瞬。

abstract.en: The same page can sell, announce or warn; money buys the attention, not the belief.
abstract.cn: 同一页纸可以卖货、可以公告、也可以警告；钱买到的是注意力，不是信任。

examples.en: The new advertisement filled the whole shop window.
examples.cn: 这张新广告占满了整个橱窗。

examples.en: The advertisement of tobacco is now tightly controlled.
examples.cn: 如今烟草广告受到严格管控。

examples.en: That shabby waiting room is no advertisement for the clinic.
examples.cn: 那间破旧的候诊室可给这家诊所做不了好招牌。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「阿德沃提斯门特」——阿德买下整页纸，只写一行字：广告。

root: 由动词 advertise 加名词后缀 -ment 构成；advertise 出自拉丁语 advertere「使转向」，所以本词本义是「使人注意的告知」，后来才专指付费的商业广告。

sensesIntro.en: Four senses: a paid notice, the act of advertising, an official public notice, and a person or thing that openly displays a quality.
sensesIntro.cn: 四个义项：付费的广告；广告宣传这一行为；正式的公开告示；公开显示某种品质的人或物。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one bought square on a crowded page, holding a single picture and a single line.
core.cn: 核心意象：拥挤版面上被买下的那一方块，只放一张图、一行字。

branches.en: THE PAGE: a printed space is bought and filled with a seller's message.
branches.cn: 纸面线：买下印刷版面，填上卖家的信息。

branches.en: THE SCREEN: the same bought attention is delivered as a short film or an online item.
branches.cn: 屏幕线：同样买来的注意力，以短片或网络内容的形式送出。

branches.en: THE ACT: the noun also names the whole business of advertising, not one item.
branches.cn: 行为线：这个名词也能指整个广告活动，而不只是一则内容。

branches.en: THE NOTICE: the older sense of making something publicly known survives in formal announcements.
branches.cn: 告示线：让公众知道的旧义，保存在正式的公告里。

branches.en: THE EXAMPLE: anything that openly shows a quality is doing the word's work without being paid.
branches.cn: 例证线：任何公开显示品质的东西，不收费也在做这个词所做的事。

intro.en: Advertisement is advertise plus -ment, and advertise in turn rests on the Latin prefix ad- and the verb vertere.
intro.cn: advertisement 是 advertise 加 -ment；而 advertise 又建立在拉丁语前缀 ad- 与动词 vertere 之上。

latinIntro.en: Latin vertere and advertere are recorded; -ment goes back to Latin -mentum through French.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 vertere 与 advertere 都有记录；-ment 经法语上溯到拉丁语 -mentum。

items.example: It joins vertere to form advertere.
items.exampleCN: 它与 vertere 结合构成 advertere。

items.example: The same root appears in convert and reverse.
items.exampleCN: 同一词根还出现在 convert 与 reverse 里。

items.example: It is the source of the English verb advertise.
items.exampleCN: 它是英语动词 advertise 的来源。

items.example: The noun adds -ment to this verb.
items.exampleCN: 名词就是在这个动词后加 -ment。

items.example: It forms advertisement.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 advertisement。

items.meaning: a person or thing that does
items.example: It forms advertiser.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 advertiser。

items.meaning: an activity or an action in progress
items.meaningCN: 活动，或正在进行的动作
items.example: It forms advertising.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 advertising。

items.example: It forms advertised.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 advertised。

items.example: It forms advertisements.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 advertisements。

derivatives.zh: 与本词同根的动词，义为「做广告；宣传」
由 advertise 加表施动者的后缀 -er 构成，义为「广告主」
由 advertise 加 -ing 构成，义为「广告业；广告活动」

definition_zh: 建议；忠告；意见；正式通知；（旧）消息
definition_en: an opinion or suggestion offered to someone about what they should do, or a formal notice in business
core_image: 一张递到面前的纸条，上面写着下一步该往哪走
scene: 年轻的店员站在柜台后，账本摊开，老板在旁边压低声音交代。She took her lawyer's advice and refused to sign the contract.
sceneCN: 这里 advice 指律师给出的专业意见（第 3 个义项：律师、医生等专业人士给出的意见）；句意为她听从律师的意见，拒绝签署那份合同。

pos.zh: 名词：建议；忠告；意见；正式通知；消息

forms.label: 复数（罕用，多见于商业用语）

derivatives.zh: 由同源动词 advise 加后缀 -able 构成，义为「明智的；可取的」
由 advisable 加名词后缀 -ity 构成，义为「可取性；明智」
由同源动词 advise 加后缀 -ory 构成，义为「顾问的；咨询的」

senses.title: An opinion about what to do
senses.definition: an opinion or suggestion offered to someone about what they should do in a situation
senses.definitionCN: 就某人该如何行动提出的看法或建议
senses.example: My advice is to wait until the roads are clear.
senses.exampleCN: 我的建议是等道路畅通了再走。
senses.why: Old French avis meant a view or opinion, so advice is literally the view you set before another person so that they can see their way.
senses.whyCN: 古法语 avis 意为「看法、意见」：advice 就是被摆到对方面前、让他看清路该怎么走的那份看法。

senses.title: Warning counsel about conduct
senses.definition: a warning or piece of moral guidance, often given because the speaker expects trouble if it is ignored
senses.definitionCN: 带有告诫意味的劝导，通常因为说话人认为不听就会出问题
senses.example: His father's advice kept him out of the fight.
senses.exampleCN: 父亲的忠告让他没有卷入那场斗殴。
senses.why: The same view can turn from information into warning: when the speaker sees danger ahead, the opinion takes on the weight of a caution.
senses.whyCN: 同一份「看法」可以从信息变成警告：当说话人看见前方有危险，这份意见就带上了告诫的分量。

senses.title: Professional counsel
senses.definition: the formal opinion of a lawyer, doctor, accountant or other expert on a matter in their own field
senses.definitionCN: 律师、医生、会计师等专家就本领域事务给出的正式意见
senses.example: She took her lawyer's advice and refused to sign the contract.
senses.exampleCN: 她听从律师的意见，拒绝签署那份合同。
senses.why: This view is no longer casual: the expert has looked closely at the case, so the opinion carries authority and often a professional duty behind it.
senses.whyCN: 这份「看法」不再是随口一说：专家仔细看过案情，意见因此带着权威，背后往往还有职业责任。

senses.title: A formal business notice
senses.definition: a formal written notice in commerce or banking, such as a letter telling a customer that a bill has been drawn or goods shipped
senses.definitionCN: 商业或银行业务中的正式书面通知，如告知客户已开出票据或已发运货物
senses.example: The bank sent a letter of advice confirming the transfer.
senses.exampleCN: 银行寄来一份通知函，确认了这笔转账。
senses.why: In trade the opinion hardens into a statement of fact sent to the other party, and English keeps the old word for this administrative notice.
senses.whyCN: 在贸易往来中，「看法」固化成了发给对方的既成事实说明；英语为这类事务性通知保留了原来的词。

senses.title: News or intelligence, in older use
senses.definition: news or information, especially in the old plural form advices as used in earlier letters and dispatches
senses.definitionCN: 消息、情报，尤见于旧时的复数形式 advices，用在早期书信与公文里
senses.example: The merchant waited for advices from his agents abroad.
senses.exampleCN: 那位商人等着海外代理传来的消息。
senses.why: A view of events sent from a distance is information, and this older sense still keeps the act of seeing behind the noun.
senses.whyCN: 把远方的情况「看」下来再送回来就是消息；这个旧义仍保留着名词背后那个「看」的动作。

intro.en: Advice and advise are a matched pair from Old French, and both rest on a Latin verb of seeing.
intro.cn: advice 与 advise 是由古法语带入英语的一对词，二者都建立在拉丁语表示「看」的动词上。

items.en: *weid- is generally reconstructed as 'to see, to know'; Latin videre descends from it, and the deeper history of the root is source uncertain.
items.cn: 一般认为原始印欧语 *weid- 意为「看见、知道」，拉丁语 videre 由它而来；这个更早词根的历史来源不确定。

items.en: The verb videre meant 'to see', and its participle visum meant 'what is seen, a sight'; the notion of a view or opinion grows out of the act of looking.
items.cn: 动词 videre 意为「看见」，其分词 visum 意为「所见之物、景象」；「看法、意见」的观念正是从「看」这个动作长出来的。

items.en: Old French avis meant 'opinion, view, judgement' and also 'advice'. It is generally explained as Latin ad plus videre or visum, though a Germanic source has also been suggested and the question is not fully settled.
items.cn: 古法语 avis 意为「看法、意见、判断」，也表示「劝告」。一般认为它出自拉丁语 ad 加 videre 或 visum，也有日耳曼语来源的假说，尚无定论。

items.en: English borrowed the noun first as avis and later as advice, while the related verb aviser became advise. The c and s spellings were fixed by printers in the sixteenth century.
items.cn: 英语先借入 avis，后作 advice；相关动词 aviser 变成 advise。c 与 s 两种拼写在十六世纪由印刷商固定下来。

items.en: The noun kept the voiceless /s/ and the verb the voiced /z/, so advice and advise are now told apart by sound as well as by spelling; commerce added the notice sense.
items.cn: 名词保留清音 /s/，动词保留浊音 /z/，advice 与 advise 如今靠读音和拼写双重区分；商业领域又添出「通知」一义。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words from the same French and Latin stock, including the verb that is often mistaken for a variant spelling; the near-meaning group gathers other words for an opinion offered to someone.
note.cn: 形近组收同一法语、拉丁来源的词，其中包括常被误当成异体拼写的动词；近义组收其他表示「向人提出的意见」的词。

entries.definition: The verb meaning to tell someone what you think they should do; it is a different word class, not another spelling of the noun.
entries.definitionCN: 同源动词，义为「建议、劝告」；它是动词，并非名词 advice 的另一种拼写，两者读音也不同。

entries.definition: An adjective meaning wise or sensible to do.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「明智的、可取的」，由动词 advise 加后缀 -able 构成。

entries.definition: An adjective or noun meaning giving advice or having the role of an adviser.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词或名词，义为「顾问的、咨询的」或「咨询机构」。

entries.definition: A piece of equipment made for a particular purpose; it only looks similar and comes from a different root.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「装置、设备」；只是拼写相近，词源不同，来自拉丁语 dividere「分开」一系。

entries.definition: An idea or plan put forward for others to consider; lighter and less directive than advice.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「提议、建议」，语气比 advice 轻，指导性也更弱。

entries.definition: A suggestion that something is good or should be chosen, often based on experience.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「推荐、建议」，常基于经验，含有「值得选用」的判断。

entries.definition: Formal advice, especially on a serious matter; it can also mean the lawyer who gives it.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「忠告、法律意见」，语气正式，多指重大事务上的意见，也可指提供意见的律师。

entries.definition: Help and direction given over time, rather than a single opinion.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「指导、引导」，指持续的帮助与方向，而不是一条单独的意见。

normalIntro.en: These hooks work with the real French and Latin history and with the phrases this noun actually appears in.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些记忆钩子依据真实的法语、拉丁语源流，以及这个词实际出现的常见搭配。

normal.en: avis is a view: advice is the view handed over to someone else.
normal.cn: avis 是「看法」：advice 就是递给别人的那份看法。

normal.en: The noun ends in c, as in a piece of advice; the verb ends in s, as in advise.
normal.cn: 名词以 c 结尾，如 a piece of advice；动词以 s 结尾，如 advise。

normal.en: Advice is uncountable: you give a piece of advice, not an advice.
normal.cn: advice 不可数：要说 a piece of advice，不说 an advice。

normal.en: Lawyers and doctors give advice in the professional sense, which is why legal advice is a fixed phrase.
normal.cn: 律师和医生给的是专业意义上的 advice，所以 legal advice 成了固定说法。

normal.en: In old letters, advices meant news sent from a distance.
normal.cn: 在旧时书信里，advices 指从远方送来的消息。

abstract.en: Picture a folded note pressed into your hand: the note is not the journey, only the direction.
abstract.cn: 想象一张折好的纸条被塞进你手里：纸条不是旅程本身，只是方向。

abstract.en: Advice stands outside you and can be taken or left, which is why the word never forces the act.
abstract.cn: 建议站在你之外，可以采纳也可以不采纳，所以这个词从不强迫行动。

abstract.en: Two people, one map: the one who has seen the road points at it, and that pointing is advice.
abstract.cn: 两个人一张地图：见过路的人伸手一指，这一指就是建议。

examples.en: She gave me some useful advice about the interview.
examples.cn: 她就面试给了我一些有用的建议。

examples.en: On his doctor's advice, he stopped running for a month.
examples.cn: 遵照医生的建议，他停跑了一个月。

examples.en: The firm sent advices to all its overseas agents.
examples.cn: 公司向所有海外代理发出了通知。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「阿德外斯」——阿德把一张纸条塞到你手里，上面只写了一句该怎么办：建议、忠告。

root: 古法语 avis「看法、意见」，一般认为出自拉丁语 ad「朝向」+ videre「看」（经 visum「所见之物」），另有日耳曼语来源的假说；英语中名词作 advice，动词作 advise。

sensesIntro.en: The five senses all turn on one image: a view of the situation is put in front of someone, whether as a suggestion, a warning, expert opinion, a business notice, or distant news.
sensesIntro.cn: 五个义项都围绕一个意象：把对局势的看法摆到别人面前，只是摆法不同——建议、告诫、专家意见、商业通知，或远方传来的消息。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a folded note is placed in someone's hand, showing which way to go.
core.cn: 核心意象：一张折好的纸条被放进对方手里，上面写着该往哪走。

branches.en: THE EVERYDAY NOTE: a plain opinion about what to do next.
branches.cn: 日常纸条线：一条关于下一步该怎么做的朴素意见。

branches.en: THE WARNING: the same view sharpened into caution about conduct.
branches.cn: 告诫线：同一份看法收紧成对行为的警告。

branches.en: THE EXPERT: close looking gives the opinion authority and professional weight.
branches.cn: 专家线：看得仔细，意见才有权威与职业分量。

branches.en: THE LEDGER: in trade the opinion hardens into a formal notice.
branches.cn: 账册线：在贸易中，意见固化成了正式通知。

branches.en: THE DISTANT REPORT: what was seen elsewhere travels back as news.
branches.cn: 远方线：在别处看到的情况传回来，就成了消息。

intro.en: Advice is an Old French noun built on a Latin verb of seeing; English added suffixes to make the adjective and noun family.
intro.cn: advice 是建立在拉丁语「看」这一动词上的古法语名词；英语再加后缀，构成形容词与名词一族。

latinIntro.en: Latin videre and visum are recorded, and ad is a common preposition; Old French avis itself is recorded, while its exact derivation is still debated.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 videre 与 visum 均有文献记录，ad 是常见介词；古法语 avis 本身也有记录，但它确切的构成方式仍有争论。

items.example: It points the act of seeing towards an object.
items.exampleCN: 它把「看」这个动作指向某个对象。

items.example: It is the seeing verb behind the family.
items.exampleCN: 它是这一词族背后表示「看见」的动词。

items.example: The noun of sight is the bridge to the sense of opinion.
items.exampleCN: 表示「所见」的名词，是把「看」引向「意见」的桥梁。

items.example: English borrowed avis before the spelling settled as advice.
items.exampleCN: 英语先借入 avis，后来拼写才固定为 advice。

items.meaning: to consider, to give an opinion
items.example: This verb became the English advise.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词变成了英语的 advise。

items.example: It forms advisable.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 advisable。

items.example: It forms advisability.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 advisability。

items.example: It forms advisory.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 advisory。

items.example: It forms advised, as in the phrase be advised that.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 advised，见于 be advised that 这类说法。

derivatives.zh: 由同源动词 advise 加后缀 -able 构成，义为「明智的；可取的」
由 advisable 加名词后缀 -ity 构成，义为「可取性；明智」
由同源动词 advise 加后缀 -ory 构成，义为「顾问的；咨询的」

definition_zh: 建议；劝告；通知；提供咨询
definition_en: to tell someone what you think they should do, to warn them, to inform them formally, or to act as their adviser
core_image: 一个人把手按在地图上，替另一个人指出该走的那条路
scene: 深夜的电话里，朋友的声音有些发抖，说想连夜开车回去。I advised him to wait until morning.
sceneCN: 这里 advise 指劝对方采取某个做法（第 1 个义项：建议某人做某事）；句意为「我劝他等到早上再走」。

pos.zh: 动词：建议；劝告；通知；提供咨询

derivatives.zh: 由同一法语来源分出的名词形式，义为「建议；忠告」，拼写以 c 结尾
由本词加后缀 -ory 构成，义为「顾问的；咨询的」
由本词加后缀 -able 构成，义为「明智的；可取的」
由本词加名词后缀 -ment 构成，义为「考虑；商议」，多见于美式正式用语

senses.title: To suggest a course of action
senses.definition: to tell someone what you think they should do in a particular situation
senses.definitionCN: 就某一具体情形告诉对方你认为他该怎么做
senses.example: The nurse advised him to drink more water.
senses.exampleCN: 护士建议他多喝水。
senses.why: Old French aviser meant to consider and form a view; advising is handing that considered view to the person who must act.
senses.whyCN: 古法语 aviser 意为「思量并形成看法」；advise 就是把这份思量过的看法交给要行动的那个人。

senses.title: To warn or urge against something
senses.definition: to warn someone strongly, especially to urge them not to do something
senses.definitionCN: 郑重告诫某人，尤指力劝其不要做某事
senses.example: The doctor advised against any strenuous exercise for a month.
senses.exampleCN: 医生劝他一个月内不要做任何剧烈运动。
senses.why: When the view sees risk, the same act turns into a warning: the speaker stops offering options and pushes one way.
senses.whyCN: 当这份看法看见了风险，同一个动作就变成告诫：说话人不再提供选项，而是往一个方向推。

senses.title: To inform formally
senses.definition: to inform someone officially, especially in business or legal writing
senses.definitionCN: 正式告知某人，尤用于商业或法律文书
senses.example: Passengers are advised that the ferry will not sail tonight.
senses.exampleCN: 特此通知乘客，今晚渡轮不开航。
senses.why: A business letter does not ask what to do; it states what is, yet English still uses the verb of giving a view and softens it into a notice.
senses.whyCN: 商业信函并不是在问该怎么做，而是在陈述既成事实；英语仍用这个「给出看法」的动词，只把语气软化成通知。

senses.title: To act as a professional adviser
senses.definition: to give expert guidance to a person or organization over a period, as a lawyer, doctor or consultant does
senses.definitionCN: 像律师、医生或顾问那样，在一段时间内为个人或机构提供专业指导
senses.example: She advises several small firms on tax matters.
senses.exampleCN: 她为几家小公司提供税务方面的咨询。
senses.why: One act of giving a view can grow into a continuing role: the adviser keeps looking at the client's case and keeps advising.
senses.whyCN: 给出一次看法的动作可以长成持续的角色：顾问不断查看客户的情况，也不断提出意见。

intro.en: The verb and the noun advice share one Old French root, but English split them by spelling and by the sound of the final consonant.
intro.cn: 动词 advise 与名词 advice 共用一个古法语词根，但英语用拼写和词尾辅音的读音把它们分开了。

items.en: *weid- is generally reconstructed as 'to see, to know', and Latin videre is one of its descendants; the deeper origin is source uncertain.
items.cn: 一般认为原始印欧语 *weid- 意为「看见、知道」，拉丁语 videre 是它的后代之一；更早的来源不确定。

items.en: The elements ad 'to, towards' and videre 'to see' lie behind the French word, though Latin itself preferred consulere and monere for advising, so the exact path is not certain.
items.cn: ad「朝向」与 videre「看见」这两个成分构成了法语词的底子；不过拉丁语表示「劝告」更常用 consulere 与 monere，因此确切路径并不确定。

items.en: The verb aviser meant to consider, take note and give an opinion, and it is the direct source of the English verb.
items.cn: 动词 aviser 意为「思量、留意并提出看法」，是英语这个动词的直接来源。

items.en: English borrowed it as avisen and later advise; the noun advice came from the same French stock but kept a different ending.
items.cn: 英语先借作 avisen，后作 advise；名词 advice 出自同一法语来源，却保留了不同的词尾。

items.en: The verb took the voiced /z/ and the noun the voiceless /s/, and the 'inform' sense grew out of commercial correspondence.
items.cn: 动词取浊音 /z/，名词取清音 /s/；「告知」这一义项则从商业往来书信中发展出来。

note.en: The look-alike group holds the noun and the personal noun from the same root, plus one word that only sounds similar; the near-meaning group holds verbs of putting an idea, a warning or information before someone.
note.cn: 形近组收同一词根的名词与人称名词，另加一个只是读音相近的词；近义组收把想法、警告或信息摆到对方面前的动词。

entries.definition: The noun meaning an opinion about what to do; it ends in c and is pronounced with a voiceless /s/.
entries.definitionCN: 同源名词，义为「建议、忠告」，以 c 结尾，词尾读清音 /s/；名词与动词不能互换。

entries.definition: The person whose role is to give advice; formed from the verb with the agent suffix -er.
entries.definitionCN: 同源人称名词，义为「顾问」，由动词加施事后缀 -er 构成。

entries.definition: An adjective or noun meaning giving advice or serving as a body that advises.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词或名词，义为「顾问的、咨询的」，或指提供咨询的机构。

entries.definition: To invent or plan something; it sounds close to advise but comes from a different root.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「设计、想出」；与 advise 读音接近、拼写相近，但只是形近音近，词源不同，来自拉丁语 dividere「分开」一系。

entries.definition: To put an idea forward for consideration; weaker and less personal than advise.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「提议、暗示」，语气比 advise 弱，也不那么像在替对方拿主意。

entries.definition: To say that something is good and should be chosen; it implies approval of the thing.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「推荐、建议」，含有「这样东西好、值得选」的判断。

entries.definition: To give formal advice, especially on a serious personal or legal matter.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「忠告、提供法律意见」，语气正式，多用于严肃的个人或法律事务。

entries.definition: To tell someone about a danger or problem so that they can avoid it; it focuses on the risk.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「警告、提醒」，重点在危险本身，而不在替对方规划做法。

entries.definition: To give someone facts; it carries no element of recommendation.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「告知、通知」，只提供事实，不含建议或劝告的成分。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the real French verb aviser, the noun-verb spelling pair, and the sentence patterns the verb actually takes.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些记忆钩子依据真实的法语动词 aviser、名词与动词的拼写配对，以及这个动词实际使用的句型。

normal.en: aviser is to consider and give a view; advise is what you do with that view.
normal.cn: aviser 是「思量并给出看法」；advise 就是把这份看法说出去。

normal.en: The verb ends in s and says /z/; the noun ends in c and says /s/.
normal.cn: 动词以 s 结尾、读 /z/；名词以 c 结尾、读 /s/。

normal.en: The two frames are advise someone to do something and advise against doing it.
normal.cn: 两个基本句型是 advise someone to do something 和 advise against doing it。

normal.en: Be advised that is the fixed frame of a formal notice.
normal.cn: be advised that 是正式通知的固定句式。

normal.en: An adviser does it as a job, and an advisory body does it as an institution.
normal.cn: adviser 以此为职业，advisory body 则以机构身份提供意见。

abstract.en: Picture a hand pressed on a map, one finger tracing the road the other person should take.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手按在地图上，一根手指沿着对方该走的那条路划过去。

abstract.en: Advising is not ordering: the finger can be ignored, and the road still belongs to the traveller.
abstract.cn: 劝告不是命令：那根手指可以被无视，路仍然属于走路的人。

abstract.en: The same finger can point at a danger, at a better route, or at a form to sign; only the tone changes.
abstract.cn: 同一根手指可以指向危险、指向更好的路线，或指向一份要签的文件；变的只是语气。

examples.en: The doctor advised her to rest for a week.
examples.cn: 医生建议她休息一周。

examples.en: I would advise against lending him the car.
examples.cn: 我劝你不要把车借给他。

examples.en: Please be advised that the office closes at noon.
examples.cn: 特此通知，办公室中午关门。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「阿德外兹」——阿德凑过来压低声音，替你拿了个主意：建议、劝告。

root: 古法语动词 aviser「思量、提出看法」，一般认为其词根出自拉丁语 ad「朝向」+ videre「看」；英语名词作 advice、动词作 advise，词尾一清一浊。

sensesIntro.en: The four senses all come from one act: a considered view is placed before another person, whether as a suggestion, a warning, an official notice, or a continuing professional role.
sensesIntro.cn: 四个义项都出自同一个动作：把思量过的看法摆到别人面前，只是身份不同——建议、告诫、正式通知，或持续的专业顾问角色。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a hand on a map, one finger showing another person which road to take.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只手按在地图上，一根手指替对方指出该走哪条路。

branches.en: THE SUGGESTION: a view about the next step is offered plainly.
branches.cn: 建议线：把关于下一步的看法平实地提出来。

branches.en: THE WARNING: the same view sees risk and presses against one course of action.
branches.cn: 告诫线：同一份看法看见风险，于是压向某一个做法、劝人避开。

branches.en: THE NOTICE: in official writing the view turns into information the reader must know.
branches.cn: 通知线：在正式文书里，看法变成读者必须知道的信息。

branches.en: THE ROLE: repeated advising becomes a profession with clients and cases.
branches.cn: 角色线：反复提出意见，就成了一份面对客户与案子的职业。

branches.en: ONE ACT, TWO REACHES: the same offering of a view happens once in a conversation or continues for years.
branches.cn: 同一动作，两种跨度：给出看法的动作可以只发生在一句话里，也可以持续多年。

intro.en: Advise is an Old French verb brought into English; the agent, adjective and noun suffixes then built its family.
intro.cn: advise 是借入英语的古法语动词；施事后缀、形容词后缀与名词后缀随后撑起了它的词族。

latinIntro.en: Latin videre, visum and the preposition ad are recorded; Old French aviser is also recorded, and only the remoter Indo-European root is reconstructed.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 videre、visum 与介词 ad 均有记录，古法语 aviser 也有记录，只有更早的印欧词根属于重构形式。

definition_zh: 顾问；指导者；导师（亦拼作 advisor）
definition_en: a person whose job is to give expert advice, or someone who guides another person's studies or decisions
core_image: 一个人站在你侧后方半步，看着同一份文件替你圈出重点
scene: 学生把选课表摊在桌上，几门课的时间撞在一起，家长也拿不定主意。Her academic adviser helped her rearrange the timetable.
sceneCN: 这里 adviser 指学校里负责指导学生学业的老师（第 2 个义项：学业导师）；句意为她的学业导师帮她重新排了课表。

pos.zh: 名词：顾问；指导者；导师

forms.label: 异体拼写 advisor 的复数

derivatives.zh: 由同源动词 advise 加后缀 -ory 构成，义为「顾问的；咨询的」
由本词加名词后缀 -ship 构成，义为「顾问职位；顾问身份」

senses.title: A professional consultant
senses.definition: a person whose job is to give expert advice to a company, a government or an individual
senses.definitionCN: 以向公司、政府或个人提供专业意见为职业的人
senses.example: The firm hired an adviser to review its energy costs.
senses.exampleCN: 这家公司聘请了一位顾问来审查能源开支。
senses.why: The French verb aviser means to form a view, and the agent suffix -er names the person who does it as a job, so an adviser is the one paid to look and judge.
senses.whyCN: 法语动词 aviser 意为「形成看法」，施事后缀 -er 指以这件事为业的人，所以 adviser 是受雇去看、去判断的那个人。

senses.title: An academic guide
senses.definition: a teacher at a school or university who helps a student choose courses and plan their studies
senses.definitionCN: 学校里帮助学生选课、规划学业的老师
senses.example: Her academic adviser suggested dropping one of the two science courses.
senses.exampleCN: 她的学业导师建议她退掉两门理科课中的一门。
senses.why: In a university the same role narrows to study: the person looks at a student's path and points out the next step.
senses.whyCN: 在大学里，同一个角色缩小到学业上：这个人看着学生的路径，指出下一步该往哪走。

senses.title: Anyone who offers advice
senses.definition: a person, often trusted or senior, who gives another person advice without holding a formal post
senses.definitionCN: 不担任正式职务、却为他人出主意的人，往往是受信任者或长辈
senses.example: Throughout the crisis he remained her closest adviser.
senses.exampleCN: 整个危机期间，他始终是她最亲近的谋士。
senses.why: No job title is needed: whoever is looked to for a view becomes an adviser for that moment.
senses.whyCN: 不需要任何头衔：谁被当成可以拿主意的人，谁在那个时刻就是 adviser。

intro.en: Adviser is the agent noun of the French verb that also gave English advise, and its two spellings reflect two different endings.
intro.cn: adviser 是那个同时带来英语 advise 的法语动词的施事名词，它的两种拼写来自两个不同的词尾。

items.en: Latin videre 'to see' and its participle visum 'what is seen' lie behind the French word; the combination with ad is generally assumed, though the exact derivation is not certain.
items.cn: 拉丁语 videre「看见」及其分词 visum「所见之物」是法语词的底子；与 ad 的结合一般认为成立，但确切构成并不确定。

items.en: The verb aviser meant to consider and to give an opinion, and from it English took both the verb advise and the idea of the person who advises.
items.cn: 动词 aviser 意为「思量、提出看法」，英语由它既取来动词 advise，也取来「提出看法的人」这一概念。

items.en: English added the native agent suffix -er to the borrowed verb, giving adviser for the person who gives the view.
items.cn: 英语给借来的动词加上本土施事后缀 -er，得到 adviser，指提出看法的人。

items.en: A second spelling, advisor, was formed with the Latin-looking ending -or. Both forms have been in use since the sixteenth century and mean exactly the same thing.
items.cn: 另一种拼写 advisor 用看起来像拉丁语的词尾 -or 构成。两种形式自十六世纪起并用，含义完全相同。

items.en: Adviser is the usual form in British edited prose, while advisor is common in American job titles and organization names; dictionaries treat them as variants, not as different words.
items.cn: 在英国编辑体例中 adviser 更常见，而 advisor 多用于美式职位头衔与机构名称；词典把二者视为异体拼写，而非两个不同的词。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the variant spelling and the words built on the same verb; the near-meaning group gathers other people who give guidance, with different degrees of formality.
note.cn: 形近组收异体拼写与同一动词构成的词；近义组收其他提供指导的人，正式程度各不相同。

entries.definition: The same noun spelled with the Latin-looking ending -or, common in job titles and organization names.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，adviser 的另一种拼写，词尾用看起来像拉丁语的 -or，多见于职位头衔与机构名称，读音和含义完全相同。

entries.definition: The verb meaning to give someone advice; the person who does this is the adviser.
entries.definitionCN: 同源动词，义为「建议、劝告」；执行这个动作的人就是 adviser。

entries.definition: An adjective meaning having the role of giving advice, or a noun for a body that does so.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「顾问的、咨询的」；作名词时指提供咨询的机构。

entries.definition: The noun for the opinion itself, ending in c and pronounced with /s/.
entries.definitionCN: 同源名词，指意见本身，以 c 结尾、读清音 /s/，与指人的 adviser 分工不同。

entries.definition: An expert who is paid by a company to advise on a particular field.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「咨询顾问」，指受公司聘请、就某一领域提供意见的专家，职业色彩比 adviser 更强。

entries.definition: A formal word for a legal adviser or for the advice itself.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「法律顾问」或「忠告」，语气正式，法律色彩明显。

entries.definition: An experienced person who guides someone over a long period, usually in work or life rather than in one case.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「导师、引路人」，指长期指导他人的人，多在工作或人生层面，而非处理单个案子。

entries.definition: A person who shows the way, literally or figuratively; broader and less technical than adviser.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「向导、指导者」，可实指带路的人，也可比喻，范围比 adviser 宽，专业色彩更弱。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the real French verb, the agent suffix, and the phrases in which this person noun appears.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些记忆钩子依据真实的法语动词、施事后缀，以及这个指人的名词实际出现的搭配。

normal.en: advise plus -er gives the person who gives the view.
normal.cn: advise 加 -er，就得到给出看法的那个人。

normal.en: Adviser and advisor are one word with two endings: -er is the English agent suffix, -or the Latin-looking one.
normal.cn: adviser 与 advisor 是同一个词的两种词尾：-er 是英语施事后缀，-or 是看起来像拉丁语的词尾。

normal.en: An academic adviser handles courses; a financial adviser handles money.
normal.cn: academic adviser 管选课，financial adviser 管钱。

normal.en: Adviser to the president shows that the role is tied to a person in power.
normal.cn: adviser to the president 说明这个角色依附于掌权者。

normal.en: A consultant is usually hired by a firm, while an adviser may be a trusted friend.
normal.cn: consultant 通常由公司聘用，而 adviser 也可能是身边受信任的朋友。

abstract.en: Picture someone standing half a step behind you, looking at the same page and circling the lines that matter.
abstract.cn: 想象一个人站在你侧后方半步，和你看同一页纸，把要紧的几行圈出来。

abstract.en: The adviser does not carry the bag or walk the road; the adviser only makes the map easier to read.
abstract.cn: 顾问不替你背包，也不替你走路；他只是让地图更好读。

abstract.en: The same figure can sit in a palace, a clinic or a dormitory: the setting changes, the half step behind does not.
abstract.cn: 同一个人物可以出现在宫殿、诊所或宿舍：场景变了，那半步的距离不变。

examples.en: The company's legal adviser reviewed the contract.
examples.cn: 公司的法律顾问审阅了这份合同。

examples.en: Academic advisers help students choose their courses.
examples.cn: 学业导师帮助学生选课。

examples.en: She served as an adviser to two mayors.
examples.cn: 她曾担任两任市长的顾问。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「阿德外泽」——阿德站在你侧后方，替你圈出文件上的重点：顾问。

root: 由古法语动词 aviser「思量、提出看法」加英语施事后缀 -er 构成；avis 一般认为出自拉丁语 ad「朝向」+ videre「看」。异体拼写 advisor 借了拉丁语风格的词尾 -or。

sensesIntro.en: The three senses all name the same figure: someone who looks at a situation and points out a way, whether as a paid expert, a study guide, or a trusted voice.
sensesIntro.cn: 三个义项都指同一种人：看清局势后指出一条路的人，只是身份不同——受聘的专家、学业上的导师，或身边受信任的进言者。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a person half a step behind you, looking at the same page and circling what matters.
core.cn: 核心意象：一个人站在你侧后方半步，和你看着同一页纸，把要紧处圈出来。

branches.en: THE PROFESSION: expert looking is sold as a service to firms and governments.
branches.cn: 职业线：专家的「看」被当作服务，卖给公司与政府。

branches.en: THE CAMPUS: the same looking narrows to courses and study plans.
branches.cn: 校园线：同样的「看」缩小到选课与学习计划上。

branches.en: THE INFORMAL VOICE: no post is needed, only the trust of the person being advised.
branches.cn: 非正式线：不需要职位，只需要被建议者的信任。

branches.en: TRUST IS THE COMMON CORE: paid or unpaid, the adviser is the one whose view is asked for.
branches.cn: 信任是共同内核：无论受聘与否，顾问都是那个被征询看法的人。

branches.en: ONE ROLE, THREE SETTINGS: office, campus and kitchen table all hold the same half step behind.
branches.cn: 一个角色，三处场景：办公室、校园与厨房餐桌旁，都站着同一个「半步之后」的人。

intro.en: Adviser is a borrowed French verb plus an English agent suffix; the second spelling simply swaps in a Latin-looking ending.
intro.cn: adviser 是借来的法语动词加英语施事后缀；另一种拼写只是换了一个看起来像拉丁语的词尾。

latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 videre 与 visum 均有记录，ad 也是有记录的介词；法语动词 aviser 同样有记录，更早的印欧词根则属重构形式。

definition_zh: 事情；事务；事件；私情；（口语）东西
definition_en: a matter that has to be dealt with, an event, a secret romantic relationship, or, informally, an object
core_image: 桌上一叠待办的文件，每一份都写着「这件事要处理」
scene: 客厅里两个人压低声音，茶几上的信件被推到一边。The whole affair was settled before the guests arrived.
sceneCN: 这里 affair 指正在发生的这件事（第 1 个义项：需要处理的事情）；句意为客人们到来之前，整件事就已经处理妥当了。

pos.zh: 名词：事情；事务；事件；私情；东西

derivatives.zh: 由 love 与 affair 复合而成，义为「恋情；风流韵事」
由 current 与 affairs 复合而成，义为「时事；时政」
法语借形，与本词同源，指「事情、事件」，多见于仿法语书面表达

senses.title: A matter to be dealt with
senses.definition: an event or situation that has to be dealt with, often one that is complicated or unpleasant
senses.definitionCN: 需要处理的事情或局面，常指复杂或令人不快者
senses.example: The whole affair was settled before the guests arrived.
senses.exampleCN: 客人们到来之前，整件事就已经处理妥当了。
senses.why: Old French afaire is literally 'to do', so an affair is whatever there is to be done, pictured as a task lying on the table.
senses.whyCN: 古法语 afaire 字面就是「去做」，所以 affair 就是眼前有待去做的任何事情，像桌上摆着的一份任务。

senses.title: Matters of business or public life
senses.definition: in the plural, the matters that belong to a person's business, a country's government or public life
senses.definitionCN: 用复数时，指属于个人业务、国家政务或公共生活的事务
senses.example: He handles foreign affairs for the ministry.
senses.exampleCN: 他在该部负责外交事务。
senses.why: The same things to be done multiply: once they belong to an office or a state, the plural affairs becomes the standard word for its business.
senses.whyCN: 「要做的事」一旦成批出现，就带上了归属：属于某个机构或国家的那些事，复数 affairs 便成了固定说法。

senses.title: An event, often a scandal
senses.definition: an event or series of events that attracts public attention, especially one involving scandal or disgrace
senses.definitionCN: 引起公众关注的事件或一连串事件，尤指涉及丑闻或不光彩行为者
senses.example: The minister resigned after the affair became public.
senses.exampleCN: 这件事曝光后，部长辞职了。
senses.why: A matter that everyone talks about stops being private business and becomes a public event, and the word carries that weight without naming it.
senses.whyCN: 一件人人都在议论的事，就不再是私事，而成了公共事件；这个词不必点明，就自带那层不光彩的分量。

senses.title: A secret romantic relationship
senses.definition: a romantic or sexual relationship between two people, especially a secret one and often one that is disapproved of
senses.definitionCN: 两人之间的恋情或性关系，尤指秘密的、往往不被认可的那种
senses.example: Their affair lasted two years and ended badly.
senses.exampleCN: 他们的私情持续了两年，最后收场很难看。
senses.why: This is the matter kept off the table: something going on between two people that is deliberately not made public.
senses.whyCN: 这是被从桌面上收起来的那件「事」：两个人之间正在发生、却刻意不让外人知道的关系。

senses.title: An object, in informal use
senses.definition: an object or device, used informally and often with an adjective of approval or disapproval
senses.definitionCN: 口语中指物品或装置，常与表示褒贬的形容词连用
senses.example: He rode up on a smart little affair with a red tank.
senses.exampleCN: 他骑着一辆红色油箱的小玩意儿过来了。
senses.why: The vague 'matter' can shrink to a thing you cannot or will not name precisely, which is exactly the tone of this informal sense.
senses.whyCN: 含糊的「事情」可以缩小成一件你说不清或不愿细说的东西，这正是这个口语义的语气。

intro.en: Affair is a French noun made from a Latin phrase meaning 'to do', and its modern senses all descend from the idea of something that has to be done.
intro.cn: affair 是由一个意为「去做」的拉丁短语构成的法语名词，它今天的各个义项都源自「有待去做的事」这个观念。

items.en: *dhe- is generally reconstructed as 'to put, to do', and the Latin verb facere is usually traced to it; the deeper history remains source uncertain.
items.cn: 一般认为原始印欧语 *dhe- 意为「放置、做」，拉丁语动词 facere 通常被追溯到它；更早的历史来源不确定。

items.en: The recorded verb facere meant 'to do, to make' and built a very large family, including factum 'a deed' and efficere 'to bring about'.
items.cn: 有文献记录的动词 facere 意为「做、制造」，衍生出庞大的词族，包括 factum「行为、事迹」与 efficere「促成」。

items.en: The phrase à faire 'to do' became the noun afaire, meaning 'business, matter, thing to be done'. Latin had no such noun, so the formation belongs to French.
items.cn: 短语 à faire「去做」变成了名词 afaire，意为「事务、事情、有待去做的事」。拉丁语没有这个名词，因此这一构词属于法语阶段。

items.en: English borrowed the word in the thirteenth century as afaire or affaire; spellings varied for a long time, and the exact first date is uncertain.
items.cn: 英语在十三世纪借入这个词，写作 afaire 或 affaire；拼写在很长时期内并不统一，确切的首次出现年代不确定。

items.en: The plural affairs became the standard term for business and public matters, while the singular kept the senses of event, secret romance and, informally, object.
items.cn: 复数 affairs 成为表示业务与公共事务的固定说法；单数则保留「事件」「秘密恋情」，以及口语中的「东西」等义。

note.en: The look-alike group holds the plural, a French-style doublet and two words that only begin with the same letters; the near-meaning group holds words for a matter, an event, business and a secret relationship.
note.cn: 形近组收复数形式、一个法语借形，以及两个只是开头字母相同的词；近义组收表示事情、事件、业务与秘密关系的词。

entries.definition: The plural of affair, used as a fixed term for business, public matters or personal concerns.
entries.definitionCN: 本词的复数形式，固定表示业务、公共事务或个人事务，与单数「一件事」的分工不同。

entries.definition: A French-style spelling of affair used in English in phrases such as affaire d'honneur.
entries.definitionCN: 法语借形，与本词同源，见于 affaire d'honneur 这类仿法语说法，多用于书面语。

entries.definition: Friendly and easy to talk to; it merely looks similar and comes from a different Latin root.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「和蔼可亲的」；只是拼写开头相近，词源不同，来自拉丁语 affabilis（ad 加 fari「说话」）。

entries.definition: A written statement sworn to be true; it only shares the opening letters and comes from another root.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「宣誓书」；只是开头字母相同，词源不同，来自中世纪拉丁语 affidare（ad 加 fidere「信任」）。

entries.definition: A subject or situation that is being dealt with; the closest general word to affair.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「事情、问题」，是与 affair 最接近的一般用词，但不含「私情」与「东西」两义。

entries.definition: Something that happens, especially something important; it has no sense of a task to be done.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「事件、活动」，尤指重要的事，但不带「有待处理」的含义。

entries.definition: Matters that concern a person, a company or an organization; it overlaps with the plural affairs.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「事务、业务」，与复数 affairs 有重叠，但更偏商业与职责。

entries.definition: A single event, often unpleasant or unusual; narrower than affair and without the scandalous suggestion.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「事件、事故」，多指单一而不快或异常的事，范围比 affair 窄，也不必然含丑闻意味。

entries.definition: A secret sexual relationship, or a working connection between groups; formal in tone.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「私通」或「联络」，前者与 affair 的私情义接近，但语气更正式、更隐晦。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the real French phrase behind the word and the fixed expressions it forms in modern English.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些记忆钩子依据这个词背后的真实法语短语，以及它在现代英语里构成的固定表达。

normal.en: afaire is à faire, 'to do': an affair is something on the to-do list.
normal.cn: afaire 就是 à faire「去做」：affair 是待办清单上的一件事。

normal.en: In the plural, affairs means the business of an office or a state.
normal.cn: 用复数时，affairs 指一个机构或一个国家的事务。

normal.en: A love affair is the matter kept off the table.
normal.cn: love affair 就是被收起来、不摆到桌面上的那件事。

normal.en: A scandal is an affair that reached the front page.
normal.cn: 丑闻就是一路闹到报纸头版的 affair。

normal.en: A smart little affair is informal for an object you do not bother to name.
normal.cn: a smart little affair 是口语说法，指一件你懒得细说的东西。

abstract.en: Picture a pile of papers on a desk, each one stamped with the words to be done.
abstract.cn: 想象桌上一叠纸，每一张都盖着「待办」的戳。

abstract.en: One sheet can be lifted out and hidden in a drawer: that is the secret affair.
abstract.cn: 其中一张可以被抽出来锁进抽屉：那就是秘密的私情。

abstract.en: The same pile can belong to one person, to a ministry, or to a whole nation, and the word does not change.
abstract.cn: 同一叠纸可以属于一个人、一个部，或整个国家，而这个词本身并不改变。

examples.en: The dinner was a quiet affair with only close friends.
examples.cn: 那顿晚饭只请了亲近的朋友，办得很安静。

examples.en: She handles public affairs for the city council.
examples.cn: 她为市议会处理公共事务。

examples.en: Their secret affair was discovered by a colleague.
examples.cn: 他们的私情被一位同事发现了。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「阿费尔」——阿费尔把一叠待办纸拍在桌上：这些事都得处理。

root: 古法语 afaire「事情、事务」字面是 à faire「去做」，其成分可追溯到拉丁语 ad「朝向」+ facere「做」；英语复数 affairs 固定表示事务、业务。

sensesIntro.en: The five senses all start from something to be done: one task, a mass of business, an event people talk about, a relationship kept off the table, and the vague object nobody bothers to name.
sensesIntro.cn: 五个义项都从「有待去做的事」出发：一件待办的事、成批的事务、被人议论的事件、藏在桌面下的私情，以及口语里那件懒得命名的东西。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a pile of papers on a desk, each one marked as something to be done.
core.cn: 核心意象：桌上一叠纸，每一张都标着「待办」。

branches.en: THE TASK: one thing on the table, waiting to be handled.
branches.cn: 任务线：桌面上的一件事，等着被处理。

branches.en: THE OFFICE: the tasks multiply and belong to a business or a state.
branches.cn: 机构线：事情成批出现，归属于一个机构或一个国家。

branches.en: THE HEADLINE: what everyone discusses turns into a public event.
branches.cn: 头条线：人人议论的事，变成了公共事件。

branches.en: THE DRAWER: one sheet is hidden away, and that is the secret relationship.
branches.cn: 抽屉线：其中一张纸被藏起来，这就是那段秘密关系。

branches.en: THE VAGUE THING: the matter shrinks to an object the speaker will not name.
branches.cn: 含糊线：事情缩小成说话人不愿点明的一件东西。

intro.en: Affair is built from Latin and Old French elements meaning 'to do'; English later added only a plural ending and a few compounds.
intro.cn: affair 由意为「做」的拉丁语与古法语成分构成；英语后来只加了复数词尾和少数复合词。

latinIntro.en: Latin facere, factum and the preposition ad are recorded; the Old French phrase à faire and the noun afaire are also recorded, and only the Indo-European root is reconstructed.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 facere、factum 与介词 ad 均有记录，古法语短语 à faire 与名词 afaire 也有记录，只有印欧词根属于重构形式。

items.example: It marks the direction of the action in the Latin phrase.
items.exampleCN: 它标出拉丁短语中动作的方向。

items.example: It is the doing verb at the centre of the word.
items.exampleCN: 它是这个词中心那个表示「做」的动词。

items.example: English fact comes from it.
items.exampleCN: 英语的 fact 来自它。

items.example: It opens the phrase à faire.
items.exampleCN: 它引出短语 à faire。

items.example: It continues the Latin verb facere.
items.exampleCN: 它延续了拉丁语动词 facere。

items.example: It is the direct source of the English word.
items.exampleCN: 它是英语这个词的直接来源。

items.meaning: a thing known to be true
items.example: It shares the Latin verb facere with affair.
items.exampleCN: 它与 affair 共享拉丁语动词 facere。

items.example: It forms affairs, the fixed term for business.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 affairs，即表示事务的固定说法。

derivatives.zh: 由 love 与 affair 复合而成，义为「恋情；风流韵事」
由 current 与 affairs 复合而成，义为「时事；时政」
法语借形，与本词同源，指「事情、事件」

definition_zh: 影响；使感动；侵袭；感染；假装；喜好使用；（心理学）情感
definition_en: to produce a change in something, to move someone emotionally, to attack the body, to pretend to have a feeling, or, as a noun, an emotional state
core_image: 一颗石子落进静水，波纹一圈圈推到岸边
scene: 暴雪过后，果园的枝条一夜之间全黑了。The early frost affected every tree in the valley.
sceneCN: 这里 affect 指低温对果树造成侵害（第 3 个义项：疾病、霜冻等侵袭身体或作物）；句意为早霜影响了谷地里的每一棵树。

pos.zh: 动词：影响；使感动；侵袭；感染；假装；喜好使用
名词（心理学）：情感；情感状态，重音在首音节

derivatives.zh: 由拉丁语 affectus 经法语进入英语，加名词后缀 -ion 构成，义为「喜爱；感情」
由 affection 加形容词后缀 -ate 构成，义为「深情的；表示爱意的」
由本词加形容词后缀 -ive 构成，义为「情感的；感情方面的」
由过去分词转成形容词，义为「受影响的」或「做作的」
由否定前缀 dis- 加 affected 构成，义为「不满的；不再忠心的」

senses.title: To produce a change in something
senses.definition: to make a difference to something or someone; to change a situation, a feeling or a result
senses.definitionCN: 对某事或某人产生作用，改变其状况、感受或结果
senses.example: Rising sea levels will affect coastal cities first.
senses.exampleCN: 海平面上升将首先影响沿海城市。
senses.why: Latin afficere meant to do something to a thing: ad- 'towards' plus facere 'do' gives the picture of an action reaching its object and leaving a mark.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 afficere 意为「对某物做点什么」：ad-「朝向」加 facere「做」，画面是一个动作落到对象身上并留下痕迹。

senses.title: To move someone emotionally
senses.definition: to cause a strong feeling in someone, especially sadness or sympathy
senses.definitionCN: 引起某人强烈的情感，尤指悲伤或同情
senses.example: The photographs of the flooded village affected her deeply.
senses.exampleCN: 那些被淹村庄的照片深深触动了她。
senses.why: The action reaching a person lands on the feelings rather than on circumstances, so the same verb names an emotional mark left behind.
senses.whyCN: 动作落到人身上时，落点是感情而不是处境，于是同一个动词就表示留在心里的那一道痕迹。

senses.title: To attack the body or a crop
senses.definition: of a disease, pest or harmful condition, to attack and damage a person, an animal or a crop
senses.definitionCN: 指疾病、害虫或有害状况侵袭并损害人、动物或作物
senses.example: The early frost affected every tree in the valley.
senses.exampleCN: 早霜影响了谷地里的每一棵树。
senses.why: Here the action is violent and physical: something outside reaches the body and works on it, which is the oldest medical use of the Latin verb.
senses.whyCN: 这里的动作猛烈而具体：外来的东西侵到身体上并起作用，这正是这个拉丁动词最早的医学用法。

senses.title: To pretend to have a feeling or manner
senses.definition: to behave as if you have a feeling, quality or way of speaking that you do not really have
senses.definitionCN: 故意表现出并不真实具备的情感、气质或说话方式
senses.example: He affected a British accent to amuse the children.
senses.exampleCN: 他故意带上一口英国腔逗孩子们开心。
senses.why: The word turns back on the person: instead of reaching an object, the person puts on a surface and keeps it up, which is why this sense is close to feign.
senses.whyCN: 这时动作折回到人自己身上：不是作用于对象，而是给自己套上一层表面并刻意维持，所以这个义项接近「假装」。

senses.title: To use or wear something by preference
senses.definition: to choose to use, wear or adopt something regularly, often to create a certain impression
senses.definitionCN: 出于偏好而经常使用、穿戴或采用某物，常为营造某种印象
senses.example: She affects a plain black coat and never wears colour.
senses.exampleCN: 她总爱穿一件素黑外套，从不穿彩色衣服。
senses.why: Pretending settles into habit: what began as putting on a manner becomes the style a person keeps choosing.
senses.whyCN: 「装出来」久了就变成习惯：最初套上的一层姿态，后来成了这个人一再选择的风格。

senses.title: Emotion as a psychological term
senses.titleCN: 情感；情感状态（心理学名词）
senses.definition: in psychology, the observable outward feeling or emotional state, pronounced with the stress on the first syllable
senses.definitionCN: 心理学中指可观察到的外显情感或情感状态，重音落在第一个音节
senses.example: The patient showed a flat affect throughout the interview.
senses.exampleCN: 整个面谈过程中，病人表现出情感平淡。
senses.why: The noun keeps the Latin affectus 'a state produced in the mind'; psychology took that old participle and made it a technical label.
senses.whyCN: 名词保留了拉丁语 affectus「在心里造成的状态」；心理学把这个旧分词借来，当作专门的术语。

intro.en: Affect comes from a Latin verb built on 'to do', and the same Latin stock also produced effect with a different prefix.
intro.cn: affect 来自一个以「做」为核心构成的拉丁语动词；同一拉丁语词源加上不同前缀，又产生了 effect。

items.en: *dhe- is generally reconstructed as 'to put, to do', and Latin facere is usually traced to it; the deeper origin is source uncertain.
items.cn: 一般认为原始印欧语 *dhe- 意为「放置、做」，拉丁语 facere 通常被追溯到它；更早的来源不确定。

items.en: The recorded verb facere 'to do, make' built a large family, among them factum 'a deed' and efficere 'to bring about'.
items.cn: 有文献记录的动词 facere「做、制造」衍生出庞大的词族，其中有 factum「行为、事迹」与 efficere「促成」。

items.en: Ad- 'towards' plus facere formed afficere, 'to do something to a person or thing, to influence or move'; its participle affectus meant 'a state produced in mind or body'.
items.cn: ad-「朝向」加 facere 构成 afficere，意为「对人或物做点什么、施加影响」；其分词 affectus 指「在心里或身上造成的状态」。

items.en: The noun affectus and the French verb affecter carried both the 'influence' sense and the 'put on a show' sense into English.
items.cn: 名词 affectus 与法语动词 affecter 把「影响」和「做出样子」两种含义一并带进了英语。

items.en: Affect and effect both descend from facere but from different prefixes: affect from ad- 'to', effect from ex- 'out'. The psychological noun keeps the first-syllable stress.
items.cn: affect 与 effect 都出自 facere，但前缀不同：affect 来自 ad-「朝向」，effect 来自 ex-「出」。心理学的名词义保留首音节重音。

note.en: The look-alike group is built on the facere family, with effect first because it is the word most often confused with affect; the near-meaning group holds verbs of changing, touching, infecting and pretending.
note.cn: 形近组围绕 facere 词族展开，effect 排在最前，因为它是最容易与 affect 混淆的词；近义组收表示改变、触动、感染与假装的动词。

entries.definition: A noun meaning a result or an influence, and a formal verb meaning to bring something about; it comes from ex- plus facere, 'to do out, bring about'.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「结果、效果」，作动词时义为「实现、促成」；与 affect 同出拉丁语 facere，但 effect 来自 ex-「出」，指做出来的结果，affect 来自 ad-「向」，指作用到对象上，两者不可互换。

entries.definition: An adjective meaning influenced, or artificial and insincere in manner.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「受影响的」，或指举止「做作的、不自然的」。

entries.definition: A feeling of fondness or love, from the same Latin participle.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「喜爱、感情」，由同一拉丁语分词 affectus 经法语进入英语。

entries.definition: An adjective meaning relating to emotion or feeling.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「情感的、感情方面的」，多用于心理学与教育语境。

entries.definition: To change how someone acts or thinks, usually gradually; broader and less physical than affect.
entries.definitionCN: 动词或名词，义为「影响」，多指逐渐改变他人的行为或想法，范围比 affect 宽，身体色彩更弱。

entries.definition: To have a strong effect on something; stronger and more forceful than affect.
entries.definitionCN: 动词或名词，义为「冲击、产生影响」，力度比 affect 强，常暗示明显的震动。

entries.definition: To cause strong feelings in someone, especially sympathy or sadness.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「打动、使感动」，与 affect 的第 2 个义项接近，但更口语、更强调情感反应。

entries.definition: To pass a disease into a body, or to make someone share a feeling; narrower than affect.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「传染、感染」，既可指疾病进入身体，也可指情绪传染，比 affect 的侵袭义更具体。

entries.definition: To pretend to have a feeling or condition; a formal near-match for the 'pretend' sense of affect.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「假装、佯装」，与 affect 的假装义接近，但语气正式，且不含「惯常穿戴」的引申。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the real Latin prefix and verb, the affect-effect pair, and the sentence frames the word takes.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些记忆钩子依据真实的拉丁语前缀与动词、affect 与 effect 的配对，以及这个词实际使用的句型。

normal.en: ad plus facere means to do something to: affect is the action landing on an object.
normal.cn: ad 加 facere 意为「对……做点什么」：affect 就是落到对象身上的那个动作。

normal.en: Effect begins with e for exit: it is the result that comes out; affect begins with a for an action aimed at something.
normal.cn: effect 以 e 开头，联想「出来」的结果；affect 以 a 开头，联想「作用于」某物的动作。

normal.en: If the sentence needs a noun for a result, the word is almost always effect.
normal.cn: 句子需要一个表示「结果」的名词时，几乎总是用 effect。

normal.en: The noun affect is a psychology term and carries the stress on the first syllable.
normal.cn: 作名词的 affect 是心理学术语，重音落在第一个音节。

normal.en: Doctors say a disease affects the lungs; patients feel the effects afterwards.
normal.cn: 医生说疾病 affects 肺部；病人随后感受到的是 effects。

abstract.en: Picture a stone dropped into still water, rings spreading outward until they touch the bank.
abstract.cn: 想象一颗石子落进静水，涟漪一圈圈荡开，直到触到岸边。

abstract.en: The rings are the change; the stone is the cause, and the bank is whatever gets touched.
abstract.cn: 涟漪是变化，石子是原因，而岸边就是被触及的那一方。

abstract.en: The same word can touch a mood, a lung or a voice: the surface differs, the reaching does not.
abstract.cn: 同一个词可以触及情绪、肺，或一口腔调：表面不同，伸手去够的动作却一样。

examples.en: Rising sea levels will affect coastal cities first.
examples.cn: 海平面上升将首先影响沿海城市。

examples.en: The photographs affected her more than she expected.
examples.cn: 那些照片对她的触动比她预想的更大。

examples.en: This decision affects everyone in the department.
examples.cn: 这个决定影响到部门里的每一个人。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「阿费克特」——阿费克特伸手一推，水面荡开一圈圈波纹：影响。

root: 拉丁语 afficere「对……做点什么、作用于」，由 ad-「朝向」+ facere「做」构成；其过去分词 affectus 义为「在心里或身上造成的状态」，心理学的名词义即由此而来。同源的 effect 来自 ex- 加 facere，指「做出来的结果」。

sensesIntro.en: The six senses all start from 'doing something to': acting on a situation, on the feelings, on the body, on one's own surface, on a habit, and finally the inner state that results.
sensesIntro.cn: 六个义项都从「对……做点什么」出发：作用于局势、作用于情绪、作用于身体、给自己套上一层表面、把表面变成习惯，最后落到由此形成的内在情感状态。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a stone dropped into still water, rings spreading until they reach the bank.
core.cn: 核心意象：一颗石子落进静水，涟漪一圈圈荡到岸边。

branches.en: THE SITUATION: the action lands on circumstances and changes them.
branches.cn: 局势线：动作落到处境上，把处境改变。

branches.en: THE FEELINGS: the same action lands on a person's emotions and leaves a mark there.
branches.cn: 情感线：同一个动作落到人的情绪上，在那里留下痕迹。

branches.en: THE BODY: disease, frost or pests reach the body or the crop and damage it.
branches.cn: 身体线：疾病、霜冻或害虫侵到身体或作物上，造成损害。

branches.en: THE SURFACE: the action turns back on the speaker, first as a pose, then as a habit of dress or manner.
branches.cn: 表面线：动作折回说话人自身，先是姿态，后来变成穿戴或举止上的习惯。

branches.en: THE INNER STATE: the old participle becomes the psychological name for what is felt inside.
branches.cn: 内在线：旧分词成了心理学里指称内在感受的术语。

intro.en: Affect is a Latin verb of doing plus a prefix of direction; English suffixes then built the emotional and psychological family.
intro.cn: affect 是表示「做」的拉丁语动词加方向前缀构成的；英语后缀随后撑起了情感与心理学的一族词。

latinIntro.en: Latin facere, afficere, affectus and efficere are all recorded, so no Latin form here is invented; only the Indo-European root is reconstructed.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 facere、afficere、affectus 与 efficere 均有文献记录，这里没有任何拉丁形式是编造的；只有印欧词根属于重构形式。

derivatives.zh: 由拉丁语 affectus 经法语进入英语，义为「喜爱；感情」
由 affection 加形容词后缀 -ate 构成，义为「深情的」
由本词加形容词后缀 -ive 构成，义为「情感的」
由过去分词转成形容词，义为「受影响的」或「做作的」
由否定前缀 dis- 加 affected 构成，义为「不满的；不再忠心的」
